2026-06-24.overview: The period is dominated by Microsoft Learn documentation work rather than a product-release announcement. The most actionable updates are an Internet Access deployment-readiness checkpoint and ID Protection guidance to test policies with a non-administrator account. Entra ID also added new group-management and application-SSO guidance. The supplied evidence contains no Message Center items or removals and does not establish a new feature, preview, general availability, retirement, or changed service behavior; the Windows passkey update, for example, has no substantive change description in the record.
2026-06-24.adminImpact: For an active Secure Access Services Edge deployment, use the Internet Access guide’s stated prerequisites—defined users and waves, a deployment schedule, and licensing requirements—as the point before enablement. For ID Protection policy rollouts, validate with a non-administrator test user before real users. Use the new SSO and group pages as planning references, and apply the stated group-owner boundaries when delegating administration. Do not infer a passkey rollout or tenant configuration change from the passkey article update alone.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Internet Access guidance now marks the post-planning handoff
keyChanges.detail: The updated GSA deployment guide says the initiate and plan stages are complete once the organization has defined which users to enable in each wave, set a deployment schedule, and met licensing requirements; it then says the project is ready to enable Microsoft Entra Internet Access. This is deployment guidance, not evidence of a new feature, preview, or GA event.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection rollout guidance calls for a non-administrator test user
keyChanges.detail: The updated ID Protection introduction instructs administrators to use a test user who isn’t an administrator to verify policies before deploying them to real users. That is security and rollout guidance; the record does not indicate a change to policy behavior or availability.

keyChanges.title: New SSO guidance adds a SAML 2.0 versus OIDC decision reference
keyChanges.detail: A new Entra ID article compares SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect for selecting an application’s SSO approach. It is part of a same-day set of new SSO material that also includes an ISV planning guide and an explanation of Microsoft’s centralized SSO model. These are architecture and planning references; no protocol-support change or release status is stated.

keyChanges.title: A new group-management reference covers core group administration
keyChanges.detail: The new “How to manage groups” article covers creating and updating Microsoft Entra groups, including membership and settings. It is new documentation for administrators, not evidence that group capabilities or defaults changed.

keyChanges.title: Updated permissions guidance defines the boundary for group owners
keyChanges.detail: The updated “Users Default Permissions” page states that a group owner can add or remove other owners, can manage only groups they own, and can add or remove members only when the group’s membership type is Assigned; it contrasts this with users assigned at least the Groups Administrator role. This is a documentation clarification of the stated scope, not evidence that the permission model changed.

2026-06-23.headline: Upcoming Conditional Access enforcement change leads a documentation-heavy 23 June
2026-06-23.overview: The main tenant-impact signal is an upcoming Microsoft Entra Conditional Access change affecting policies with resource exclusions. Microsoft also published new guidance for passwordless sign-in to Entra Connect Sync. Most other activity consists of documentation maintenance or operational clarification; no retirements or explicit general-availability or preview announcements are evidenced.
2026-06-23.adminImpact: Prioritize the Message Center notice and identify Conditional Access policies that use resource exclusions. The supplied evidence does not provide the rollout timing or exact enforcement semantics. The new Connect Sync article may help assess operator sign-in procedures using FIDO2 keys or passkeys, but it does not by itself establish a new capability or tenant-configuration requirement. The remaining changes do not show a supported need for configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access: upcoming enforcement change for resource exclusions
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Message Center reports an upcoming change intended to improve enforcement for Conditional Access policies with resource exclusions. It is a tenant-facing notice, but the supplied text does not state the timing, precise policy-evaluation change, or whether any reconfiguration is required. Review the full notice and affected policies rather than treating this as a completed GA or preview launch.

keyChanges.title: New Entra Connect Sync guidance covers FIDO2 and passkey sign-in
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft added Learn documentation for signing in to Microsoft Entra Connect Sync with passwordless methods, including FIDO2 security keys and passkeys. This is a new documentation article, not evidence that a new Connect Sync feature has launched or that tenant settings changed; it provides a sign-in procedure for administrators to assess against current operating practices.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection guidance links source IP restoration with more accurate risk detection
keyChanges.detail: The updated Source IP Restoration documentation states that the capability improves the accuracy of Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk detections. The supplied evidence describes a documentation update and does not identify a new detection, availability change, or configuration requirement.

keyChanges.title: Connect Sync staging-server guidance adds export analysis help
keyChanges.detail: The Connect Sync Staging Server page now documents using the csanalyzer.ps1 PowerShell script to map export.csv changes from connector-space distinguished names to common identifiers such as displayName and userPrincipalName. This is an operational documentation improvement that can make pending-export review easier, not a stated change to synchronization behavior.

2026-06-20.headline: Microsoft Authenticator’s rooted-device block is the key behavior change; most other updates clarify documentation
2026-06-20.overview: The period is documentation-heavy rather than a feature-launch or retirement day. The clearest operational notice says Microsoft Authenticator will move from warning to blocking Entra credentials on jailbroken or rooted iOS and Android devices, automatically for all users on those devices. Other notable updates clarify External ID billing, Internet Access lab sequencing, ID Protection risk-detection guidance, and Global Secure Access signaling. Three new Entra ID pages document Purview workload roles, but the supplied evidence does not establish a change to role availability or permissions.
2026-06-20.adminImpact: Notify users and update support documentation for the Authenticator device-integrity behavior; the notice specifies that no admin configuration is required. For Internet Access exercises, create the baseline security profile and Conditional Access policy as instructed and reuse them in later labs. Use the updated External ID MAU guidance for billing estimates. The ID Protection and Global Secure Access entries are documentation references in the supplied evidence, not confirmed new rollouts or required configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Authenticator will block Entra credentials on rooted or jailbroken devices
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice describes a warning phase followed by blocking on jailbroken or rooted iOS and Android devices. It says the behavior is automatic, applies to all users on those devices, and requires no admin action; administrators should notify users and update documentation.

keyChanges.title: External ID billing guidance defines monthly active users
keyChanges.detail: The updated FAQ defines MAU as unique users with authentication activity during a calendar month. It also distinguishes the core offer from premium add-ons and states that the core offering is free for the first 50,000 MAU. This is a pricing-documentation clarification, not evidence of a changed price or tenant feature.

keyChanges.title: Internet Access tutorials clarify reuse of the baseline security configuration
keyChanges.detail: The updated tutorial says the exercises should be followed in order. The baseline web-filtering lab creates a security profile and assigns it to a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy; later labs should use that existing profile and policy rather than creating duplicates.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection documentation links source IP restoration to detection accuracy
keyChanges.detail: The updated Source IP Restoration page states that the capability improves the accuracy of risk detection in Microsoft Entra ID Protection. The supplied summary does not identify a new setting, rollout status, or required administrator change, so this is best treated as guidance rather than a confirmed service launch.

keyChanges.title: Universal Tenant Restrictions now points to Global Secure Access signaling guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated page links administrators to instructions for enabling Global Secure Access signaling for Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Graph. The record supports a documentation cross-reference, not a claim that signaling is newly available or automatically enabled.

2026-06-19.headline: Agent ID documentation flags a coming Agent 365 requirement for agent protection; External ID adds Android fraud-SDK header guidance
2026-06-19.overview: 19 June's meaningful changes are mostly documentation updates rather than announced service launches. The clearest licensing change is the Agent ID guidance that ID Protection for agents will require a Microsoft Agent 365 license starting soon. A new External ID article covers custom x-* headers for native authentication requests in Android (Kotlin), while updated Entra ID material describes a bulk-operations experience explicitly marked Preview and clarifies that Connect staged-rollout group edits can take up to 24 hours to apply. The supplied evidence indicates no retirement or general-availability announcement.
2026-06-19.adminImpact: Teams using Microsoft Entra Agent ID should validate the licensing path for ID Protection for agents and track the effective timing; no specific deadline is supplied. The External ID item is app-integration guidance, so Android/Kotlin application owners are the primary audience rather than tenant administrators. Treat the bulk-operations experience as Preview, and allow up to 24 hours after Connect staged-rollout group membership edits. Use the updated Conditional Access entitlement statement when checking plans; it is licensing documentation, not evidence of a Conditional Access behavior change.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection for agents gains a stated licensing requirement
keyChanges.detail: Updated Agent ID licensing guidance says ID Protection for agents will require a Microsoft Agent 365 license starting soon to extend protection through Microsoft Entra Agent ID. This is a forthcoming licensing requirement in the documentation, not a reported general-availability launch or retirement, and no effective date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: External ID adds Android/Kotlin custom-header integration guidance
keyChanges.detail: A new Microsoft Learn article explains how an Android (Kotlin) app can attach custom x-* headers to native authentication network requests so fraud-detection SDKs can integrate with Microsoft Entra External ID. The evidence establishes new implementation guidance, not a tenant-side setting or a service-availability change.

keyChanges.title: Bulk operations experience is documented as Preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Entra bulk-operations article describes a new experience for managing users, groups, and devices and labels it Preview. Same-day updates cover CSV-based bulk add and remove operations and bulk group-membership download, but the supplied evidence does not establish general availability or a rollout date.

keyChanges.title: Connect staged-rollout group edits may take up to 24 hours
keyChanges.detail: Updated Connect staged rollout guidance says adding or removing users in a staged-rollout group can take up to 24 hours to take effect. This is an operational timing clarification in the documentation, not evidence of a new rollout feature or an immediate propagation guarantee.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access licensing coverage is spelled out for Entra Suite and Microsoft 365 E7
keyChanges.detail: The updated Conditional Access licensing page states that Microsoft Entra Suite includes all Microsoft Entra Conditional Access features, and that Microsoft 365 E7 includes those features through Entra Suite. This is an entitlement-documentation clarification; the evidence does not indicate a Conditional Access behavior change.

2026-06-18.headline: Agent ID service plans are slated for July 2026; the day otherwise clarifies security and governance guidance
2026-06-18.overview: The most consequential item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for new Conditional Access for Agents and ID Protection for Agents service plans in Microsoft Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 E7. Rollout starts in July 2026, with automatic enabling and no policy changes required; a license review is recommended. Related Microsoft Learn updates call out an upcoming Microsoft Agent 365 licensing requirement for agent protection, explain Conditional Access evaluation during Agent ID token exchange, and clarify an Entitlement Management guest-lifecycle rule. The External ID update is guidance-focused, while the one new Private Access item is a release-notes tracker rather than evidence of a new sensor release.
2026-06-18.adminImpact: Review licensing for agent protection ahead of the July rollout, but do not change Conditional Access policies solely because of the Message Center notice. When designing Agent ID policies, account for Conditional Access evaluation of on-behalf-of token exchanges. In Entitlement Management, review invited guests that remain ungoverned and use Mark Guests as Governed when package-based governance is the intended lifecycle. Treat the External ID and Private Access entries as documentation updates unless further release evidence is available.

keyChanges.title: Planned service plans for agent Conditional Access and ID Protection
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announces Conditional Access for Agents and ID Protection for Agents as new Entra service plans for Microsoft Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 E7. Rollout starts in July 2026; the plans will be enabled automatically, and Microsoft says no policy changes are required. This is a rollout announcement, not evidence that the capabilities are generally available today.

keyChanges.title: Updated guidance calls out an upcoming ID Protection license requirement
keyChanges.detail: The Licensing Identity Protection article says ID Protection for agents will require a Microsoft Agent 365 license to extend protection through Microsoft Entra Agent ID, described as starting soon. The supplied evidence gives no exact enforcement date, so this is licensing-planning guidance rather than a dated tenant change.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID on-behalf-of exchanges are evaluated by Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: The Agent ID guidance explains that an agent cannot reuse the user's original token when it was issued for a different audience. It instead uses on-behalf-of token exchange to obtain a resource-scoped token, and that exchange is evaluated by Conditional Access. This is a documented behavior and implementation clarification, not a notice of a new policy setting.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management clarifies the fate of ungoverned guests
keyChanges.detail: Updated lifecycle guidance says guests invited outside access packages are ungoverned and can remain in the tenant indefinitely after losing their last access-package assignment. When package access is their only reason to remain, administrators can convert them using Mark Guests as Governed while the assignment exists. This is a lifecycle clarification with direct governance and cleanup implications.

keyChanges.title: External ID custom-extension guidance maps REST callbacks to user-flow events
keyChanges.detail: The updated page describes custom authentication extensions as event listeners that call a REST API at defined points in sign-up and sign-in flows, including attribute-collection validation and custom claims provider data in tokens. The entry is an updated guidance page; it does not by itself announce a new External ID capability or availability change.

2026-06-17.headline: Global Secure Access documents AI-agent discovery in preview; Entra updates reinforce ROPC migration and identity guidance
2026-06-17.overview: 17 June 2026 was primarily a documentation-maintenance day: 30 items were updated and one new item appeared, with no removals or Message Center entries. The substantive exceptions are a new Global Secure Access preview description, explicit security guidance for deprecated ROPC, and concrete clarifications for Agent ID’s identity model and dynamic-group limits. The supplied evidence does not establish a general-availability launch, retirement, or broad tenant behavior change.
2026-06-17.adminImpact: Evaluate AI agent discovery as a preview capability only; the evidence does not imply a required rollout or GA availability. If desktop applications still use username/password authentication (ROPC), identify them and plan migration to more secure flows. Review the Agent ID and dynamic-group guidance where those capabilities are in scope, but the supplied changes do not support a tenant-wide configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access: AI agent discovery is documented as a preview
keyChanges.detail: A new Microsoft Learn entry describes AI agent discovery in Global Secure Access (preview), providing network-level visibility into managed and shadow AI agents reaching the internet from the environment. It is explicitly preview documentation, not evidence of general availability or a required deployment.

keyChanges.title: Security guidance: ROPC is deprecated for desktop apps
keyChanges.detail: An updated Entra ID article explains how the username-and-password (ROPC) flow works in desktop apps, why it is deprecated, and how to migrate to more secure authentication flows. This is security guidance, not evidence that ROPC was retired on this date or that tenant behavior changed; affected applications should be identified for migration planning.

keyChanges.title: Documentation clarification: Agent ID identity and token model
keyChanges.detail: An updated Agent ID platform overview describes an OAuth 2.0- and OpenID Connect-compliant authentication service that issues tokens for resource and API access, supporting application-only and delegated scenarios. It also defines the agent identity blueprint, agent identity, and agent’s user account as core constructs. This clarifies fundamentals rather than announcing a new availability milestone or tenant setting.

keyChanges.title: Dynamic-group guidance states a 50-member-group cap
keyChanges.detail: The updated member-of dynamic-group guidance states that each dynamic group can have up to 50 member groups. The supplied record does not say whether this is a new service limit or a clarification of an existing rule, so administrators using member-of rules should verify designs against the stated cap without assuming a behavior change.

2026-06-16.headline: Updated Workload ID and Global Secure Access preview guidance lead a documentation-heavy 16 June
2026-06-16.overview: The period contains 2,893 records: 2,892 updates, one new item, and no removals. Every supplied representative item is marked Updated. The clearest substantive entries are targeted guidance updates—not evidence of a launch, general-availability change, retirement, or changed default behavior. Two selected entries are explicitly labeled Preview: workload identity authentication for SAP SuccessFactors provisioning and Conditional Access for Global Secure Access Explicit Forward Proxy. The other entries provide implementation guidance without stating a lifecycle status.
2026-06-16.adminImpact: No tenant-wide action is supported by the supplied evidence. Administrators working with SAP SuccessFactors provisioning or Explicit Forward Proxy should review the preview guidance before planning changes, but should not assume existing authentication, provisioning, or Conditional Access behavior changed automatically. Agent, Security Copilot, and account-recovery teams can use the other updated pages as implementation references; the records do not establish mandatory rollout actions or general availability.

keyChanges.title: Workload ID: federated-token authentication guidance for SAP SuccessFactors provisioning
keyChanges.detail: The updated Workload ID article documents replacing basic authentication with short-lived, federated OpenID Connect tokens for Microsoft Entra provisioning to SAP SuccessFactors. The title labels this capability Preview, so provisioning teams should treat it as an evaluation and configuration path rather than evidence of general availability or an automatic change to existing connectors.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access: Conditional Access configuration for Explicit Forward Proxy
keyChanges.detail: The updated page explains how to configure a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy for Explicit Forward Proxy. Its title explicitly marks the capability as preview. The entry supports configuration review for administrators evaluating the proxy, but does not indicate that existing policies or enforcement changed.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID: authentication patterns for third-party AI agents
keyChanges.detail: The updated Agent ID guidance explains how to integrate third-party AI agents with Microsoft Entra Agent ID using sidecar and federation patterns for secure authentication. No Preview or general-availability status is stated, so this is implementation guidance rather than a launch announcement. Teams onboarding such agents can use it to assess the documented integration patterns.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot: chat guidance for the Conditional Access Optimization Agent
keyChanges.detail: The updated Security Copilot page covers the chat feature for the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access Optimization Agent. The supplied record identifies the feature but gives no availability or rollout status, so it does not establish a change to Conditional Access recommendations or policies.

keyChanges.title: Verified ID: custom claim validation during account recovery
keyChanges.detail: The updated Verified ID article describes a custom authentication extension that validates Verified ID claims during Microsoft Entra account recovery through an Azure Function and REST API. This is an integration pattern, not evidence of a default account-recovery behavior change; recovery architects using Verified ID can review the extension design.

2026-06-13.headline: New Entra ID PowerShell samples document dynamic-membership incident response
2026-06-13.overview: 13 June was a documentation-heavy day. The main substantive addition is a coordinated set of six new Microsoft Entra ID PowerShell samples for pausing and resuming dynamic membership processing for groups and administrative units. The evidence describes operational scripts for incident response—not a new Entra capability, preview, general-availability announcement, retirement, or confirmed change in service behavior. Other updates cover External ID B2B invitations, Agent ID administrator and developer pages, Entra RBAC and Global Administrator material, and Global Secure Access external-user access, but their summaries do not specify a behavior or availability change.
2026-06-13.adminImpact: Administrators who manage dynamic groups or administrative units and maintain incident-response procedures should review the new samples as possible runbook material. They cover broad and selective pause/resume operations, including staged recovery, but the evidence does not say to execute them now or indicate that a tenant-wide issue is in progress. No concrete action is supported for the other documentation updates from the supplied detail.

keyChanges.title: New incident-response PowerShell samples for dynamic membership
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID published a set of samples for pausing and resuming dynamic membership rule processing on groups and administrative units. The set includes controls for all objects, selected objects or exceptions, and recovery paths for noncritical and critical objects. This is new operational documentation and code-sample coverage, not evidence of a product feature launch or changed platform behavior.

2026-06-12.headline: 12 June 2026: New PIM preview guidance, with sharper Entra coverage for agent controls and reauthentication
2026-06-12.overview: The period was dominated by targeted Microsoft Learn updates rather than announced service launches. The only new item documents a Preview approach for adding custom business logic to Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management role activation. Other notable updates clarify Conditional Access for agent identities, organization-specific recommendations from the Conditional Access Optimization Agent, post-revocation behavior in Identity Protection, and stronger-sign-in registration campaigns. The supplied evidence contains no general-availability announcement, retirement, or Message Center notice.
2026-06-12.adminImpact: Treat the PIM item as preview guidance, not evidence of general availability. Administrators evaluating AI-agent deployments should review the updated Conditional Access material, while Identity Protection administrators should verify that their expected post-revocation reauthentication experience matches the documented policy behavior. The registration-campaign update is useful for reviewing passkey or Microsoft Authenticator enrollment plans; the documentation updates alone do not establish a tenant-wide service change.

keyChanges.title: PIM custom extensions are documented as a Preview workflow
keyChanges.detail: A new ID Governance article explains how to configure custom extensions in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management so custom business logic can be integrated into role-activation workflows. It is explicitly marked Preview; the record does not establish general availability or a service launch.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access guidance now covers targeting agent identities
keyChanges.detail: Updated Agent ID guidance describes using Conditional Access policies for agent identities, including targeting the appropriate agents, evaluating signals, and enforcing controls as organizations deploy more agents. This is expanded documentation coverage, not evidence of a newly announced availability status.

keyChanges.title: The Conditional Access Optimization Agent guidance addresses organization-specific standards
keyChanges.detail: The updated knowledge-base article explains that knowledge bases help the Conditional Access Optimization Agent produce policy recommendations tailored to an organization’s unique standards. Administrators assessing this workflow should review the related standards and knowledge-base guidance rather than treat the update as a standalone product launch.

keyChanges.title: Identity Protection guidance clarifies reauthentication after session revocation
keyChanges.detail: The updated Identity Protection Policies guidance states that Require authentication strength and Sign-in frequency – Every time are automatically applied so that, after session revocation, users are immediately prompted to reauthenticate with the specified authentication strength. The evidence supports a documentation clarification of expected behavior, so administrators should check their policy and user-experience expectations.

keyChanges.title: Registration-campaign guidance reinforces passkey and Authenticator adoption
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID guidance explains how to run a registration campaign that nudges users toward passkeys or Microsoft Authenticator for stronger sign-in security. It is rollout and security guidance, not evidence that a new campaign capability launched during this period.

2026-06-06.headline: Entra Internet Access will change web categorization in mid-June, potentially affecting filtering
2026-06-06.overview: The period’s substantive change is a planned Microsoft Entra Internet Access update within Entra Global Secure Access: Microsoft will add an AI Agents web category and refine existing categories, which may reclassify some websites. Three Entra ID documentation pages were also marked updated, but their supplied summaries do not establish a feature, behavior, availability, or security change.
2026-06-06.adminImpact: Microsoft states that no action is required. Because site reclassification can affect category-based filtering policies, administrators should review relevant policies and adjust them if needed. No tenant action can be inferred from the three Entra ID documentation updates.

keyChanges.title: Web categorization changes are planned for Entra Internet Access
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice describes a mid-June 2026 change that adds the AI Agents category and refines existing web categories. Some sites may move between categories, potentially changing the outcome of existing filtering policies. This is a planned behavior change; the evidence does not indicate a separate preview or general-availability milestone.

2026-06-05.headline: Agent ID security and governance guidance was the substantive thread on 5 June
2026-06-05.overview: This was primarily a documentation-maintenance day: all 1,797 recorded changes were marked Updated, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The representative Entra ID changes are routine partner SSO and provisioning how-to pages, including Citrix, SAP, and Slack integrations. The more consequential updates concern Microsoft Entra Agent ID: they clarify how agent tokens differ from human sessions, how agent and blueprint identities relate, and what sponsorship means. The evidence supports security guidance and documentation clarification—not a stated preview, general-availability launch, retirement, or tenant-wide behavior change.
2026-06-05.adminImpact: Most administrators have no evidenced tenant change to implement from this day's records. Organizations deploying Agent ID should review whether their Conditional Access assumptions depend on interactive-user signals, account for the agent-risk model described by Entra ID Protection for agents, and verify that every agent identity and blueprint has a sponsor. Sponsorship should remain distinct from technical ownership, and blueprint grants merit review because they can propagate to child agents. The partner integration edits matter only where those SSO or provisioning configurations are in scope.

keyChanges.title: Agent tokens do not carry the human-user Conditional Access signal set
keyChanges.detail: Updated Agent ID security guidance says agent identities can obtain resource-access tokens without an interactive user session and without the device, location, or MFA signals that classic Conditional Access uses for human-user trust decisions. It also describes Microsoft Entra ID Protection for agents as continuously evaluating agent behavior and emitting an agent risk level. This is security guidance about the signal model, not evidence of a new Conditional Access policy or rollout.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID distinguishes identities from blueprint principals
keyChanges.detail: The updated governance guidance identifies two identity types: agent identities and agent identity blueprint principals. Both derive from service principals; blueprint principals are the provisioning surface for child agents and can hold grants that propagate to them. The documentation therefore applies service-principal ownership, lifecycle-management, and cleanup practices to these objects.

keyChanges.title: Every agent identity and blueprint requires a sponsor
keyChanges.detail: The governance update states that every agent identity and agent identity blueprint must have at least one sponsor, either a human user or supported group, with business accountability for lifecycle decisions such as access-expiry extensions and suspension during incidents. It explicitly distinguishes the sponsor from the owner responsible for technical operations and incident response, so technical ownership should not be treated as a substitute for sponsorship.

2026-06-04.headline: 4 June: Agent-aware access and governance guidance sharpened; no new Entra release was recorded
2026-06-04.overview: All eight recorded items were Microsoft Learn updates, with no new or removed entries and no Message Center notices. The most substantive changes clarify Conditional Access signals for agents, autonomous-agent policy targeting, and the resource roles available in Agent Access Packages. An External ID passkey page also documents a user capability around viewing registered passkeys. The supplied evidence does not identify a launch, general-availability event, retirement, or tenant behavior change.
2026-06-04.adminImpact: Administrators responsible for agents should compare their Conditional Access scope, autonomous-agent targeting, and access-package role design with the updated guidance. The access-package excerpt specifically identifies security groups, directory roles, and API permissions as resource roles, while cautioning against application roles. The remaining updates—including smart lockout, Connect Sync, and an OfficeSpace provisioning tutorial—appear to be documentation maintenance based on the supplied excerpts and do not establish a required tenant change.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID Conditional Access guidance now describes agent-aware risk evaluation
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance describes Conditional Access evaluating both users and agents through context, device, location, and session-risk signals, with possible outcomes including allowing, blocking, limiting, or requiring additional verification. This is a documentation update, not evidence of a new release or changed tenant behavior. Teams governing agent access should use the clarified model when reviewing existing policy design.

keyChanges.title: Autonomous-agent policies are documented as targeting all or selected agent users
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID policy guidance explicitly identifies two targeting choices: all agent users or a selected set of agent users. This clarifies policy scope for implementation and audits, but the evidence does not indicate whether the behavior is new, in preview, or generally available.

keyChanges.title: Agent Access Packages clarify supported resource-role types
keyChanges.detail: The updated instructions say agent-identity access packages can include security group memberships, directory roles, or API permissions as resource roles. The API-permission path is marked as preview in the linked guidance, and the excerpt warns not to add application roles. Administrators designing agent entitlements should validate that assignments use the documented role types.

keyChanges.title: External ID passkey guidance now includes viewing registered passkeys
keyChanges.detail: The Sign In With Passkey update includes the step that users can view their registered passkeys. The supplied record does not establish a new authentication flow, rollout status, or administrative configuration requirement, so this should be treated as a documentation clarification unless it differs from an existing implementation.

2026-06-03.headline: System-preferred authentication guidance is the main signal in an otherwise documentation-only day
2026-06-03.overview: All three changes on 3 June were Microsoft Learn documentation updates; there were no new items, removals, or evidence of a preview, general-availability release, retirement, or changed service availability. The most substantive update concerns system-preferred authentication in Entra ID. The External ID cross-tenant synchronization overview was also updated, but its supplied summary provides no technical change beyond an AI-assisted marker.
2026-06-03.adminImpact: The evidence does not support a required tenant-configuration change or a new rollout action. Administrators should treat the system-preferred authentication update as security guidance and review it against existing authentication plans. The remaining updates appear to be documentation or mapping clarifications rather than announcements of new capability.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred authentication guidance updated
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Fundamentals page describes system-preferred authentication as prompting users to use the most secure method they have registered, with passwords and SMS cited as less-secure alternatives. This is documented security guidance; the evidence does not establish a new feature launch, changed tenant behavior, or a required configuration change.

keyChanges.title: GitHub Enterprise managed-user OIDC provisioning tutorial exposes a mapping entry
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID provisioning tutorial includes the mapping expression `emails[type eq "other"].value` with type `String`. The supplied evidence supports treating this as a tutorial or attribute-mapping clarification, not as proof of a new connector capability or a mandatory change to existing provisioning.

2026-06-02.headline: 2 June 2026: documentation updates sharpen Global Secure Access filtering and SSPR bootstrap guidance; device soft delete is described as a preview
2026-06-02.overview: This was a documentation-only day: all 11 recorded changes were Microsoft Learn updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The most substantive updates cover existing implementation and operations guidance for Global Secure Access web filtering, SSPR authentication-data synchronization, Private Access, and Entra RBAC. The supplied evidence does not announce a new feature, general-availability milestone, retirement, or service-behavior change.
2026-06-02.adminImpact: The feed does not support an immediate tenant-wide configuration change. Administrators using these capabilities should review the relevant guidance, confirm whether synchronized AD DS authentication data fits their SSPR design, keep device soft delete within its documented preview scope, and use the filtering and Private Access procedures to validate policy and operational ownership. These are targeted documentation reviews, not mandatory rollout actions inferred from the update list.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access web content filtering guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Entra Internet Access how-to describes user-aware internet filtering by website category, URL, and FQDN, using security profiles and Conditional Access. This is an implementation-guidance update; the evidence does not establish that the filtering capability itself launched, changed behavior, or reached general availability.

keyChanges.title: SSPR bootstrap can use synchronized AD DS authentication data
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID SSPR guidance explains that existing authentication data from Active Directory Domain Services can be synchronized into Microsoft Entra ID and SSPR. Users can then change or reset a password without first registering contact information. The feed presents this as documentation guidance, not a new availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Device soft delete is explicitly scoped as a preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID device-soft-delete page says preview support applies to specified device types. keyChanges.title: Conditional Access agent guidance now documents high-risk sign-in MFA suggestions

keyChanges.title: Deep analysis guidance covers policy gaps, overlap, and exclusions
keyChanges.detail: Conditional Access analysis guidance clarification: deep analysis is documented as reviewing policies that block legacy authentication or device control flow and those requiring device or MFA controls. The update does not report changes to existing tenant policies.

keyChanges.title: Private Access runbook specifies connector high-resource thresholds
keyChanges.detail: Operational guidance: the updated Operate Private Access page documents a connector-host alert condition of CPU above 80% or memory above 85% sustained for more than 15 minutes. keyChanges.title: Entra schema-extension limits are spelled out
keyChanges.detail: Service-limit clarification: string extensions are limited to 256 characters and binary extensions to 256 bytes; no more than 100 extension values across all types and applications can be written to one resource. The page also limits string or binary single-valued attributes to User, Group, TenantDetail, Device, Application, and ServicePrincipal entities, and states that DateTime extensions support only the equals operator, not range operators.

keyChanges.title: Account Discovery licensing prerequisite is clarified

keyChanges.title: New Entra ID guide covers core user lifecycle tasks

2026-05-08.headline: Federation validation tightening and Verified ID key retirement are the main 8 May watch items
2026-05-08.overview: This was primarily an update and clarification day rather than a broad product launch. 2026-05-08.adminImpact: Review federated domains configured before December 2025 for mismatches between internalDomainFederation and users' UPN domains. If Verified ID deployments use non-FIPS-compliant P-256K signing keys, upgrade them before 1 July 2026. Tenants using the early-access model-driven app in-app skills control should note the 21 May service transition. The Global Secure Access and FIDO2 items are documentation clarifications with implications for preview planning and device compatibility, not evidence of new general availability.

keyChanges.title: External ID: stricter federated sign-in validation is scheduled for mid-August
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra will apply stricter federatedTokenValidationPolicy defaults starting in mid-August 2026. This is a planned security-related default-behavior change; review affected federation configurations before enforcement.

keyChanges.title: Verified ID: non-FIPS P-256K signing keys retire on 1 July 2026
keyChanges.detail: The updated Verified ID What's New entry says non-FIPS-compliant P-256K signing keys will be retired on 1 July 2026. keyChanges.title: Early-access Entra Group control will move to a new underlying service on 21 May
keyChanges.detail: For tenants that activated early access to the Entra Group control for model-driven app in-app skills in Power Apps or Dynamics 365 Apps, Microsoft says the feature will switch to a new underlying service on 21 May 2026 in preparation for general availability. keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access Explicit Forward Proxy preview documentation clarifies its Entra-based session model
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says Explicit Forward Proxy uses Microsoft Entra authentication and authorization before allowing network traffic, enabling Conditional Access, passkeys, and Continuous Access Evaluation with session revocation. Basic, digest, NTLM, and Kerberos proxy authorization methods are not supported. This is a preview behavior and configuration clarification, not evidence of a new GA release.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID FIDO2 compatibility guidance sets a Google Play Services requirement for passkeys
keyChanges.detail: The compatibility update states that passkey sign-in requires Google Play Services 21 or later because Microsoft Entra ID requires user verification for multifactor authentication. keyChanges.title: Agent ID documentation explains configuration of inheritable blueprint permissions

2026-05-02.headline: Agent ID guidance adds third-party authentication and lifecycle safeguards; Private Access documents ILA enablement

keyChanges.title: Agent ID documentation lists sign-in and audit logs for agents as new

2026-04-30.headline: Explicit Forward Proxy guidance is expanding, but the capability remains in preview

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Internet Access can use EFP with PAC-capable browsers
