Administrators should also review emergency access accounts against the passwordless-authentication guidance.

keyChanges.title: Registration Campaigns: passkey support continues with automatic tenant updates
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center update is a rollout and behavior notice, not a new passkey launch. Microsoft Entra will continue supporting Passkeys (FIDO2) in the Enabled and Microsoft-managed Registration Campaign states. Eligible tenants will receive automatic campaign-setting updates and passkey-registration nudges after MFA during the worldwide mid-May–late June 2026 rollout. No immediate administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Workday provisioning: termination lookahead guidance exposes a Pacific Time dependency
keyChanges.detail: The updated Workday connector guidance explains that the Integration System User retrieves worker data through the Get_Workers SOAP API but always operates in Pacific Time. This can delay termination-event processing for workers in time zones ahead of Pacific Time. This is an operational-behavior clarification rather than evidence of a new connector capability; time-sensitive offboarding plans should account for the documented lag.

keyChanges.title: PIM role approvals: delegated requests expire after 24 hours
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Entra role-approval guidance states that PIM can require approval and use one or more users or groups as delegated approvers. Approvers have 24 hours to act; an unapproved request must be submitted again, and the 24-hour window cannot be configured. This is a workflow clarification, not a newly announced capability.

keyChanges.title: PIM Discovery and insights remains a preview action tool
keyChanges.detail: The updated Discovery and insights page, formerly Security Wizard, describes a preview capability that analyzes privileged Microsoft Entra role assignments and lets administrators view or change permanent assignments to just-in-time assignments. The record confirms preview status and the documented actions; it does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: Emergency-access guidance points to passwordless authentication
keyChanges.detail: The updated Security Emergency Access guidance instructs administrators to configure emergency access accounts to use passwordless authentication. This is security guidance in an updated document, not evidence of a new enforcement change or feature rollout; account configuration should be reviewed against the guidance.

2026-04-23.headline: Cross-tenant group synchronization leads the day; Entra guidance adds important recovery and authentication detail
2026-04-23.overview: 23 April was primarily a documentation-update period, with no new or removed items in the supplied set. The clearest product announcement is Microsoft Entra ID Governance’s cross-tenant security group synchronization, which is described as being in public preview with general availability planned by the end of May 2026. Other notable items are updated capability documentation for backup and recovery and more specific Authenticator Lite guidance; the remaining edits are largely procedural or reference clarifications.
2026-04-23.adminImpact: ID Governance administrators evaluating cross-tenant synchronization should treat it as preview until the stated GA target and update attribute mappings and access policies if they enable it. For Authenticator Lite, verify that Authenticator push notifications are enabled for the intended users through the Authentication methods policy and account for on-premises accounts and active MFA Server exclusions. The Backup and Recovery and authentication-transfer entries are documentation updates and do not, on their own, establish a new rollout, GA event, or required tenant configuration change.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance cross-tenant security group synchronization is in preview, with GA planned
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice announces cross-tenant security group synchronization to centralize group management across tenants. It places the public preview start in late January 2026 and forecasts general availability by the end of May 2026. Administrators can enable synchronization by updating attribute mappings and access policies; the notice is a rollout timeline, not confirmation that GA has already occurred.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID documentation describes built-in, always-on backup and recovery
keyChanges.detail: The updated Agent ID What's New documentation describes Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery as built in and always on by default, with automatic backups of critical directory objects including agent IDs, users, groups, applications, service principals, managed identities, Conditional Access policies, named locations, and authentication and authorization policy. Because the evidence is an updated Learn page, it should be read as capability documentation rather than a separate launch or configuration-change notice.

keyChanges.title: Authenticator Lite guidance clarifies prerequisites and unsupported environments
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID guidance says organizations need to enable Authenticator second-factor push notifications for all users or selected groups, preferably through the modern Authentication methods policy. It also states that Authenticator Lite is not eligible for on-premises user accounts or organizations with an active MFA Server. Administrators planning to use Lite should validate policy scope and these exclusions.

keyChanges.title: Authentication transfer preview documentation clarifies scope and limitations
keyChanges.detail: The updated Conditional Access: Authentication transfer page covers supported applications, the desktop-to-mobile end-user experience, limitations, and troubleshooting. The entry remains explicitly labeled as a preview, and the supplied evidence does not indicate a new availability milestone or behavior change; teams evaluating the capability should use the documented constraints when assessing it.

2026-04-22.headline: Entra ID Governance Account Discovery is the day’s substantive rollout signal; most other changes clarify documentation
2026-04-22.overview: 22 April was primarily a Microsoft Learn maintenance day: 15 documentation updates, no new or removed Learn items, and one Message Center announcement. The consequential product change is Entra ID Governance Account Discovery, which is announced for public preview in mid-April 2026 with general availability beginning in August 2026. The strongest documentation updates clarify ID Protection self-remediation across authentication methods, Microsoft Entra Internet Access content-policy scope, and Entra Connect password-hash synchronization behavior. None of those Learn updates is presented as a separate availability milestone.
2026-04-22.adminImpact: Account Discovery is off by default and requires administrator opt-in, so there is no default user impact or mandatory action; administrators can evaluate it if they need visibility into local or orphaned application accounts. The other items support conditional review of existing ID Protection policies and runbooks, Internet Access content-policy configurations, and password-synchronization support guidance. The supplied evidence indicates no required tenant-wide change or retirement.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Governance Account Discovery: public preview with August GA target
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Message Center says Account Discovery identifies local and orphaned application accounts outside Microsoft Entra ID to improve access visibility and control. Public preview starts in mid-April 2026 and general availability begins in August 2026. The capability is off by default and requires administrator opt-in, with no user impact unless an administrator acts.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection documentation clarifies all-method risk self-remediation
keyChanges.detail: The updated Conditional Access Grant guidance says users whose risk is detected can self-remediate regardless of authentication method. It specifically states that the Microsoft-managed remediation policy accommodates both password-based and passwordless authentication. This is a documentation clarification of the supported remediation flow, not evidence of a separate feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Internet Access content-policy guidance details file and label filtering
keyChanges.detail: The updated tutorial describes network content filtering that can block uploads and downloads of selected file types, including .doc, .docx, .pdf, and .zip, when users access web applications. It also documents using Microsoft Purview to scan files and apply network-level policies based on document sensitivity labels. The evidence describes an updated tutorial, not a new availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Entra Connect password-hash synchronization behavior is clarified
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance states that users can continue signing in to cloud services with a synchronized password that has expired in the on-premises environment. The cloud password is updated the next time the user changes the password on-premises. This is a behavior clarification for administrator and support runbooks rather than a reported service change.

2026-04-21.headline: Entra ID documentation updates: FIDO2 vendor status and Group Policy backup-access guidance
2026-04-21.overview: On 21 April 2026, Microsoft Learn recorded two updates for Entra ID and no new features, previews, general-availability announcements, retirements, or message-center changes. The updates are documentation-level: a Feitian ePass FIDO authenticator entry was changed in the FIDO2 hardware-vendor material, and Group Policy backup-access guidance was clarified.
2026-04-21.adminImpact: Administrators using Feitian ePass authenticators should review the updated vendor entry before relying on its compatibility indicators; the supplied data does not identify the status columns, so it does not establish a specific capability change. Administrators responsible for Group Policy backups should verify that backup locations and network shares are restricted with appropriate Active Directory security groups and ACLs consistent with GPMC. No tenant behavior or configuration change is evidenced.

keyChanges.title: Feitian ePass FIDO2 vendor entry updated
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Fido2 Hardware Vendor documentation changed the entry for “Feitian ePass FIDO Authenticator (CTAP2.1, CTAP2.0, U2F),” including its four status markers. The evidence supports a compatibility-documentation update, but not a conclusion that Microsoft added or removed authenticator support.

keyChanges.title: Group Policy backup access controls clarified
keyChanges.detail: Updated security guidance states that backup locations and network shares should use appropriate Active Directory security groups so only authorized administrators can access backup data, with ACLs aligned to permissions used in Group Policy Management Console. This is documentation guidance for GPO backup security, not evidence of a new Entra capability or runtime behavior change.

2026-04-20.headline: No substantive Entra product change identified on 20 April; the only update was to the What's New Archive
2026-04-20.overview: The period contains one Entra ID update to Microsoft Learn's Whats New Archive, categorized under Authentications (Login). The supplied record does not describe a new feature, preview, general availability release, retirement, behavior change, or security guidance.
2026-04-20.adminImpact: No tenant configuration, rollout, or security action is supported by the available evidence. Administrators tracking authentication changes may review the archive entry, but the record provides no concrete change to implement.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID What's New Archive received a documentation update
keyChanges.detail: This is an update to the archive page rather than an identified product launch or service change. The record only names the Authentications (Login) category and gives no further detail about affected capabilities or administrator behavior.

2026-04-18.headline: External ID MFA regional opt-in clarification leads an otherwise documentation-only day
2026-04-18.overview: On 18 April 2026, all 20 recorded changes were Microsoft Learn documentation updates: there were no new items, removals, or Message Center notices. The most consequential update is preview guidance that some regions require country codes to be enabled for SMS telephony verification in Microsoft Entra External ID external tenants. Other meaningful edits clarify Agent ID setup sequencing, ID Governance relationship behavior, and Global Secure Access cloud-firewall configuration. The remaining updates are primarily routine External ID how-to documentation for federation, social sign-in, B2B collaboration, claims, API connectors, attributes, and administration; the evidence does not support treating them as launches or general-availability changes.
2026-04-18.adminImpact: External ID administrators using SMS telephony verification should check whether their regions require country-code opt-in and configure it if applicable. Teams automating Agent ID setup should create the blueprint principal only after creating the blueprint. ID Governance administrators should review the effect of any default governance policy template on newly created add-on tenants. Administrators using Remote Networks for Internet Access can review the cloud-firewall configuration guidance. No broader tenant-wide action is indicated by the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Preview: regional opt-in for External ID MFA telephony verification
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says some regions require administrators to enable country codes before external tenants can receive SMS telephony verification. This is a configuration and security prerequisite for affected regions, not evidence of a new generally available capability.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID setup sequence now separates blueprint and blueprint-principal creation
keyChanges.detail: The Agent ID AI-guided setup guidance states that the blueprint principal must be created as a separate step after the blueprint. Teams using automation or runbooks should account for that ordering; the supplied evidence supports a procedure clarification, not a product launch.

keyChanges.title: Default policy behavior for automatic governance relationships is clarified
keyChanges.detail: The ID Governance guidance explains that, when a default governance policy template is defined, creating an add-on governed tenant forms a relationship with the home governing tenant and applies that default template. Administrators should verify that the default policy reflects their intended cross-tenant governance behavior.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access cloud-firewall guidance covers Remote Networks for Internet Access
keyChanges.detail: The updated Internet Access documentation describes configuring cloud firewall to protect branch-office internet access through Remote Networks. This is security configuration guidance for deployments using that topology; the evidence does not establish new availability or changed enforcement.

2026-04-17.headline: Guest governance now depends on a linked Azure subscription; other changes are documentation-focused
2026-04-17.overview: The period has one direct operational and billing change: Microsoft Entra ID Governance requires a linked Azure subscription for guest governance actions under the Monthly Active User model. The remaining activity consists of documentation updates, including guidance for the Account Discovery preview and Global Secure Access application discovery; the supplied evidence does not establish new availability, general availability, or changed product behavior for those capabilities.
2026-04-17.adminImpact: If the tenant uses guest governance features, verify that an Azure subscription is linked. Without one, creating or updating guest-scoped policies is blocked, although existing policies continue to run. The documentation updates may help teams evaluating Account Discovery or Global Secure Access, but they do not by themselves require configuration changes or indicate a rollout.

keyChanges.title: Azure subscription required for Entra ID Governance guest governance
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center major update states that, starting January 30, 2026, tenants must link an Azure subscription to continue using guest governance features. Creating or updating guest-scoped policies is blocked without the subscription; existing policies continue to run, while new actions use subscription-linked billing under the Monthly Active User model. This is a changed prerequisite and billing requirement, not a new feature launch.

keyChanges.title: Account Discovery preview guidance updated
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID documentation now covers using Account Discovery to find and categorize existing accounts in target applications, match them to Microsoft Entra ID users, and prepare for provisioning governance. This is an update to guidance for a capability explicitly marked preview; the evidence does not show a new release, general availability, or a change to tenant behavior.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access Application Discovery guidance updated
keyChanges.detail: The updated documentation explains how Application Discovery detects applications accessed by users and supports creating separate private applications. The supplied change is documentation guidance only and does not establish new availability or require an administrator configuration change.

2026-04-16.headline: Microsoft Entra passkey campaign plans will not proceed; Global Secure Access remote-network guidance is refreshed
2026-04-16.overview: The most consequential item on 16 April is a Microsoft 365 Message Center decision not to add Passkeys (FIDO2) to Microsoft Registration Campaigns starting in April 2026; the previously planned automatic updates and nudges for MFA-capable users will not be implemented at this time. The remaining evidence is mainly documentation maintenance, focused on Global Secure Access remote-network connectivity and ID Governance license-usage guidance. There are no new or removed entries in the supplied period, so the documentation updates do not establish a new feature, preview, general-availability milestone, retirement, or tenant behavior change.
2026-04-16.adminImpact: Treat the passkey item as a change to rollout planning: the described Registration Campaign updates and nudges should not be expected at this time. The message references MC1279092 for further updates, but no details for that item are supplied here. For Global Secure Access, the updated articles are relevant to administrators working on remote-network routing or test environments; they document assignment and Azure-based simulation paths without stating that an existing tenant must be reconfigured or that availability changed. The ID Governance item is usage and entitlement monitoring guidance, not evidence of a licensing or entitlement change.

keyChanges.title: Registration Campaign passkey plans are not proceeding
keyChanges.detail: MC1253746 says Microsoft will not add Passkeys (FIDO2) as an authentication method in Microsoft Registration Campaigns starting April 2026. The previously planned automatic updates and nudges for MFA-capable users will not be implemented at this time. The notice addresses Registration Campaigns and does not describe a general passkey retirement.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access remote-network assignment guidance was updated
keyChanges.detail: The updated article describes assigning remote networks to traffic forwarding profiles through the Microsoft Entra admin center or Microsoft Graph API, with the goal of routing branch-office traffic through Global Secure Access. This is an operational documentation update; the record does not say that the capability is newly launched, in preview, or generally available.

keyChanges.title: Azure VNG simulation guidance for Global Secure Access was updated
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance covers configuring Azure resources to simulate remote-network connectivity to Microsoft's Security Edge Solutions with Global Secure Access. It supports remote-office testing scenarios, but the supplied change is a documentation update and does not announce an availability or behavior change.

keyChanges.title: License usage insights guidance was refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The ID Governance article explains how to use the license usage insights page in the Microsoft Entra admin center to monitor license usage and entitlements. Nothing in the supplied record indicates a change to licensing, entitlements, or tenant configuration; this is ordinary documentation clarification.

2026-04-15.headline: Conditional Access resource-exclusion enforcement is rolling out; most other changes are documentation maintenance
2026-04-15.overview: The most consequential item is a changed-behavior rollout in Microsoft Entra ID: Conditional Access policies targeting All resources with resource exclusions are being enforced more consistently. Related updates explain the affected sign-in scopes and how to assess or preview the impact. The remaining changes are mainly reference and how-to updates for provisioning, ID Governance, Verified ID, and Global Secure Access. The removed FAQ is a documentation-page removal; the supplied evidence does not indicate a product retirement, new GA launch, or message-center announcement.
2026-04-15.adminImpact: Prioritize review of Conditional Access policies that target All resources while excluding resources. Use the supplied impact-assessment, preview, and legacy-behavior guidance to determine whether rollout plans or tenant configuration need adjustment. Administrators using Global Secure Access (Preview) for MCP traffic can consult the updated monitoring guidance. The Kerberos update is a behavior clarification for design and troubleshooting, not evidence of a newly announced feature or security advisory.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access enforcement is changing for All resources policies with exclusions
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is rolling out an improved enforcement model for Conditional Access policies that target All resources and include one or more resource exclusions. The documented effect is that sign-ins requesting only baseline scopes receive the same Conditional Access protections as other resource access. Treat this as a changed-beavior rollout rather than a stated GA announcement, and review the related guidance for impact assessment, preview, and retaining legacy behavior.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access updates MCP traffic-log monitoring guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated Global Secure Access (Preview) page explains how to view and analyze Model Context Protocol traffic between AI agents and remote MCP servers through the Generative AI Insights page. This is operational guidance for a preview capability; the evidence does not establish a new launch or general availability change.

keyChanges.title: Entra Kerberos documentation clarifies partial-TGT behavior
keyChanges.detail: The updated Kerberos reference states that Microsoft Entra Kerberos does not issue partial ticket-granting tickets to identities that are not synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. This should be treated as a documentation clarification of an authentication boundary, so administrators should not design or troubleshoot around an expectation that unsynchronized identities will receive partial TGTs.

2026-04-14.headline: Global Relay SCIM authorization warning stands out in an otherwise documentation-only Entra ID day
2026-04-14.overview: On 14 April 2026, the feed contains 19 updated Microsoft Learn entries for Entra ID, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The meaningful operational signal is a warning that the Global Relay Identity Sync provisioning connector uses a SCIM authorization method that is no longer supported because of security concerns; the other updates are primarily routine provisioning, SCIM reference, and passkey/FIDO2 documentation edits. No new Entra capability, preview, GA, or broad behavior change is evidenced.
2026-04-14.adminImpact: If your tenant uses Global Relay Identity Sync, review the connector dependency and track the planned move with Global Relay to a more secure authorization method. The supplied documentation gives no cutoff date or immediate outage statement, so it does not support an emergency tenant-wide change. For the remaining items, consult the revised pages during relevant provisioning or FIDO2 work; they are documentation clarifications rather than evidence of a product rollout.

keyChanges.title: Global Relay Identity Sync SCIM authorization is flagged as unsupported
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID provisioning tutorial says the connector uses a SCIM authorization method that is no longer supported due to security concerns, and that efforts are underway with Global Relay to switch to a more secure authorization method. This is a security and compatibility warning; the update does not state a migration deadline or that the connector has already stopped functioning.

keyChanges.title: Passkey guidance was cross-linked to dedicated FIDO2 support documentation
keyChanges.detail: The passkey authentication page now directs readers to the Microsoft Entra FIDO2 support article. This is an ordinary documentation-navigation clarification, not evidence of a new passkey feature, preview, or general availability change.

2026-04-13.headline: Global Secure Access documentation clarifies MAU licensing for guest users
2026-04-13.overview: The only recorded change on 13 April 2026 is an update to Global Secure Access fundamentals documentation. It states that guest users are covered by Monthly Active User (MAU) licensing, which differs from the licensing model for employees. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a new feature, availability change, retirement, or changed security behavior.
2026-04-13.adminImpact: When planning Global Secure Access access for guest users, administrators should evaluate licensing using the MAU model and keep it distinct from employee licensing. The supplied evidence does not indicate a required tenant-configuration or security change.

keyChanges.title: Guest-user licensing guidance updated
keyChanges.detail: The Global Secure Access documentation now identifies MAU licensing as the model for guest users and directs administrators to the licensing overview for employee-specific details. The update provides licensing guidance rather than announcing a product capability or rollout change.

2026-04-11.headline: Guest access-review licensing guidance changed; the rest of 11 April was documentation maintenance
2026-04-11.overview: The supplied record is a quiet, documentation-only period: nine Microsoft Learn pages were updated, with no new, removed, or message-center items. The clearest substantive detail is an ID Governance licensing example for 300 guest users and a second access review; the larger Entra ID set consists of six app-provisioning tutorial updates, while Internet Access documents the enterprise-CA certificate seen during TLS inspection. The Global Secure Access guest-user licensing entry exposes only a note marker, so its product impact cannot be determined from the evidence.
2026-04-11.adminImpact: Do not treat this set as a feature rollout, preview, GA, retirement, or confirmed service-behavior change. Governance administrators using the 300-guest security-group and user-to-group-affiliation pattern should review the updated licensing example. Provisioning and Internet Access administrators can compare their runbooks and TLS-inspection certificate flow with the updated pages; the supplied evidence does not justify broader tenant configuration or licensing changes.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance licensing guidance includes a concrete guest access-review scenario
keyChanges.detail: The licensing-for-guest-users update specifically describes a Tailspin case in which a second access review is created for a security group with 300 guest users when user-to-group affiliation is enabled. Administrators can compare this scenario with their guest access-review design, but the record does not say that licensing rules or access-review behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID SaaS provisioning runbooks were refreshed across six integrations
keyChanges.detail: Updated pages cover Velpic, IDEO, Unifi, Vonage, Gtmhub, and H5mag. The supplied excerpts are procedural, including an IDEO field-format line, a Unifi screenshot, a Vonage portal sign-in step, an H5mag token-save step, and Gtmhub's description of automatic user and group provisioning and deprovisioning. This supports documentation maintenance of integration runbooks, not a new Entra provisioning capability.

keyChanges.title: Internet Access TLS inspection guidance documents the enterprise-CA certificate flow
keyChanges.detail: The updated tutorial states that the client sees a certificate signed by the enterprise CA. The evidence supports a documented certificate-flow detail for TLS inspection; it does not establish a new capability or changed service behavior. Administrators troubleshooting inspection can verify that their expected client certificate path matches this statement.

2026-04-10.headline: Agent registry and collections blades retire May 1; most other changes are documentation maintenance
2026-04-10.overview: The most consequential change on 10 April is an Agent ID management transition: Microsoft will retire the Agent registry and Agent collections blades in the Microsoft Entra admin center starting 1 May 2026. Agent 365 becomes the unified agent-management platform, and a new API will replace the existing one. The remaining activity is largely 52 Entra ID documentation updates; the supplied evidence does not establish a new feature launch, general availability change, or tenant-behavior change.
2026-04-10.adminImpact: Administrators using the Agent registry or Agent collections blades should account for their retirement and the move to Agent 365, including any dependency on the existing API. The Message Center notice says no immediate administrative action is required. For Conditional Access administrators, review the updated Agent Optimization Settings documentation if that capability is relevant to the tenant; the evidence does not indicate that configuration behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: Agent registry and Agent collections blades are being retired
keyChanges.detail: This is a service-management retirement, not merely a documentation update. Starting 1 May 2026, the two blades will be removed from the Microsoft Entra admin center. Agent 365 is designated as the unified platform for agent management, and a new API will replace the existing API.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access Agent Optimization Settings documentation highlights the Capabilities category
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID article specifically calls out important settings in the Capabilities category for review. The supplied evidence supports treating this as documentation guidance; it does not show a new preview, general availability announcement, or change in Conditional Access policy behavior.

2026-04-09.headline: 9 April 2026: a preview security capability and reference updates, with no rollout or retirement evidenced
2026-04-09.overview: All four supplied changes are updates to Microsoft Learn pages rather than new or removed items. The most substantive are documentation for Global Secure Access prompt-injection protection, explicitly marked preview, and an Entra ID optional-claims reference update covering the `acrs` claim. The External ID change is a partner-listing update, while the Continuous Access Evaluation entry contains only `- has-adal-ref`, indicating a likely mechanical reference edit. The evidence does not establish general availability, tenant-wide rollout, retirement, or a required configuration change.
2026-04-09.adminImpact: Treat this as an awareness and documentation-review day rather than a rollout day. Application teams using Auth Context IDs should review the clarified `acrs` and `xms_cc` relationship. Teams evaluating AI application protections can assess the Global Secure Access preview, but should not infer general availability from this page update. The External ID partner entry is informational migration-planning content, and the Continuous Access Evaluation edit provides no actionable behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documents prompt-injection protection as a preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated page describes using Microsoft’s AI Gateway prompt-injection protection to protect enterprise generative AI apps. It is explicitly labeled preview; the supplied evidence does not establish general availability, deployment scope, or a required administrator change.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID optional-claims reference clarifies the `acrs` claim
keyChanges.detail: The reference describes `acrs` as a Microsoft Entra ID JWT claim containing Auth Context IDs. It says these IDs indicate which operations the bearer is eligible to perform, can be used to trigger step-up authentication from an application or service, and are often used with `xms_cc`. This is reference clarification, not evidence of a new rollout.

keyChanges.title: External ID partner documentation adds a Grit Software listing
keyChanges.detail: The Services Integration Partners page lists Grit Software and describes its service for Azure AD B2C-to-Microsoft Entra External ID migrations, including the vendor’s statement that customer data is not sent to the underlying AI models. The supplied change is partner-directory content and does not evidence a change to External ID migration behavior.

2026-04-08.headline: Conditional Access guidance changes for patched Windows 11 23H2; the rest is targeted administrator documentation
2026-04-08.overview: 8 April was a documentation-maintenance period rather than a release day: all 24 supplied records are updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The most consequential item is revised Entra ID Conditional Access guidance for Windows 11 version 23H2 with KB5034848 or later. Other substantive updates cover a Windows App Protection/MAM enrollment caveat, break-glass account exclusions, and the location of authentication-context targeting controls. The page titled “Add a Microsoft Entra ID tenant as an OpenID Connect identity provider (Preview)” was updated, but the evidence does not establish a new preview rollout, general availability, retirement, or changed availability.
2026-04-08.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access exclusions associated with Windows 11 23H2: the updated guidance says KB5034848 or later removes the need for the exclusion, while retaining a policy remains an option if the toast authentication prompt is not desired. When configuring application filters, preserve the documented exclusion for emergency-access or break-glass accounts. If Windows app protection is enforced, review MAM enrollment for pre-existing unregistered Edge accounts and sign-ins that skip Heads Up Page registration. Use Assignments > Target resources > Authentication context when working with published authentication contexts. Treat the remaining link, navigation, screenshot, and reference-page edits as documentation review unless a tenant process depends on them.

keyChanges.title: Windows 11 23H2 Conditional Access exclusion guidance is revised
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID authentication guidance says the authentication prompt normally occurs after a device has been offline for an extended period, and that Windows 11 version 23H2 with KB5034848 or later no longer needs an exclusion in the Conditional Access policy. It also says a policy can still be used when the administrator does not want the authentication prompt delivered as a toast notification. This documents a behavior change; it is not evidence of a new Entra feature launch.

keyChanges.title: Windows App Protection documentation flags a MAM enrollment failure mode
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID policy guidance identifies a known issue: a pre-existing, unregistered account in Microsoft Edge, or a user who signs in without registering through the Heads Up Page, is not properly enrolled in MAM; this configuration blocks proper enrollment. Administrators relying on Windows app protection should validate the affected sign-in and enrollment paths.

keyChanges.title: Application-filter instructions explicitly exclude emergency-access accounts
keyChanges.detail: The updated Filter For Applications instructions direct administrators to use Exclude > Users and groups and select the organization’s emergency-access or break-glass accounts. This is security configuration guidance for protecting recovery access, not evidence of a new filtering capability or enforcement change.

keyChanges.title: Published authentication-context targeting path is clarified
keyChanges.detail: The Conditional Access cloud-apps documentation states that administrators select published authentication contexts under Assignments > Target resources, using the Select what this policy applies to menu. This is a navigation and configuration clarification; the supplied evidence does not indicate that authentication contexts entered preview or general availability on this date.

keyChanges.title: Policy example pages point administrators to common Conditional Access templates
keyChanges.detail: The updated Policy Block By Location page shows a link to the shared Conditional Access templates reference, and similar link-only updates appear on several other policy-example pages. This is ordinary documentation organization; the supplied evidence does not show a change to those policies’ defaults or enforcement behavior.

2026-04-07.headline: Entra guidance says custom controls do not satisfy MFA claims and clarifies the 240-policy Conditional Access limit
2026-04-07.overview: The 7 April period contained six updated Microsoft Learn pages, with no new or removed items and no Message Center announcements. This was documentation-led rather than a feature launch: the strongest operational guidance concerns migrating custom-control deployments to external authentication methods and counting Conditional Access policies in every state toward the tenant limit. Other meaningful updates cover Certificate-Based Authentication’s revocation dependency and Workload ID licensing for user-based service accounts; the remaining admin-center and custom-controls overview updates show no specific rollout or behavior change in the supplied summaries.
2026-04-07.adminImpact: Review custom-control configurations and migration plans, including whether the external provider supports external authentication methods and supplies integration guidance. Inventory Conditional Access policies in report-only, on, and off states against the 240-policy limit. Include the configuration-dependent CRL distribution point dependency in CBA resilience planning, and assess the documented user-based-license/workload-identities-license path for service accounts where relevant. The evidence supports guidance and planning actions, not a retirement date, preview, GA announcement, or new rollout.

keyChanges.title: Custom controls do not satisfy multifactor authentication claim requirements
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID Managed Policies guidance states that custom controls do not satisfy multifactor authentication claim requirements and identifies external authentication methods as their replacement. Organizations using custom controls are directed to migrate, with an external provider that supports external authentication methods and supplies integration guidance. This is security and configuration guidance, not evidence of a dated retirement.

keyChanges.title: The Conditional Access ceiling includes policies in every listed state

keyChanges.title: Certificate-Based Authentication has a configuration-dependent CRL dependency

keyChanges.title: Workload ID guidance documents licensing for service-account Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: The Mandatory Multifactor Authentication page describes a path for customers applying Conditional Access to user-based service accounts: reclaim the user-based license and add a Workload Identities license to apply Conditional Access for workload identities. This is licensing and configuration guidance, not evidence of a new Workload ID launch.

2026-04-04.headline: Agent ID architecture guidance expanded on 4 April; no service rollout is evidenced
2026-04-04.overview: The day's most substantive work focused on Microsoft Entra Agent ID: two new architecture pages were added, while related identity, service-principal, and design-pattern guidance was revised. The evidence describes Microsoft Learn documentation changes, not a feature launch, preview, general availability announcement, retirement, or changed tenant behavior. The remaining notable entries are updates to existing External ID and Entra ID administration guidance.

They should also review the documented distinctions between agent and traditional service principals for permission and lifecycle planning. The supplied records do not support any required tenant configuration change, migration, or rollout action. The External ID and joined-device updates matter primarily to administrators responsible for those areas.

keyChanges.title: New Microsoft Entra Agent ID design-patterns guidance
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Learn added a new article that maps AI-agent architectures to blueprints, agent identities, and an agent's user account. This is new architecture documentation, not evidence of a product launch or availability change.

keyChanges.title: New decision guide for planning Agent ID architecture
keyChanges.detail: A new guide helps teams choose the identity type, operation pattern, and blueprint and agent-identity structure for AI agents. It provides an architecture-planning aid; the record does not announce preview, general availability, or a tenant behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Agent service-principal guidance was updated
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance explains how agent service principals differ from traditional service principals in authentication, permissions, and lifecycle management. The change improves coverage of the Agent ID identity model, but does not state that permission or lifecycle behavior changed in the service.

keyChanges.title: External ID planning guidance highlights token-claim requirements
keyChanges.detail: The updated Planning Your Solution page notes that applications requiring specific user attributes can include them in the token sent to the application. The supplied evidence supports a documentation clarification, not a change to token issuance or supported claims.

keyChanges.title: Joined-device local-administrator guidance was updated
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID guide covers assigning Azure roles to the local administrators group of a Windows device. It documents an administration approach but does not identify a new role or changed device behavior.

Review the updated least-privilege and Conditional Access guidance for generative-AI scenarios, but do not treat it as evidence of a new tenant-wide policy or rollout. keyChanges.title: Generative-AI security guidance now emphasizes least privilege and Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: The updated Secure Generative AI architecture guidance directs organizations to enforce least privilege and use Conditional Access policies as the access-control mechanism, with examples such as requiring MFA or device compliance. keyChanges.title: A Copilot AI security documentation page was removed
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID security page titled Policy All Users Copilot Ai Security is marked Removed. keyChanges.title: Provisioning passwords are recorded as unsupported
keyChanges.detail: An updated Entra ID Known Issues page states that provisioning passwords aren't supported. 2026-04-02.headline: Authentication Methods Policy audit logs will change in April; 2 April otherwise is documentation-led
2026-04-02.overview: The clearest product-behavior update is a Microsoft Entra ID change to Authentication Methods Policy Update audit logs: records will show only changed properties with their old and new values, with worldwide rollout beginning in April 2026. keyChanges.title: Changed behavior: Authentication Methods Policy audit logs will show only changed properties
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID will change these audit-log records so they contain only changed properties with their old and new values. Rollout begins worldwide in April 2026. Event names and policy enforcement do not change, but automated log-processing logic may need review.

keyChanges.title: Access Reviews guidance clarifies halfway-point reminders
keyChanges.detail: The updated Create Access Review page documents a Reminders option that sends reminders for in-progress reviews to all reviewers halfway through the review, including reviewers who have already finished. keyChanges.title: Updated ID Governance overview documents on-premises role-model migration
keyChanges.detail: The overview directs organizations that previously used an on-premises identity governance product to guidance for migrating their organizational role model to Microsoft Entra ID Governance. keyChanges.title: Access Review Agent pages were removed, but retirement is unconfirmed
keyChanges.detail: The Learn pages Access Review Agent and Access Review Agent Logs Metrics are marked Removed. The supplied evidence confirms page removal only; it does not say that the agent or related logs and metrics capability was retired, replaced, or made unavailable.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID Manage Agents: preview documentation describes owner and sponsor controls

keyChanges.title: Account Discovery is documented as a preview provisioning-governance workflow
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID guidance covers finding and categorizing existing accounts in target applications, matching them to Microsoft Entra ID users, and preparing for provisioning governance. keyChanges.title: SCIM disable guidance states the tenant-wide API consequence
keyChanges.detail: The updated Disable SCIM API instructions say that, after confirmation and once the feature is turned off, all SCIM API calls to the tenant return an error and billing stops. keyChanges.title: Agent ID AI-guided setup lists concrete validation prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The updated setup guidance says the workflow validates that Frontier is enabled, checks Microsoft Entra roles, and verifies that PowerShell 7 or later and the Microsoft Graph beta module are installed. keyChanges.title: Agent ID security guidance highlights external exposure
keyChanges.detail: The updated Security for AI overview identifies interactions with external users, third-party systems, and the public internet as exposure paths that could allow adversaries to compromise agents and reach organizational systems. 2026-03-31.headline: Documentation-maintenance day, with Agent Registry convergence and delegated-administration scope as the main signals
2026-03-31.overview: All four reported changes are Microsoft Learn updates; there are no new or removed items and no Message Center announcements. keyChanges.title: Agent Registry guidance now describes convergence under Microsoft Agent 365
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains how Agent Registry experiences are converging under Microsoft Agent 365, what that means for Microsoft Entra Agent ID, and how to view all agents in the organization. The evidence does not establish a rollout status or require configuration changes, so this should be treated as a product-experience clarification rather than a confirmed launch.

keyChanges.title: Delegated Administration guidance clarifies post-sign-in administrative scope
keyChanges.detail: The update states that, after successful sign-in, administrators perform tasks in the governed tenant according to the roles assigned to their security group. This is an operational and permissions-model clarification; the supplied evidence does not indicate new roles, changed availability, or a security-policy change.

2026-03-28.headline: 28 March 2026: DirectAccess migration guidance and a Global Secure Access DNS prerequisite lead a documentation-heavy Entra day
2026-03-28.overview: The clearest administrator-impacting updates are a new phased migration guide for Microsoft Entra Private Access and updated Global Secure Access threat-intelligence guidance stating that DNS over HTTPS must be disabled for tunneled traffic. Microsoft Entra External ID also refreshed B2B multifactor authentication and email one-time passcode guidance. Most remaining changes are Microsoft Learn maintenance, including multitenant organization, cross-tenant synchronization, PIM, and guest-administration content. The supplied evidence shows no preview, general availability announcement, retirement, Message Center notice, or confirmed service-behavior change.
2026-03-28.adminImpact: If DirectAccess or Global Secure Access is in scope, review the phased migration path and verify the documented DNS and traffic-forwarding settings before changing rollout plans. Recheck B2B MFA and email OTP procedures where applicable. Because these are documentation updates and no service announcement is supplied, do not infer a tenant-wide configuration change or mandatory rollout from the page edits alone.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access threat-intelligence guidance specifies a DNS prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The updated configuration page states that DNS over HTTPS (Secure DNS) must be disabled to tunnel network traffic and directs administrators to use FQDN rules in the traffic forwarding profile. For deployments using this tunneling path, verify the DNS and forwarding-profile configuration. The record provides configuration guidance, not evidence that service behavior changed on this date.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Private Access gains a new DirectAccess migration guide
keyChanges.detail: The only new item is a Microsoft Learn guide for migrating client devices from DirectAccess to Microsoft Entra Private Access through a phased approach intended to avoid tunnel conflicts and connectivity failures. This is migration documentation, not evidence of a new Private Access feature, a GA milestone, or a DirectAccess retirement. Organizations planning the transition now have a documented sequence to review.

keyChanges.title: External ID B2B MFA and Conditional Access guidance was refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The updated page focuses on enforcing multifactor authentication policies for Microsoft Entra B2B users. Administrators reviewing B2B access should compare their documented policy procedures with the updated instructions.

keyChanges.title: External ID email one-time passcode fallback instructions were updated
keyChanges.detail: The updated page covers enabling and using email one-time passcode authentication for B2B guest users and describes it as a fallback sign-in method. The evidence supports a how-to refresh only; it does not establish a new preview or GA milestone or a change in availability. Review guest sign-in flows if email OTP is part of the tenant design.

keyChanges.title: Multitenant organization and cross-tenant synchronization documentation was broadly refreshed
keyChanges.detail: Updates cover multitenant organization capabilities, policy templates, provisioning, cross-tenant synchronization, topologies, and limitations. Teams implementing these patterns should recheck the relevant setup and limitations pages.

2026-03-27.headline: My Groups gains owner controls; the rest of 27 March is targeted documentation guidance
2026-03-27.overview: The clearest service change is an Entra ID My Groups enhancement: Microsoft 365 group owners will gain controls for usage guidelines, email aliases, sensitivity labels, Exchange settings, and security options when creating or editing groups. keyChanges.title: My Groups adds owner-configurable Microsoft 365 group settings
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Message Center notice says My Groups creation and editing will be enhanced by late March 2026. Owners will be able to configure usage guidelines, email aliases, sensitivity labels, Exchange settings, and security options. keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documentation makes the enriched-log prerequisite explicit
keyChanges.detail: The updated View Enriched Logs guidance says the Microsoft traffic forwarding profile must be enabled to capture traffic directed to Microsoft 365 services, which is required for log enrichment. This is operational documentation guidance; the supplied update does not announce a new Global Secure Access capability or rollout.

keyChanges.title: Application Proxy documentation clarifies SameSite cookie handling
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains that cookies without a SameSite attribute are treated as SameSite=Lax, while Application Proxy requires cookies to be preserved in a third-party context to keep users signed in. The supplied excerpt says updates were made for that requirement but does not specify a new runtime behavior, so this should be treated as configuration and troubleshooting clarification.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID security guidance expands its treatment of AI-agent risk
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra Agent ID security article introduces the security differences between autonomous AI agents and traditional applications, including agent sprawl, and describes Microsoft’s security mechanisms for agents. It is foundational security guidance rather than evidence of a new Agent ID feature, preview, or enforcement change.

2026-03-26.headline: Security Copilot’s Microsoft 365 E5 inclusion is the material change; Entra guidance was otherwise refreshed

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access guidance emphasizes scoped traffic-forwarding rollout

keyChanges.title: Private Access guidance links Kerberos access to Conditional Access and MFA
keyChanges.detail: The updated Active Directory Domain Controllers guide says to enforce Conditional Access and multifactor authentication for Kerberos authentication through Microsoft Entra Private Access. keyChanges.title: Application Proxy documentation clarifies wildcard publishing

keyChanges.title: External ID cross-tenant synchronization procedures cover API and PowerShell operation

keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra External ID / Cross-tenant synchronization

2026-03-25.headline: Tenant Restrictions V2 cross-cloud behavior clarified; Entra security and Global Secure Access guidance refreshed
2026-03-25.overview: 25 March was primarily a documentation-maintenance day: all 36 recorded changes were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The most consequential clarification concerns Tenant Restrictions V2: cross-cloud requests can be permitted at authentication while being blocked at the data plane, with a specific Windows Group Policy consequence. Other substantive updates provide app-credential escalation guidance for the Privileged Authentication Administrator role, passkey deployment guidance, compliant-network Conditional Access guidance, and documentation for Global Secure Access prompt-injection protection, which is explicitly marked preview. The evidence does not establish a new launch, general-availability milestone, or retirement.
2026-03-25.adminImpact: Prioritize a Tenant Restrictions V2 compatibility review where cross-cloud access and Windows GPO are in scope; successful authentication should not be treated as proof of data-plane access. Review assignments and application ownership or credential-management exposure relevant to the Privileged Authentication Administrator warning. Use the passkey and Global Secure Access articles as implementation or preview guidance where those capabilities are being evaluated; the supplied evidence does not indicate a tenant-wide configuration change or new rollout requirement.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Restrictions V2 documents separate cross-cloud outcomes at the authentication and data planes
keyChanges.detail: The updated External ID guidance states that TRv2 does not enforce cross-cloud restrictions at the authentication plane, so authentication is permitted, but blocks cross-cloud requests at the data plane. It specifically says Windows Group Policy users cannot access TRv2-enlightened resources across cloud boundaries. This is a documentation clarification of compatibility behavior, not evidence that a new control launched on 25 March.

keyChanges.title: Privileged Authentication Administrator guidance calls out an application-credential escalation path
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID role guidance notes that Application Registration and Enterprise Application owners can manage credentials for apps they own, and those apps may have privileged permissions. It describes how updating credentials can allow an Authentication Administrator to assume an application-owner identity and then a privileged application identity. This is security and permission-boundary guidance; the record does not say that the role permissions changed.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access guidance covers compliant-network checks with Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: The updated article explains how to require known compliant network locations for connections to secured resources through Conditional Access. It is configuration guidance for Global Secure Access; the supplied item does not establish a new availability milestone or a change to existing tenant behavior.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access Optimization Agent guidance supports passkey deployment
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID authentication article describes using the Conditional Access Optimization Agent to safely deploy a passkey program and roll out phishing-resistant authentication methods. keyChanges.title: Prompt-injection protection for enterprise generative AI apps is documented as preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated Global Secure Access security article describes Microsoft's AI Gateway prompt-injection protection for enterprise generative AI apps. 2026-03-24.headline: Entra guidance clarifies Conditional Access reauthentication and diagnostics, while affected Apple SSO clients face a compatibility migration
2026-03-24.overview: 24 March was a documentation-only update day: all 48 supplied changes were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The most consequential material clarifies existing policy behavior, troubleshooting paths, app-targeting dependencies, and Apple SSO compatibility; the supplied evidence does not identify a new feature launch, preview, general availability milestone, retirement, or tenant-wide configuration change.

Review the updated Conditional Access guidance when investigating unexpected blocks or sign-outs, designing Office 365 app-scoped policies, or tuning reauthentication frequency. Applications and MDM solutions that access Microsoft Entra device-registration keys through Keychain should assess the required move to MSAL and the Enterprise SSO plug-in. keyChanges.title: Conditional Access documents a five-minute floor for “Sign-in frequency — every time”
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification: when “every time” is selected, the service accounts for five minutes of clock skew, so users are not prompted more often than once every five minutes. If MFA was completed within the previous five minutes, another Conditional Access policy requiring reauthentication does not prompt the user again. The guidance warns that excessive prompts can reduce productivity and encourage approval of unsolicited MFA requests, and recommends using this setting only for specific business needs. This��

keyChanges.title: Authentication-flow policy troubleshooting is made explicit
keyChanges.detail: Updated operational guidance directs administrators investigating an unexpected Conditional Access block or device sign-out to open the relevant sign-in event, inspect the Conditional Access tab in Activity details, and determine whether an authentication flows policy was enforced. Selecting that policy shows which authentication flow matched. This is a troubleshooting clarification, not evidence of a new policy capability or changed rollout status.

keyChanges.title: Office 365 app targeting requires awareness of service dependencies
keyChanges.detail: The Conditional Access Cloud Apps guidance clarifies that the Microsoft 365 suite appears as “Office 365” in Conditional Access and that services are deeply integrated. Administrators should account for those dependencies when reviewing policy scope and troubleshooting outcomes; the evidence describes documentation clarification rather than a change to app targeting.

keyChanges.title: Apple SSO guidance requires affected consumers to move to MSAL and the Enterprise SSO plug-in
keyChanges.detail: Compatibility guidance says applications or MDM solutions that depend on accessing Microsoft Entra device-registration keys through Keychain must update to use the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) and the Enterprise SSO plug-in to maintain compatibility with the Microsoft identity platform. Owners of affected apps and device-management integrations have a concrete assessment and migration action, but the supplied update gives no deadline or separate retirement announcement.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection guidance spells out managed-policy response to high-risk sign-ins
keyChanges.detail: Security guidance describes a managed policy that covers all users and requires multifactor authentication and reauthentication when high-risk sign-ins are detected. Examples include highly abnormal travel, password-spray attacks, and token-replay attacks. The update explains the managed policy’s coverage and response; it does not indicate that a new policy was introduced or that administrators must change configuration.

2026-03-21.headline: Tenant Governance preview gets end-to-end documentation; risk and recovery guidance sharpen
2026-03-21.overview: The 21 March period was documentation-led. keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance gains end-to-end preview documentation
keyChanges.detail: A new ID Governance page covers deployment from setup through tenant discovery, governance, and configuration monitoring. This is a documentation addition for a preview capability, not evidence of general availability.

keyChanges.title: Identity Protection documentation clarifies risk-remediation coverage

The evidence describes documented behavior; it does not establish a new policy rollout.

keyChanges.title: Recovery History guidance documents partial-recovery status

keyChanges.title: Application recovery guidance adds a secret-impact check
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance tells administrators to validate whether application secrets were affected after determining the cause of changes. keyChanges.title: External ID WAF guidance details the Azure Front Door Premium setup
keyChanges.detail: The updated tutorial says to enable WAF protection by configuring a WAF policy and associating it with Azure Front Door Premium. 2026-03-20.headline: Documentation-heavy day: ID Governance and workload-identity guidance sharpened, with new Global Secure Access mobile diagnostics

keyChanges.title: ID Governance relationship guidance covers delegated roles and multitenant application configuration

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access publishes a mobile-client health-check article
