It provides a diagnostic path for support and administration teams; the record does not say that the utility or mobile client itself is newly available or generally available.

keyChanges.title: An iOS-specific Global Secure Access health-check page is marked removed
keyChanges.detail: The period includes a Removed record for “Troubleshoot Global Secure Access Client Ios Health Check Utility.” This establishes a page removal, not retirement of iOS support, the health-check utility, or client behavior. Administrators with internal links or runbooks pointing to the page should verify the current troubleshooting documentation.

keyChanges.title: Entra Cloud Sync prerequisites clarify supported OU structures
keyChanges.detail: The updated prerequisites state that nested OUs are supported—even an OU with 130 nested OUs—but that 60 separate OUs cannot be synchronized in the same configuration. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence that the synchronization engine’s limits changed; use the stated constraint when validating a Cloud Sync design.

2026-03-19.headline: Windows passkeys are announced for public preview; Baseline Security Mode CA-draft issue is being fixed
2026-03-19.overview: The most consequential 19 March items are two Entra ID Message Center notices: a phishing-resistant, passwordless Windows Hello passkey public preview scheduled for late March through May 2026, and a service correction for unintended disabled Conditional Access drafts. The remaining material is chiefly updated operational and security guidance for Microsoft Entra Private Access and Global Secure Access/Internet Access. Nothing supplied announces a general-availability release or retirement.
2026-03-19.adminImpact: Organizations participating in the passkey preview must opt in and configure passkey policies; existing security policies remain unchanged. Microsoft says no action is required for the Baseline Security Mode issue. Treat the Private Access and Global Secure Access items as deployment-specific configuration guidance, not as a mandatory tenant change or an availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows enter a phishing-resistant public preview
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice describes passwordless, phishing-resistant sign-in through Windows Hello on managed and unmanaged devices. The preview is scheduled for late March through May 2026 and requires organizational opt-in and passkey-policy configuration. This is a preview, not a general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Baseline Security Mode unintentionally created disabled Conditional Access drafts
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft reports that, between November 2025 and February 2026, Baseline Security Mode automatically created two disabled draft Entra Conditional Access policies in some tenants. The drafts were unintended; a fix will remove them and prevent automatic creation. Microsoft says this is not a security issue and requires no action.

keyChanges.title: Private Access guidance covers Conditional Access and MFA for Kerberos to domain controllers
keyChanges.detail: An updated Private Access procedure explains how to enforce Conditional Access and multifactor authentication for Kerberos authentication to Active Directory Domain Controllers through Private Access. This is deployment and security guidance; the supplied evidence does not identify a new capability or availability change.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access web-content-filtering guidance becomes more specific
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance describes controlling Internet Access by website category, URL, and FQDN, with granular, user-aware filtering policies built from security profiles and Conditional Access. It is a documentation clarification rather than a stated preview or GA release.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access traffic-forwarding assignments support scoped rollout
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance documents assigning users and groups to traffic-forwarding profiles, allowing administrators to limit scope during testing or deployment and roll out policies gradually. No separate feature-release status is stated.

2026-03-18.headline: Documentation maintenance dominates; the Entra ID `memberOf` dynamic-group preview is the standout capability item
2026-03-18.overview: The 18 March record contains 42 updated items, with no new, removed, or Message Center entries. The most substantive item is updated documentation for an Entra ID feature preview that builds dynamic groups and administrative units from other groups. The other meaningful exceptions are an External ID account-lifecycle warning and Entra ID clarifications on naming policies and delegated administration. Nothing supplied establishes general availability, retirement, a rollout date, or a mandatory tenant change.
2026-03-18.adminImpact: Most administrators have no evidenced action from this period. Administrators evaluating the `memberOf` preview should treat it as preview functionality; naming-policy owners should verify that their rules use supported attributes; CSP-managed tenants can use the DAP/GDAP guidance to understand delegated relationships; and organizations with legacy unmanaged accounts should assess the cleanup guidance. The supplied evidence does not provide additional prerequisites or required migrations.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID: `memberOf` dynamic groups are documented as a feature preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated article describes a preview that lets administrators create dynamic membership groups and administrative units populated from members of other groups through the `memberOf` attribute. It also says applications can read the full membership of these groups and that the groups can be used for licensing assignments. This is preview documentation, not evidence of general availability or a tenant-wide rollout.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID: groups naming-policy attribute limits are clarified
keyChanges.detail: The naming-policy guidance explicitly lists six supported built-in user attributes: Department, Company, Office, StateOrProvince, CountryOrRegion, and Title. Unsupported attributes are treated as fixed strings, while extension attributes and custom attributes aren't supported. This is an ordinary documentation clarification rather than evidence of a product behavior change on 18 March.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID: delegated-administration guidance explains CSP relationships and DAP/GDAP
keyChanges.detail: The updated article explains that the Microsoft Entra admin portal includes capabilities for administrators to see relationships with Microsoft Cloud Service Providers. It also distinguishes the older Delegated Admin Permissions (DAP) model from Granular Delegated Admin Permissions (GDAP). The supplied evidence provides no migration deadline or new-role announcement; the practical value is permissions and relationship review for CSP-managed tenants.

keyChanges.title: External ID: legacy unmanaged accounts are flagged as a persistent-access cleanup concern
keyChanges.detail: The updated cleanup guidance highlights that, before August 2022, email-verified self-service B2B sign-up could create accounts in unmanaged or “viral” tenants. Access can persist after users leave the organization. Organizations with this legacy scenario should assess whether unmanaged accounts remain and consult the cleanup guidance; the supplied summary does not specify a new cleanup mechanism or enforcement change.

2026-03-17.headline: Entra ID documents a new bulk-operations preview; Verified ID support is recorded for GCC
2026-03-17.overview: The period’s most consequential signals are narrow. Microsoft Entra ID’s bulk-operations experience is explicitly described as new and available in preview, while the Microsoft Entra Verified ID “What’s New” entry states that the service is supported in Microsoft GCC environments. Most of the 47 recorded changes were updates to how-to, API, reference, and overview documentation. The supplied evidence identifies no retirement or Message Center event and does not establish a new general-availability release. The TLS inspection update provides operational context but does not announce a new capability or behavior change.
2026-03-17.adminImpact: Large-tenant administrators can evaluate the Entra ID bulk-operations preview for bulk administration while factoring its preview status into rollout decisions. Administrators operating in Microsoft GCC environments can review Verified ID applicability for planned solutions, but the supplied evidence does not specify additional prerequisites or configuration changes. The remaining updates generally warrant documentation review rather than immediate migration, retirement, or security action.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID bulk operations are available in preview
keyChanges.detail: The new bulk-operations experience covers create, update, and delete actions for groups, devices, administrative units, and role assignments. Microsoft describes it as improving performance, reducing timeouts, and removing scaling limitations for large tenants. The item explicitly identifies the capability as a preview, not as generally available.

keyChanges.title: Verified ID support is recorded for Microsoft GCC environments
keyChanges.detail: The updated Verified ID “What’s New” entry states that Microsoft Entra Verified ID is supported on Microsoft GCC environments. The supplied text does not provide a rollout stage, prerequisites, or configuration delta, so this should be treated as an applicability and planning signal rather than evidence of a new GA launch.

keyChanges.title: TLS inspection documentation clarifies encrypted-traffic visibility
keyChanges.detail: The Entra Internet Access overview explains that TLS inspection makes encrypted content available for protections including malware detection, data loss prevention, prompt inspection, and other advanced security controls, and describes the inspection process. This is an explanatory documentation clarification; the evidence does not indicate that TLS inspection is newly released, that defaults changed, or that administrators must take a specific action.

2026-03-14.headline: Global Secure Access operational guidance dominates 14 March; system-preferred MFA precedence is clarified
2026-03-14.overview: This is a documentation refresh rather than a release event: all 39 supplied changes are marked Updated Microsoft Learn documentation, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The bulk concerns Global Secure Access, including traffic-forwarding rollout, remote-network security, SSE coexistence, and troubleshooting. The clearest Entra ID-specific clarification covers dynamic system-preferred MFA ordering and Conditional Access precedence. Nothing supplied establishes a new feature, preview, general-availability milestone, retirement, or changed tenant behavior.
2026-03-14.adminImpact: Use the updated pages for targeted operational review—especially profile assignment, remote-network policy coverage, partner coexistence, and the DFS workaround—rather than assuming a tenant-wide change. MFA administrators should ensure user and help-desk guidance reflects dynamic method ordering and Conditional Access priority. The Native Authentication API and Cloud Sync entries are too sparse or general in the supplied summaries to support a specific administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access traffic-forwarding rollout guidance was refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The updated article covers rolling out traffic-forwarding profiles to users and groups. Related same-day updates cover management of the Microsoft, Internet Access, and Private Access profiles, plus per-app and Quick Access paths to private resources. This is rollout documentation, not evidence of a newly introduced profile or availability change; teams deploying Global Secure Access should verify assignments against the current procedure.

keyChanges.title: Remote-network security guidance covers the main policy controls
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance covers applying web content filtering, threat intelligence, and cloud firewall to remote network traffic, with companion pages listing filtering categories and threat types. This is security guidance; the evidence does not say that policy semantics changed. Remote-network operators can use it to check their documented controls and scope.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access SSE coexistence guidance was refreshed across partner scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The partner ecosystem material covers integrations and coexistence, while parallel updates include solution guides for Zscaler, Netskope, Palo Alto Networks, Cisco Secure Access, Cisco Umbrella, and Cisco VPNs. The evidence supports refreshed coexistence guidance, not a new integration, preview, or GA announcement. Organizations with another SSE should consult the relevant guide when planning a mixed deployment.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred MFA documentation clarifies dynamic ordering and policy precedence
keyChanges.detail: The update says the preferred authentication-method order is dynamic, changes as stronger methods emerge and the security landscape evolves, and is subordinate to Conditional Access requirements; users can cancel and choose another available method. This is an ordinary documentation clarification, not evidence of a new MFA method or tenant policy change. Update user and help-desk explanations if they describe a fixed order.

keyChanges.title: A Global Secure Access DFS workaround is documented
keyChanges.detail: The updated troubleshooting article addresses a case where a Distributed File System does not operate correctly with Global Secure Access and includes a workaround. The stated impact is limited to deployments using DFS; the evidence does not indicate a general client or connector fix or a broader service change.

2026-03-13.headline: 13 March 2026: documentation clarifications across Entra ID, with no reported feature launches or retirements
2026-03-13.overview: All four recorded changes were updates to Microsoft Learn documentation for Microsoft Entra ID. The most relevant content concerns native-authentication feature availability and provisioning guidance for G Suite and GitHub Enterprise Managed User (OIDC). The supplied evidence does not indicate a new preview, general-availability release, retirement, changed service behavior, or tenant-wide action.
2026-03-13.adminImpact: Administrators do not have an evidenced configuration change to implement from this period. Teams planning native-authentication adoption should consult the updated availability table, while provisioning owners may want to use the clarified scoping-filter and GitHub provisioning guidance when maintaining those integrations.

keyChanges.title: Native Authentication documentation now presents feature availability by authentication model
keyChanges.detail: The Native Authentication fundamentals article was updated to show feature availability for browser-delegated and native authentication. This is an availability-documentation clarification; the evidence does not identify a new feature or change in service availability.

keyChanges.title: Provisioning tutorials received more explicit implementation guidance
keyChanges.detail: The G Suite provisioning tutorial now points administrators to the scoping-filter guidance for conditional provisioning rules. The GitHub Enterprise Managed User (OIDC) tutorial describes the Entra provisioning service’s automatic user and group provisioning and de-provisioning flow and links to the broader provisioning reference. These updates improve implementation guidance but do not report a change to provisioning behavior.

keyChanges.title: The Entra ID ‘What’s new’ page was updated with Entra Connect categorization
keyChanges.detail: The supplied change identifies an update to the ‘What’s new’ documentation and labels the service category as Entra Connect. No specific Entra Connect feature, availability milestone, or administrator action is described, so this should be treated as documentation or categorization maintenance rather than a product announcement.

2026-03-12.headline: Entra Connect’s upgrade safeguard and new Agent ID onboarding stand out in an otherwise Application Proxy-heavy documentation day
2026-03-12.overview: The 12 March feed is dominated by Microsoft Learn maintenance: a large set of updated Microsoft Entra Application Proxy PowerShell samples and integration guides. The clearest operational change is Entra Connect’s handling of servers with customized configuration files, while Agent ID receives new AI-assisted onboarding guidance covering blueprint creation, credentials, and identity provisioning. Separate updates add federated SSO certificate-rollover and Global Secure Access Secure Web Gateway guidance. The supplied evidence does not establish preview, general availability, retirement, or a tenant-wide rollout for these items.
2026-03-12.adminImpact: Entra Connect administrators should identify servers where either configuration file has been modified before the next upgrade. Teams evaluating Agent ID automation should review its credential and identity-provisioning steps against existing controls. Application Proxy administrators can use the refreshed scripts for inventory, assignments, connector groups, and certificate management. Federation and Global Secure Access teams should treat the certificate and TLS material as security and configuration guidance; no broader mandatory tenant change is evidenced.

keyChanges.title: Entra Connect auto-upgrade now skips servers with modified configuration files
keyChanges.detail: The Connect Version History update describes changed upgrade behavior: auto-upgrade detects edits to `miiserver.exe.config` and `miisclient.exe.config` and skips automatic upgrade on those servers, addressing an issue in which auto-upgrade could stop the server unexpectedly. A manual upgrade can still fail when those files were previously modified, so the linked known-issues guidance remains relevant. This is an operational behavior change, not a retirement or availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID adds AI-guided onboarding documentation
keyChanges.detail: New Agent ID guidance describes using an AI coding agent, such as GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, to automate onboarding. The workflow includes blueprint creation, credential configuration, and agent identity provisioning. The evidence establishes new setup documentation, but does not identify the workflow as preview or generally available and is not evidence of a product launch.

keyChanges.title: Application Proxy documentation refreshes its PowerShell operations runbook
keyChanges.detail: The updated PowerShell sample set documents inventorying Application Proxy apps and private network connectors, assigning users and groups, and retrieving certificate information. Related examples cover connector-group moves, custom and default domains, wildcard publishing, token-lifetime policies, and bulk certificate replacement. These are documentation and scripting updates; the supplied evidence does not describe a new Application Proxy service capability.

keyChanges.title: Federated SSO guidance emphasizes automated SAML certificate rollover
keyChanges.detail: The updated federated SSO certificate tutorial gives ISVs best practices for automated rollover as SAML certificates approach expiry. It notes that Entra signing certificates typically expire every one to three years and that customer and SaaS-provider coordination is needed to avoid downtime. This is security and operational guidance, not evidence that Entra changed certificate lifetimes or introduced automatic rollover.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documentation details SWG defense-in-depth and TLS checks
keyChanges.detail: Global Secure Access Secure Web Gateway material describes five security layers forming an inspection chain for internet-bound traffic. Same-day pages frame checks around keeping TLS inspection failures below 1% and preventing custom bypass rules from duplicating system bypass destinations. This is security and configuration documentation; no new SWG availability milestone or behavior change is supplied.

2026-03-11.headline: Windows passwordless guidance explicitly records passkey OOBE and Web sign-in support; Lifecycle Workflows documents non-impacting simulation, alongside a broad Application Proxy ­
2026-03-11.overview: 11 March was a documentation-led day for Microsoft Entra. All 11 records were updates to Microsoft Learn pages: there were no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. Eight Entra ID pages also form a coordinated Microsoft Entra Application Proxy guidance refresh. The evidence does not classify any item as a preview, general-availability release, retirement, or confirmed service-behavior change.
2026-03-11.adminImpact: Treat this as a documentation review rather than a rollout notice. Application Proxy administrators should compare their architecture, connector and authentication, security, deployment, onboarding, custom-domain, SSO, troubleshooting, and home-page runbooks with the refreshed guidance; no specific tenant change is identified. Teams using Windows passwordless sign-in should verify that OOBE and device-unlock procedures align with the documented passkey and Web sign-in scenarios, although prerequisites are not supplied here. Lifecycle Workflows administrators can use the documented What-if path to preview execution before affecting actual users. The remaining SLA Performance update shows a 2026 column but provides no evidence of an SLA or service-level change.

keyChanges.title: Windows passwordless guidance explicitly covers two device sign-in scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID passwordless Windows documentation states that OOBE sign-in with a passkey is supported and that Web sign-in can unlock a Windows device. This is a support statement in updated guidance; the supplied record does not establish that either capability launched or changed service behavior on 11 March.

keyChanges.title: Lifecycle Workflows documents What-if simulation without user impact
keyChanges.detail: The updated ID Governance guidance explains how to use the What-if tool to simulate workflow execution and preview results without affecting actual users. It provides an operational way to inspect expected workflow outcomes, but the evidence identifies an updated guide rather than a new, preview, or generally available feature announcement.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Application Proxy guidance was refreshed across the deployment lifecycle
keyChanges.detail: Eight Entra ID pages were updated around Application Proxy, covering architecture, connectors, authentication, security, deployment planning, app onboarding, troubleshooting, custom domains, single sign-on, and custom home pages. This is a broad documentation refresh; the supplied evidence does not state a change to Application Proxy availability or behavior.

2026-03-10.headline: 10 March 2026: Entra documentation clarifies external-user catalog settings and access-review scope; no rollout is evidenced
2026-03-10.overview: This was a documentation-led period: all seven tracked items were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The most consequential edits are in ID Governance: catalog guidance now ties the Enabled for external users setting to access-package policies for connected organizations, while access-review guidance distinguishes group or application reviews from access-package reviews. Other updates cover security-key and S/MIME wording, administrative-unit group procedures, support, and developer setup. The supplied evidence identifies no new feature, preview, general-availability release, retirement, or changed service behavior.
2026-03-10.adminImpact: No tenant change or rollout action is established by the evidence. Catalog owners should verify that the documented Enabled for external users setting and the relevant access-package request policies match whether external users should be able to request access. Administrators using security keys, access reviews, or administrative units should consult the refreshed procedures; the remaining support and developer-account edits appear to be documentation maintenance.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management clarifies the control for external catalog requests
keyChanges.detail: The Catalog Create guidance says to set Enabled for external users to Yes when users in external directories from connected organizations should be able to request access packages, and to pair that setting with an access-package policy allowing those users to request. It says to set the setting to No when the catalog is intended only for users already in the directory. This is an administrative guidance clarification, not evidence of a new capability.

keyChanges.title: Access Review guidance separates group or application reviews from access-package reviews
keyChanges.detail: The Perform Access Review page describes reviews of group members and users with application access, and directs administrators to a separate entitlement-management article for access-package reviews. The change clarifies which procedure applies to each resource type; it does not announce a change to access-review behavior.

keyChanges.title: Passwordless security-key guidance adds S/MIME wording
keyChanges.detail: The Windows security-key documentation includes “S/MIME using a security key.” The supplied record does not establish whether this represents new support or changed behavior, so it should be treated as updated authentication and security guidance rather than a feature launch.

keyChanges.title: Administrative-unit guidance distinguishes creating a group from adding an existing group
keyChanges.detail: The Admin Units Members Add instructions clarify that one request creates a new group directly in an administrative unit, while adding an existing group uses the separate Add groups to an administrative unit procedure. This is a procedural documentation clarification.

2026-03-09.headline: Entra ID documentation clarifies tenant deletion and licensing PowerShell examples
2026-03-09.overview: The 9 March period contained two Microsoft Learn updates for Entra ID, with no evidence of a new feature, preview, general-availability launch, retirement, or service-behavior change. The most consequential update adds explicit managed-administrator guidance to the tenant-deletion procedure; the other adjusts a licensing automation code sample.
2026-03-09.adminImpact: Administrators planning tenant deletion should verify that their procedure includes a managed administrative account from the tenant being deleted. Teams using the licensing PowerShell/Graph example should review the revised sample if their scripts need the group identifier. No broader tenant configuration change is indicated.

keyChanges.title: Tenant-deletion guidance adds a managed administrative account step
keyChanges.detail: The Directory Delete Howto now includes a step to create or use a managed administrative account in the tenant being deleted, with an example account format. This is a procedural documentation clarification, not evidence of a change to the deletion service itself.

keyChanges.title: Licensing PowerShell/Graph example adds the group ID to its output
keyChanges.detail: The licensing example now adds a `Group ID` property populated from `$group.Id`. Administrators maintaining scripts or local copies of this example should review the revised code if they need the group identifier in their results; the update does not indicate a change to licensing behavior.

2026-03-07.headline: AI Administrator RBAC expands for Agent 365; native-authentication OTP guidance points to a Private Preview
2026-03-07.overview: 7 March was mostly a documentation-maintenance day: 58 of 67 records were updates, eight were new, and none were removals. The clearest operational change is the single Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about expanded AI Administrator permissions for Agent 365, with rollout starting in March 2026. Entra ID also added a coordinated set of native-authentication guides for email and SMS OTP MFA and strong authentication method registration; one updated tutorial explicitly points to a Private Preview. The 27 ID Governance records are chiefly PIM how-to updates, and their supplied summaries do not establish a new PIM capability or changed behavior.
2026-03-07.adminImpact: Administrators should review AI Administrator role assignments and delegation boundaries ahead of the March 2026 rollout. The expanded scope includes Agent 365 lifecycle management, tenant-wide consent except Microsoft Graph app permissions, and Identity Protection risk monitoring. Application teams using native authentication should review the new client-capability, authentication-context, and registration guidance, while treating the OTP material as preview guidance rather than evidence of GA. Dynamic-group owners should review who can write the attributes referenced by membership rules in Microsoft Entra ID and connected source directories. The supplied PIM summaries indicate documentation maintenance, not a confirmed configuration change.

keyChanges.title: AI Administrator role gains Agent 365 and Identity Protection scope
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says the AI Administrator role is being updated for Agent 365. Routine agent management can be delegated without Global Admin involvement; the expanded scope covers agent lifecycle management, tenant-wide consent except Microsoft Graph app permissions, and risk monitoring through Identity Protection. This is a service and RBAC rollout notice, not a documentation-only edit.

keyChanges.title: New native-authentication guidance documents email and SMS OTP MFA for apps
keyChanges.detail: New Entra ID documentation shows how to add email and SMS one-time-passcode MFA to an Android app using native authentication. Related entries extend the implementation guidance to iOS/macOS and to registering email or SMS OTP as a strong authentication method. The feed supports a documentation expansion, not a stated feature launch or GA announcement.

keyChanges.title: Native Authentication OTP MFA is explicitly presented as a Private Preview
keyChanges.detail: An updated Android strong authentication method registration tutorial tells implementers to enroll in a Private Preview of SMS and Email OTP MFA on Native Authentication. That status is the important availability boundary: the new material should be read as preview implementation guidance, and the supplied evidence provides no GA or broad-rollout statement.

keyChanges.title: Dynamic-group security guidance focuses on attribute write access
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID guidance says the security of a dynamic group’s membership depends on who can modify the attributes referenced by its rule. It specifically calls for reviewing write permissions in Microsoft Entra ID and connected source directories before choosing an attribute. This is security guidance and clarification, not evidence that dynamic-membership behavior changed.

2026-03-06.headline: 6 March 2026: Entra ID documents Bulk Operations preview limits and staged Token Protection rollout
2026-03-06.overview: This was a documentation-update day rather than a confirmed release or retirement: all 22 records were updates, with no new or removed entries. The most consequential changes clarify the current scope of Entra ID Bulk Operations (Preview), provide more explicit Token Protection rollout and token-theft monitoring guidance, and document an External ID cross-tenant limitation. The remaining updates are mainly provisioning connector tutorials, app integration instructions, and other how-to maintenance; the evidence does not support treating them as new feature launches or general availability announcements.
2026-03-06.adminImpact: Treat Bulk Operations as a preview limited to Groups, Devices, and User Export; do not plan on Enterprise Applications support yet. For Token Protection on Apple, follow the documented report-only assessment step before enforcement, and review the Defender XDR monitoring guidance if token-theft detection is in scope. For External ID, account for the documented inability of B2B users to manage certain Microsoft 365 services in remote tenants. No broad tenant configuration change is indicated by this set of documentation updates.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Bulk Operations preview scope is specified
keyChanges.detail: The updated What's New entry describes the Bulk Operations service as Preview and says it currently supports Groups, Devices, and User Export. Enterprise Applications are not yet supported and are described as coming soon. This is a scope and availability clarification, not evidence of general availability or a launch date.

keyChanges.title: Token Protection guidance requires a report-only phase before enforcement
keyChanges.detail: The updated Apple deployment guide instructs administrators to deploy the Token Protection policy in report-only mode first, assess its effect, and identify noncompliant sign-in sessions before enforcing it. This is rollout guidance, not evidence of a change to enforcement behavior or availability.

keyChanges.title: Token-theft defense guidance points to Defender XDR monitoring
keyChanges.detail: The updated Protecting Tokens guidance tells administrators to deploy Defender XDR workloads to alert on suspicious or anomalous behavior surrounding token theft. The supplied evidence supports this as security guidance and does not indicate that a new Defender XDR integration launched.

keyChanges.title: External ID documents a cross-tenant B2B management limitation
keyChanges.detail: The updated Known Issues page states that B2B users are unable to manage certain Microsoft 365 services in remote tenants, such as Exchange Online, because there is no directory picker. This records a known limitation rather than a fix or changed product behavior.

2026-03-05.headline: Entra ID documentation clarifies seven-day report retention, TAP/Windows Hello flows, and provisioning-agent prerequisites
2026-03-05.overview: On 5 March 2026, Microsoft Learn recorded seven Entra ID documentation updates. There were no new or removed items and no Message Center announcements. 2026-03-05.adminImpact: Review the updated guidance where your tenant uses these workflows, especially reporting, TAP-assisted device setup, Windows Hello for Business, or provisioning agents. keyChanges.title: Entra reports retain only up to seven days of activity data
keyChanges.detail: The updated retention guidance states that the free version stores up to seven days of activity data and that moving to a premium version still exposes only up to seven days. keyChanges.title: Temporary Access Pass setup behavior is clarified for Windows join and Windows Hello

keyChanges.title: SMS sign-in configuration guidance was updated without a demonstrated rollout
keyChanges.detail: The revised page covers how to configure and enable users to sign in to Microsoft Entra ID using SMS. 2026-03-04.headline: 4 March 2026 was mainly documentation maintenance, with native-authentication reference changes and an ID Governance page removal standing out
2026-03-04.overview: Microsoft Entra had 14 documentation updates and one removed page, with no Message Center items. Account Recovery and Agent ID viewing are also described in updated pages, while most other edits concern prerequisites, permissions, links, or explanatory material. 2026-03-04.adminImpact: No broad tenant configuration or licensing action is supported by this evidence. Treat the remaining prerequisite and access wording changes as documentation clarification unless the full pages show otherwise.

keyChanges.title: Native Authentication Challenge Types reference was updated
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID reference states that new challenge-type values are added when native authentication supports new authentication methods. keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID overview describes Account Recovery as enabling users to regain access after losing all authentication methods through identity verification. 2026-03-03.headline: 3 March 2026: Global Secure Access source-IP behavior and Conditional Access rollout guidance clarified
2026-03-03.overview: This was a documentation-only day: all 10 recorded changes were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. Two updates have clear operational relevance. Global Secure Access guidance explains how source IP restoration affects the origin seen for authentication requests, while Entra ID Conditional Access guidance describes the agent’s suggestions throughout a phased rollout. The remaining provisioning, governance, and security-page edits do not, in the supplied evidence, establish a new feature, preview, general availability event, retirement, or changed tenant requirement.
2026-03-03.adminImpact: Prioritize review if you use Global Secure Access as a cloud proxy or have an active Conditional Access phased rollout. Check source-IP assumptions in authentication controls and consult the rollout guidance before progressing or rolling back. No broader tenant action is supported by the supplied record; the other edits appear to be documentation maintenance.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access: authentication requests can appear from the proxy IP
keyChanges.detail: Updated authentication guidance says that when Global Secure Access is deployed as a cloud-based network proxy, failing to enable source IP restoration causes all authentication requests to come from the proxy’s IP address rather than the user’s actual public egress IP. This is a security-relevant behavior clarification, not evidence of a new feature or availability milestone. Administrators should verify that authentication designs relying on source-IP visibility account for this behavior.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Conditional Access: phased-rollout agent guidance covers the full process
keyChanges.detail: Updated Conditional Access documentation says the phased-rollout suggestion remains present throughout the rollout and can report no action needed, recommend progressing to the next phase, or suggest rolling back. This clarifies the agent’s operational guidance for an in-progress rollout; it is not presented as a new launch, preview, or GA change. Administrators running a phased rollout should review the suggestion as they move through its phases, with no separate tenant configuration change identified here.

2026-02-28.headline: External ID guidance clarifies paid SMS limits, customer password recovery, and role permissions; Entra ID MFA guidance also changed
2026-02-28.overview: 28 February was a documentation-clarification day: all four recorded items were Microsoft Learn updates—three for External ID and one for Entra ID—with no new, removed, or Message Center items. The clearest operational point is that External ID SMS is described as an additional-cost option for second-factor verification and self-service password reset, not first-factor authentication. The evidence does not establish a new feature launch, preview, general-availability change, retirement, or tenant-wide behavior change.
2026-02-28.adminImpact: For External ID tenants, validate SMS-based MFA and password-reset designs against the stated cost and first-factor restriction. Also check customer recovery flows and assumptions about default versus assigned permissions. The system-preferred MFA record provides no specific configuration or behavior delta, so treat it as guidance to review rather than evidence of a rollout action.

keyChanges.title: External ID SMS is documented as paid second-factor and SSPR support only
keyChanges.detail: The updated Multifactor Authentication Customers guidance states that SMS is available at additional cost for second-factor verification and self-service password reset in external tenants, but is not currently supported for first-factor authentication. This is a documented support and cost boundary, not evidence of a newly launched capability.

keyChanges.title: Email OTP guidance clarifies the customer self-service recovery path
keyChanges.detail: The updated Email OTP page says customers can change or reset their passwords without administrator or help-desk involvement. It also describes prompts that let customers unblock themselves after an account lockout or forgotten password. The record clarifies the recovery experience but does not identify a new availability or behavior change.

keyChanges.title: External ID role and default-permission guidance is clarified
keyChanges.detail: The updated Supported Features Customers page states that roles and administrators are supported for administrative and user accounts, roles are supported for all users, and users in an external tenant have default permissions unless assigned an admin role. Administrators should check designs that depend on default permissions or explicit admin-role assignment.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred MFA guidance was updated without a specified product change
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID System-preferred multifactor authentication page was updated with guidance on how to use the capability. The supplied record gives no detail about changed policy, availability, configuration, or rollout status, so it should be treated as an ordinary documentation update rather than evidence of a launch, preview, retirement, or behavior change.

2026-02-27.headline: 27 February 2026: Internet Access web-filtering guidance updated amid a broad Entra documentation sweep
2026-02-27.overview: This was a documentation-maintenance day rather than a product-launch day: all 1,510 recorded changes were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The most specific change describes Microsoft Entra Internet Access web content filtering—domain-name filtering integrated with Microsoft Entra ID and Conditional Access. Most of the other representative Entra ID changes refresh partner SSO and automatic provisioning/de-provisioning guides; External ID direct federation and Global Secure Access Points of Presence documentation were also revised. No preview, general-availability announcement, retirement, security advisory, or runtime behavior change is identified in the supplied evidence.
2026-02-27.adminImpact: No immediate tenant change is supported by this evidence. Administrators using the named capabilities should review the revised documentation when validating an existing or planned configuration, particularly web-filtering policies, direct-federation settings, or partner provisioning. These updates alone do not support enabling a feature, changing Conditional Access, or inferring a new network-location rollout; the Points of Presence excerpt has no before/after context or column definitions.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Internet Access — Web Content Filtering guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated page describes the service’s first Secure Web Gateway features as domain-name-based web content filtering, with granular policies tied to Microsoft Entra ID and Conditional Access so filtering can be user- and context-aware. This is an ordinary documentation update in the supplied record, not evidence of a new preview, GA milestone, retirement, or changed filtering behavior.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID partner integration guides received a broad refresh
keyChanges.detail: The representative set includes SAML single sign-on guides and automatic user provisioning/de-provisioning tutorials. The Netskope entry specifically documents provisioning and de-provisioning between Microsoft Entra ID and Netskope User Authentication. These records describe configuration guidance, not a stated change to the underlying SSO or provisioning service or to connector availability.

keyChanges.title: External ID — Direct Federation configuration considerations
keyChanges.detail: The Direct Federation page points administrators to configuration considerations in the SAML/WS-Fed identity-provider guidance. The supplied change is marked Updated and does not state a new federation mode, availability change, or enforcement or behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access — Points of Presence table update
keyChanges.detail: The update excerpt includes a France South point of presence in Marseille, France, with both displayed status markers checked. 2026-02-26.headline: Entra Connect’s domain-join prerequisite is the clearest operational update; the rest is documentation maintenance
2026-02-26.overview: 26 February 2026 was a quiet Microsoft Entra documentation day. The updated Entra Connect prerequisites explicitly state that Microsoft Entra Connect must be installed on a domain-joined server. Other targeted edits cover guest-user licensing, Quick Access licensing references, and device-identity export controls. All supplied items are documentation updates: there are no new, removed, or Message Center entries, and the evidence does not support calling any item a feature launch, preview, general-availability milestone, retirement, or security advisory.
2026-02-26.adminImpact: Admins planning new Microsoft Entra Connect installations should verify that the target server is domain joined. The guest-user licensing and Configure Security updates are useful references for entitlement reviews, but the supplied summaries do not establish a changed licensing rule. The device-identity item is a usability/documentation clarification, and no tenant-wide remediation or rollout action is evidenced. The remaining version-history, tutorial, and minimum-license edits are not specific enough to establish an Entra behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra Connect prerequisite is explicitly documented
keyChanges.detail: The updated Connect Install Prerequisites page states that Microsoft Entra Connect must be installed on a domain-joined server. This is an operational prerequisite or documentation clarification, not evidence of a new Connect capability or changed service behavior. For a new installation, check the target server’s domain-join status; the evidence does not indicate that existing deployments must be changed.

keyChanges.title: Guest-user licensing guidance was updated
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Entra ID Governance Licensing for Guest Users page was updated to explain how Microsoft Entra ID is licensed for guest users. The supplied summary gives no specific entitlement, pricing, or policy change, so this should be treated as refreshed guidance rather than a licensing announcement.

keyChanges.title: Configure Security documentation includes a Quick Access licensing reference
keyChanges.detail: The updated Configure Security content includes a reference for Quick Access user or group assignments alongside the Microsoft Entra Suite Add-on for Microsoft Entra ID P2. 2026-02-25.headline: Graph-based External ID username validation and scoped Lifecycle Workflows are the key exceptions in a documentation-maintenance day
2026-02-25.overview: 25 February was quiet in release terms: all 20 recorded items were Microsoft Learn updates, with no new or removed entries and no Message Center notices. The substantive content is concentrated in ID Governance guidance for delegated workflow management and custom-attribute triggers, an External ID clarification that custom username regex validation is configured through Microsoft Graph rather than the admin center, and an explicitly preview Global Secure Access Prompt Shield page. The remaining updates are largely app-integration tutorials and troubleshooting or reference edits; the supplied evidence does not indicate a GA launch, retirement, service-behavior change, or mandatory tenant action.
2026-02-25.adminImpact: Focus review on the pages with direct design or operational implications. Workflow owners can assess whether Administrative Unit scoping should limit who manages particular Lifecycle Workflows, and whether custom attributes can supply needed triggers. External ID teams requiring custom username validation need a Microsoft Graph configuration path because validationRegEx is not exposed in the admin-center UI. Global Secure Access teams evaluating AI Gateway Prompt Shield should treat it as preview guidance. The health-check and other tutorial edits support troubleshooting or configuration work, but the evidence does not justify a broader rollout or configuration change.

keyChanges.title: External ID Sign In Alias: custom regex validation is configured through Graph
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says admins can set a custom regular expression through validationRegEx on the username attribute. The setting is not currently available in the admin center UI; the documented route is Microsoft Graph's authenticationAttributeCollectionInputConfiguration resource, with an example tied to a self-service sign-up user flow. This is a documentation clarification and configuration constraint, not evidence of a new External ID rollout.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance: delegate Lifecycle Workflows by Administrative Unit
keyChanges.detail: The updated page describes delegated workflow management: by default, workflows are managed by users with Lifecycle Workflows or Global administrator roles, while Administrative Unit scoping can limit specific admins to specific workflows. This provides a least-privilege administration option; the record does not say the capability launched or changed behavior on this date.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance: use custom attributes as Lifecycle Workflow triggers
keyChanges.detail: The page documents using custom attributes as execution conditions for automatic workflow runs when the default attribute set is insufficient, including scenarios involving users moving within the organization. Administrators reviewing workflow design can use the guidance to identify where a custom attribute is needed; the update itself does not establish a new availability milestone.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access: Prompt Shield is documented as preview security guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated security page describes protecting enterprise generative AI applications from prompt-injection attacks with Microsoft's AI Gateway Prompt Shield. Because the title explicitly labels the capability as preview, this should be treated as preview guidance rather than a GA announcement; the supplied record gives no rollout or configuration requirements.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access: client health-check troubleshooting guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated Windows client troubleshooting page directs administrators to use the Health check tab in the Advanced diagnostics utility. This is an operational documentation clarification for diagnosing client issues, not evidence of a client feature change or availability event.

2026-02-24.headline: Application Proxy/Traffic Manager setup and SPA consent guidance were clarified; Global Secure Access documents a preview URL-filtering option
2026-02-24.overview: 24 February was a documentation-maintenance day: all six recorded items were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The most meaningful changes clarify Application Proxy and Traffic Manager setup, make SPA scope-consent behavior explicit, and list a valid URL (Preview) option in Global Secure Access web-content-filtering instructions. The evidence does not establish a new feature launch, general availability milestone, retirement, or service-behavior change.
2026-02-24.adminImpact: The supplied evidence does not identify a mandatory tenant-wide action. Administrators using Application Proxy with Traffic Manager should compare their configuration with the updated URL guidance; application owners should verify that SPA scopes match the documented sign-in consent experience; and Global Secure Access administrators should confirm whether the documented URL (Preview) input is available in their tenant before relying on it. The App Proxy overview change is modernization guidance, while two other updates do not provide enough detail to infer administrator impact.

keyChanges.title: Application Proxy and Traffic Manager guidance reiterates the required setup and URL definitions
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID page states that Traffic Manager use requires Application Proxy configuration and refers to defined URLs for the subsequent steps. This is a procedural documentation clarification, not evidence of a new integration or changed service availability. Organizations using this topology should compare their configuration with the revised instructions.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access web filtering instructions list a URL option marked Preview

keyChanges.title: Single-page app guidance makes sign-in consent for added scopes explicit

keyChanges.title: App Proxy fundamentals emphasize Entra ID as the control plane for on-premises apps
keyChanges.detail: The updated overview presents extending Microsoft Entra ID to an on-premises environment as a major benefit and connects moving away from on-premises authentication with reducing the on-premises footprint and using Entra identity management as the control plane. 2026-02-23.headline: Global Secure Access external user access guidance was updated

2026-02-21.headline: Documentation-only day: Global Secure Access compatibility and Kerberos guidance sharpened

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documentation lists Azure Virtual Desktop single-session support
keyChanges.detail: The Install Windows Client page now states that Azure Virtual Desktop single-session is supported. This is the clearest deployment-relevant change in the record; no client version, prerequisite, or indication that support was newly introduced is provided.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access Kerberos SSO guidance includes an nltest command
keyChanges.detail: The Configure Kerberos SSO update includes `nltest /dsgetdc:contoso /keylist /kdc`. This gives administrators a documented command in the Kerberos SSO workflow, but the evidence does not indicate a changed Kerberos requirement or protocol behavior.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Managed Policies documentation surfaces MFA-for-all-users content
keyChanges.detail: The Managed Policies update includes a “Multifactor authentication for all users” section or link. keyChanges.title: Entra ID service-limits documentation shows a Category/Limit table

2026-02-20.headline: 20 February 2026: documentation clarifies Internet Access, Agent ID, External ID, and PIM administration
2026-02-20.overview: This was a documentation-maintenance period: 83 updates were recorded, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The most useful updates are implementation clarifications and security guidance—not evidence of a new feature launch, preview, general availability change, retirement, or changed service behavior. Most other supplied updates concern routine partner SSO and provisioning tutorials.
2026-02-20.adminImpact: Most administrators do not need to change tenant configuration solely because these Learn pages were updated. Review the relevant guidance if you operate Internet Access, Agent ID, External ID BYOD, or PIM: verify the Conditional Access delivery model, establish ownership and token settings for agent blueprints, set expectations about registered-device tenant switching, and use task-specific roles rather than Global Administrator where appropriate.

keyChanges.title: Internet Access: Conditional Access is documented as the policy-delivery path for web filtering
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says administrators create a Conditional Access policy for users or groups and deliver Internet Access security profiles through Conditional Access session controls. It identifies Conditional Access as the mechanism that provides user and context awareness for Internet Access policies. This is an implementation clarification, not a launch announcement.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID: blueprint setup now details accountability and token-facing configuration
keyChanges.detail: The Agent ID guidance describes an agent identity blueprint as the basis for creating agent identities and requesting tokens. It calls for assigning an owner and sponsor, and for configuring an identifier URI and scope when agents created from the blueprint will receive requests from other agents or users. The update does not establish preview or general availability status.

keyChanges.title: External ID: BYOD guidance documents a registered-device tenant-switching limitation
keyChanges.detail: For a Windows Microsoft Entra registered device, the documented experience is that the user selects a tenant at first sign-in and remains connected to it; switching to other registered tenants is not currently supported. The guidance distinguishes this from switching to a resource tenant through external user access, or B2B. It clarifies expected behavior rather than stating that the service behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: PIM deployment guidance reinforces least-privilege role assignment
keyChanges.detail: The PIM Deployment Plan update advises assigning users the least-privileged role needed for their tasks, minimizing Global Administrator assignments, and using specific administrator roles for particular scenarios. This is security and deployment guidance, not evidence of a new PIM capability.

2026-02-19.headline: Microsoft Rewards account linking retires on 19 March; new Entra web-filtering guidance is the main documentation thread
2026-02-19.overview: The clearest operational event on 19 February is the retirement of Azure AD Account Linking for Microsoft Rewards, rather than a change to Entra sign-in or access-policy behavior. Work-account linking will stop by 19 March 2026, while existing points and personal accounts remain unaffected. Most other notable entries are documentation additions or clarifications: new Web content filtering material, a revised passkey support matrix, updated Application Proxy and Traffic Manager guidance, and a documented Global Secure Access port limitation. No supplied item establishes preview, general availability, or broader service-behavior changes.
2026-02-19.adminImpact: Microsoft explicitly says no administrator action is required for the Rewards retirement. Administrators evaluating Web content filtering should treat the new category-rule, security-profile, and Conditional Access pages as design documentation, not as evidence of a launch or required tenant changes. Teams using passkeys, Application Proxy with Traffic Manager, or Global Secure Access should review the relevant updated guidance and limitation, but the evidence does not support a general remediation requirement.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Rewards retires Azure AD Account Linking
keyChanges.detail: This Message Center major update says Azure AD Account Linking for Microsoft Rewards will retire by 19 March 2026. Users will no longer be able to link work accounts to earn Rewards points; existing points and personal-account use are unaffected. Microsoft states that no administrator action is required. This is a feature retirement in the Rewards experience, not an announced change to Entra authentication or access controls.

keyChanges.title: New Web content filtering documentation connects rules, security profiles, and Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: A set of new Entra ID documentation pages covers category-based Web content filtering rules, policy linkage to security profiles, and integration with Conditional Access. The supplied evidence identifies documentation additions only; it does not establish preview, general availability, a launch, or changed service behavior.

keyChanges.title: The passkey/FIDO2 authentication matrix was updated
keyChanges.detail: The revised Microsoft Entra ID matrix addresses web-browser and native-app support for FIDO2 passwordless authentication. This is a compatibility-documentation update, not evidence that new client support or a tenant configuration change became available on this date.

keyChanges.title: Application Proxy guidance specifies regional Traffic Manager endpoints
keyChanges.detail: Updated Microsoft Entra Application Proxy guidance says that, in a Traffic Manager solution, each app's regional Application Proxy URL should be added as an endpoint. This is an implementation clarification for administrators using that architecture; the evidence does not announce a change to Application Proxy availability or runtime behavior.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documentation records an HTTP/S port limitation
keyChanges.detail: The updated Current Known Limitations page states that Global Secure Access assumes standard HTTP/S ports 80 and 443. Administrators whose designs depend on nonstandard HTTP/S ports should treat this as an operational constraint to review. The update does not say that the platform newly imposed this limitation.

2026-02-18.headline: Global Secure Access timing and Agent ID governance guidance lead a documentation-heavy 18 February
2026-02-18.overview: The most actionable clarification is in Global Secure Access: web content filtering changes made in the Global Secure Access experience typically take effect in less than five minutes, while related Conditional Access changes take approximately one hour. Other meaningful updates cover Agent ID administrative relationships, the Entra ID control for blocking new app password credentials, and Access Reviews API behavior when notifications are disabled. All 29 tracked entries are marked Updated, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The supplied record therefore supports documentation clarification, security guidance, and governance/API guidance—not a confirmed feature launch, preview, GA release, or retirement.
2026-02-18.adminImpact: Use the two documented propagation windows when validating or scheduling web content filtering changes. If your organization administers Agent ID, review accountability across owners, sponsors, and managers. App-registration administrators should verify the documented password-credential restriction against their security policy, while access-review automation should account for contactedReviewers returning users who were or would have been notified even when notifications are turned off. The remaining summaries do not support broader tenant action on their own.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access: web content filtering propagation expectations are explicit
keyChanges.detail: Classification: ordinary operational documentation clarification. The updated page distinguishes changes made in the Global Secure Access experience, which typically take effect in less than five minutes, from Conditional Access changes related to web content filtering, which take approximately one hour. The evidence clarifies expected timing but does not say that the timings themselves changed.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID guidance separates technical administration from business accountability
keyChanges.detail: Classification: governance guidance. The updated administrative-relationships page describes a model separating technical administration from business accountability and applies it to agent identities, agent identity blueprints, and agent identity blueprint principals. This gives administrators a more specific framework for reviewing Agent ID accountability; it is not presented as a new availability milestone.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID documents the app password-credential restriction control
keyChanges.detail: Classification: security and configuration guidance. The update directs administrators to select Restricted Mode and locate the setting "Block addition of new password credentials to apps." It clarifies the control's location and name, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the control is newly introduced or that tenant settings changed.

keyChanges.title: Access Reviews clarifies reviewer-notification API semantics
keyChanges.detail: Classification: API behavior documentation clarification. The FAQ states that the contactedReviewers API returns users who were, or would have been, notified to perform a review, even when notifications were disabled, and includes timestamps indicating when notification would occur. Audit and automation workflows can use this behavior when reconciling reviewer populations and notification schedules; the entry does not claim a new API release.

2026-02-17.headline: Documentation-only updates: TAP lifetime guidance and Workload Identity Federation security content
2026-02-17.overview: The 17 February period contains two Microsoft Learn updates, covering Entra ID Temporary Access Pass (TAP) authentication and Workload ID federation. The evidence indicates documentation clarification or refreshes—not a new feature launch, preview, general-availability change, retirement, or confirmed service-behavior change.
2026-02-17.adminImpact: Administrators should check whether internal TAP procedures and workload-authentication guidance match the revised documentation. The supplied changes do not establish that tenant configuration or service behavior must change.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID TAP documentation now specifies the minimum-lifetime setting and range
keyChanges.detail: The updated Temporary Access Pass documentation table lists a minimum lifetime of 1 hour and an allowed range of 10–43,200 minutes (30 days). This is evidenced as a documentation update; it does not by itself prove that the Entra ID policy default or tenant behavior changed. Administrators using TAP should reconcile this wording with their internal runbooks and configured policy.

keyChanges.title: Workload ID federation guidance was refreshed around secretless access
keyChanges.detail: The Workload Identity Federation page was updated to describe how external software workloads can access Microsoft Entra-protected resources without managing secrets. The record supports a security-guidance refresh, but does not identify a new capability, availability milestone, or required configuration change.

2026-02-14.headline: Guest licensing guidance was clarified; the remaining Entra updates are primarily documentation maintenance
2026-02-14.overview: On 14 February 2026, all five reported changes were updates to Microsoft Learn documentation, with no new, retired, or Message Center items. keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access configuration navigation was clarified

keyChanges.title: Workload ID guidance highlights the risk of privileged workload identities
keyChanges.detail: The updated Workload ID monitoring guidance warns that privileged roles assigned to service principals or managed identities create significant exposure if those identities are compromised. Administrators can use this guidance to prioritize review of privileged workload-identity assignments; it is not evidence of a new enforcement feature.

keyChanges.detail: The update explains that an application with open assignment can still retain security controls when provisioning is properly scoped, such as through department filters or group-membership requirements. Applications lacking both assignment restrictions and provisioning scoping can create unrestricted access pathways that attackers may exploit. Review applications that provision accounts to determine which controls limit their scope.

keyChanges.title: Compromised guest identities are documented as a persistence and lateral-movement risk
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID security guidance warns that compromised guest identities can establish credential persistence, exploit trust relationships with internal resources, and serve as staging points for lateral movement toward more privileged assets. This supports reviewing guest access paths and the connected resources exposed through those relationships.

keyChanges.title: Dormant external guests are called out as a monitoring blind spot
keyChanges.detail: The monitoring update says prolonged dormancy of external guest accounts can give attackers time for reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and backdoor establishment because monitoring often focuses on active internal users. Include dormant guest accounts in monitoring reviews rather than limiting attention to currently active internal users.
