keyChanges.title: ID Protection’s Identity Risk Management Agent guidance now describes a Preview operating model
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance identifies the Identity Risk Management Agent as Preview and describes analysis of risky identities, suggested remediation, and LLM-assisted review of risky activity. Three new pages cover the agent, its settings, and findings in the Risky user report, while older similarly named agent pages were removed. This indicates documentation restructuring; it does not establish general availability or that the capability itself was retired.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID documentation now defines four governance object types
keyChanges.detail: The updated Agent Id Governance Overview documents agent identity blueprints, agent identity blueprint principals, agent identities, and agent users. It explains that agent identities—and optionally agent users—can give AI agents digital identities in Microsoft Entra, which can then be governed through lifecycle and access features, with sponsors assigned to agent identities. This is an updated governance model description, not evidence of a new GA release.

keyChanges.title: Access Review guidance documents an agent-assisted Teams workflow
keyChanges.detail: The updated Perform Access Review page says the Access Review Agent assists with pending reviews in Microsoft Teams using natural-language guidance, insights, and recommendations. The supplied change is documentation guidance and provides no availability, licensing, or rollout details, so it should not be treated as a confirmed launch.

keyChanges.title: Sign-in documentation clarifies how MFA retries appear in Azure Monitor
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sign In Log Activity Details page explains that failed or timed-out MFA validations can generate multiple MFA events. Microsoft Entra sign-in logs show those events as one line item, whereas Azure Monitor can show multiple line items sharing the same correlationId. This is a monitoring and interpretation clarification rather than evidence that the sign-in behavior changed on this date.

2025-11-28.headline: External ID documentation details Security Store access to security capabilities
2025-11-28.overview: The only change on 28 November was an update to Microsoft Learn documentation for Microsoft Entra External ID. It describes integrated security capabilities—including DDoS protection, sign-up fraud prevention, and unified monitoring—as well as partner integrations available through the Microsoft Security Store and the Security Store blade wizard. This is a documentation update, not evidence of a new launch, preview, general availability change, or retirement.
2025-11-28.adminImpact: Review the updated External ID guidance against current tenant security configuration and rollout plans, particularly where the Security Store blade could provide access to these capabilities or partner solutions. The evidence does not establish a new availability date or require a migration.

keyChanges.title: External ID security feature and partner access is documented through the Security Store
keyChanges.detail: The updated Supported Features Customers page explains that organizations can enable described security solutions directly in External ID and access partner integrations through the Microsoft Security Store, with the features available through a Security Store blade wizard. Administrators should treat this as clarified product documentation rather than proof of a newly introduced capability.

2025-11-27.headline: Entra ID Protection alert defaults change on 11 December; most other updates clarify documentation
2025-11-27.overview: The clearest administrator-facing change is an upcoming Microsoft Defender XDR behavior change for Entra ID Protection alerts: risk-level filtering will be introduced and the default will become High risk only. The other meaningful items are Microsoft Learn updates covering a macOS platform credential preview, access-package assignments for agent identities, and Entitlement Management catalog restrictions. The supplied evidence does not establish a general-availability launch, retirement, or tenant-wide rollout for those documentation entries.
2025-11-27.adminImpact: Plan to review Defender XDR alert configuration by 11 December. If Medium-risk or all alerts are required, select the High + Medium or All option when available. In Entitlement Management, ensure required groups or applications are already in the catalog before an access package manager uses them. Treat the macOS and Agent ID entries as planning and governance documentation, not as evidence of GA availability or a required rollout.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Protection alerts in Defender XDR will default to High risk only
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Message Center says that starting 11 December 2025, Defender XDR will let administrators filter Entra ID Protection alerts by High only, High + Medium, or All. The default will change to High risk only, reducing alert volume. This is an upcoming alert-behavior change rather than a retirement.

keyChanges.title: macOS platform credentials are now listed as a preview prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID planning documentation for phishing-resistant passwordless authentication was updated to include “Platform credential for macOS (preview).” This supports rollout planning, but the supplied change does not establish general availability or a new tenant configuration requirement.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID governance documentation describes access-package assignments
keyChanges.detail: The Agent ID Governance Overview now documents that agent identities can receive resources directly through access packages. An agent can request a package itself, or its owner or sponsor can request one on its behalf. This clarifies the documented governance and request paths; it does not state a launch or availability status.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management catalog boundaries are clarified
keyChanges.detail: The Access Package Resources documentation states that access package managers can use only resources already available in the package’s catalog. They cannot add resources to a catalog, even when they own those resources. This is a documentation clarification of an operational restriction, so catalog availability must be handled before package creation.

2025-11-26.headline: 26 November: Entra guidance sharpened agent governance, token claims, and LDAP SSL setup—no new release evidenced
2025-11-26.overview: This was a documentation-led period: 17 pages were updated, none were new, no Message Center items were supplied, and one External ID page was removed. The most substantive updates clarify governed access and ownership for agent identities, the documented OnTokenIssuanceStart flow for custom claims providers, and a certificate-permission prerequisite for on-premises LDAP connector SSL. External ID’s domain-acceleration note and the removal of the Solutions Customers page are documentation changes; the evidence does not establish a product retirement, new availability, or changed service behavior.
2025-11-26.adminImpact: The supplied evidence does not indicate a tenant-wide configuration change. Administrators managing AI agents should review access-assignment and ownership processes. Teams using custom claims providers should check their event, provider, and application mapping, while LDAP connector deployments using SSL should include the NETWORK SERVICE certificate-read permission. The remaining ID Governance updates are mainly role, sign-in, and catalog-instruction clarifications; the Global Secure Access entry provides no version or fix details requiring action.

keyChanges.title: Access packages are documented as the governance model for agent identities
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra entitlement-management guidance describes access packages as a way to make agent access intentional, auditable, and time-bound, including standardized access for fleets of agents. This is a governance documentation clarification, not evidence of a new access-package or Agent ID capability becoming available. Organizations governing agent permissions can use the guidance when moving away from ad-hoc assignments.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID (entitlement management and agent identities)

keyChanges.title: Agent ID guidance calls for maintained sponsors and owners
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says sponsors and owners should be assigned and maintained for each agent ID to prevent orphaned identities. This is lifecycle guidance rather than a stated enforcement change; organizations operating agent IDs should check that ownership is assigned and retained.

keyChanges.title: Custom claims provider documentation clarifies OnTokenIssuanceStart
keyChanges.detail: The updated overview states that OnTokenIssuanceStart is triggered when a token is about to be issued, is configured within a custom claims provider, and can use a REST API to map claims from external systems into tokens for one or more applications. The change clarifies the documented flow rather than announcing a new event. Administrators using this capability should validate their event, provider, and application assignments against the description.

keyChanges.title: LDAP connector SSL instructions add a certificate permission prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The on-premises LDAP connector preparation guidance specifies that SSL requires granting NETWORK SERVICE read permission on the newly created certificate. This is deployment and security configuration guidance, not a product release. Teams setting up the connector with SSL should include this permission step.

2025-11-25.headline: Tenant Restrictions v2 scope and Agent ID workflows are the meaningful updates; no confirmed feature rollout is evidenced
2025-11-25.overview: The 25 November period contains six Microsoft Learn updates and no new, removed, or Message Center entries. The clearest changes clarify External ID Tenant Restrictions v2 coverage and Agent ID collection and application-assignment procedures. These records describe documentation updates rather than establishing a preview, general availability release, retirement, or changed service behavior. A What's New Archive entry is labeled “New feature,” but the supplied evidence does not identify the feature.
2025-11-25.adminImpact: Treat this as primarily a documentation-review day. Administrators validating Tenant Restrictions v2 should account for the documented Office app scope, including all versions and release channels. Teams managing Agent ID should consult the updated collection and application-assignment guidance. The evidence does not support an immediate tenant-wide configuration change or rollout action.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Restrictions v2 documentation lists coverage for all Office apps
keyChanges.detail: The External ID Tenant Restrictions V2 page now includes “All Office apps (all versions/release channels)” in its documented scope. This is a concrete scope clarification; the record does not establish a service-behavior change or a new availability status.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID application-assignment guidance calls out the SAML helper registration
keyChanges.detail: The Assign Agent Identities To Applications page identifies the SAML helper application registration as the resource. This adds a specific procedural detail for Agent ID application assignments, but the evidence does not indicate a new capability or rollout.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID collection management is documented as a tabbed view
keyChanges.detail: The Agent Registry Manage Collections page describes the Agent collections view as a tabbed section containing two options. Because the supplied excerpt does not name the options or describe a behavior change, this should be read as a navigation or documentation clarification rather than a launch.

keyChanges.title: Windows 11 OOBE guidance for Microsoft Entra join was refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID page provides guidance for setting up Microsoft Entra join on a Windows 11 device during OOBE. The record supplies no changed prerequisites, policy requirements, or availability information, so the supported impact is to use the updated instructions when reviewing provisioning procedures.

2025-11-22.headline: Native Authentication guidance gains setup and model clarifications; cross-tenant custom-role documentation also updated
2025-11-22.overview: The 22 November period contains three Microsoft Learn documentation updates: two covering Native Authentication and one covering Cross Tenant Custom Roles. The clearest substantive edit adds guidance for associating an app registration with a user flow in External ID. The evidence indicates documentation clarification, not a new feature launch, preview, general availability announcement, retirement, security advisory, or confirmed runtime behavior change.
2025-11-22.adminImpact: Treat this as a documentation-focused update. Administrators implementing External ID Native Authentication should verify the app-registration and user-flow association guidance. Administrators using cross-tenant custom roles should review the updated Actions table. The supplied summaries do not establish a required tenant change, rollout, or permission change.

keyChanges.title: External ID Native Authentication documentation adds app-registration and user-flow guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Native Authentication API page now includes guidance to associate an app registration with the user flow. This is an implementation-documentation change; the evidence does not indicate that the API, user flow, or availability changed. Teams implementing this setup should review the linked procedure.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Native Authentication documentation updates the authentication comparison
keyChanges.detail: The Native Authentication page updates a comparison covering browser-delegated authentication and native authentication. This clarifies the documented distinction between the approaches, but does not by itself establish a new capability or behavior change.

keyChanges.title: External ID cross-tenant custom-role documentation updates its Actions table
keyChanges.detail: The Cross Tenant Custom Roles page has an updated Actions table. The supplied excerpt does not identify which actions changed, so no specific role, permission, or tenant-configuration impact can be inferred from this update alone.

2025-11-21.headline: 21 November 2025: Entra documentation clarifies federation limits, RDP access, and agent API consent
2025-11-21.overview: All 10 supplied records are Microsoft Learn updates; there are no new or removed records and no Message Center item. The period therefore reflects documentation clarification rather than a feature launch, preview, general-availability change, or retirement. The most consequential details concern a regional Workload ID restriction, an Entra ID Remote Desktop access limitation, the Agent ID API-consent model, and the guest-account consequence of external access-package assignment.
2025-11-21.adminImpact: Check the Workload ID region list before creating federated identity credentials on user-assigned managed identities. If Remote Desktop access on Microsoft Entra joined devices relies on groups delivered through the Assign Local Admin policy, review that design and use the documented individual-user SID path. For Agent ID integrations, review the OAuth scopes and service-principal consent involved; for external access packages, account for the guest account created by direct assignment. These are targeted review points, not evidence of emergency tenant-wide remediation.

keyChanges.title: Workload ID: regional limitation for federated identity credentials
keyChanges.detail: The updated Workload Identity Federation Considerations guidance says federated identity credentials cannot currently be created on user-assigned managed identities in certain regions. The supplied extract does not include the region names, so administrators should use the page’s region list when planning deployments. This is a documented constraint, not evidence of an availability expansion.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID: device-policy groups do not apply to Remote Desktop
keyChanges.detail: The updated Assign Local Admin guidance states that Microsoft Entra groups deployed to a device through this policy do not apply to Remote Desktop connections. To control RDP permissions on Microsoft Entra joined devices, it directs administrators to add the individual user’s SID to the appropriate group. This is a documented behavior caveat, not a reported new policy feature.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID: application API access is modeled through OAuth scopes and consent
keyChanges.detail: The assignment guidance explains that an application can expose an API and OAuth scopes, while the tool’s service principal can be granted consent to those scopes to call the API. For agent integrations, the concrete administrative concern is which scopes and consent are assigned; the update does not by itself establish a new release or availability stage.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Kerberos: an internet access scenario is spelled out
keyChanges.detail: The updated Kerberos page describes an Entra ID-joined Windows client accessing a file share or application over the internet, with Microsoft Entra ID issuing the necessary Kerberos tickets as a KDC associated with the resource. This is an architecture and scenario clarification; the supplied evidence does not say that tenant configuration or availability changed.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance: direct external assignment creates a guest account
keyChanges.detail: The access-package request-policy guidance says that, after an access package is created, administrators can directly assign internal or external users and that specifying an external user creates a guest user account in the directory. This is a lifecycle detail to account for when managing external assignments, not evidence of a new entitlement-management policy.

2025-11-20.headline: A future passkey-policy API retirement is the day’s material Entra change
2025-11-20.overview: The 20 November evidence is led by a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update: Microsoft plans to retire two duplicative properties from the Microsoft Entra ID passkey (FIDO2) policy API in the October–November 2027 window. The other substantive entries are updated TLS inspection guidance for Global Secure Access and Microsoft Entra Internet Access, plus Entra Connect certificate-monitoring guidance. The supplied record contains no new-feature, preview, or general-availability announcement; the latter items are documentation clarifications.
2025-11-20.adminImpact: Identify configurations, automation, and integrations that use the affected passkey-policy properties and plan the schema update ahead of the retirement window. Teams using TLS inspection can review the updated policy-assignment and certificate-authority guidance, but the evidence does not establish a new availability milestone. Entra Connect operators can use the documented 30-day threshold and Event IDs 1011 and 1012 in the Application event log as certificate-rotation monitoring signals. The remaining role, permission, tutorial, and reference-page edits do not provide enough detail to justify a configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra ID schedules retirement of two passkey-policy API properties
keyChanges.detail: Retirement and future API schema change: Microsoft plans to retire isAttestationEnforced and keyRestrictions from the fido2AuthenticationMethodConfiguration API from October through November 2027. During the transition, the notice says these properties will sync with new properties in the updated passkey policy API schema. Administrators must update configurations, automations, and integrations that depend on them; the notice does not announce an immediate change to end-user authentication behavior.

keyChanges.title: TLS inspection policy-assignment guidance was updated
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification and security guidance: the updated Global Secure Access page covers configuring a TLS inspection policy and assigning it to users. Related updates cover inspection certificate-authority settings and explain that Microsoft Entra Internet Access can make encrypted-traffic content available for malware detection, data loss prevention, prompt inspection, and other advanced controls. The supplied evidence does not identify this as a new preview or general-availability milestone.
keyChanges.product: Global Secure Access and Internet Access

keyChanges.title: Entra Connect certificate-rotation monitoring guidance was clarified
keyChanges.detail: Ordinary troubleshooting documentation, not a behavior-change announcement: Microsoft Entra Connect warns when a certificate expires in 30 days or less, logs warning Event ID 1011, and emits error Event ID 1012 when the certificate is already expired. Both signals are available in the Application event log, giving operators concrete monitoring points for certificate rotation.

2025-11-19.headline: Agent ID preview guidance expands around tenant control and sign-in, while Security Copilot enters a phased E5 rollout
2025-11-19.overview: The meaningful changes on 19 November center on Microsoft Entra Agent ID preview operations rather than a confirmed broad general-availability launch. New Learn content covers the agent sign-in, consent, and trust flow, plus known issues; updated guidance says agent identities are enabled by default and clarifies preview security coverage. A separate Message Center notice announces Microsoft Security Copilot inclusion in Microsoft 365 E5 with phased rollout and Entra group controls. Five Agent App Lifecycle pages are marked removed, but the supplied records do not establish whether content was consolidated or whether a capability was retired.
2025-11-19.adminImpact: Review Agent ID tenant controls before allowing or piloting agent identities, and use the new sign-in and known-issues guidance for consent, trust, permissions, and troubleshooting planning. Treat ID Protection for agents as a preview capability covered by Microsoft Entra P2, not as a general-availability entitlement. For Security Copilot, monitor the phased E5 rollout and use Entra ID group membership controls as described. The removed lifecycle pages warrant bookmark or link checks, but the evidence does not support concluding that the underlying product capability was retired.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID is documented as enabled by default, with tenant-control guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says agent identities are enabled by default in all Microsoft Entra ID tenants and explains that customers can configure settings to control which Agent IDs are allowed. It also identifies Agent ID as subject to standard preview terms. This is an updated guidance statement, not evidence that the default changed on this date.

keyChanges.title: New Agent ID sign-in documentation defines consent and trust checkpoints
keyChanges.detail: A new article describes the Agent ID sign-in process, including consent pages, trust criteria, and management of agent permissions for secure access to AI agents using work accounts. It is an operational documentation addition; the record does not claim a new sign-in feature or general availability.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID preview gets a dedicated known-issues reference
keyChanges.detail: A new troubleshooting page covers current known issues and errors encountered in the Microsoft Entra Agent ID preview. The supplied summary does not enumerate those issues, so administrators should consult the page during pilots and troubleshooting rather than infer a specific blocker or required fix from this record.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection for agents is explicitly a P2 preview entitlement
keyChanges.detail: The updated Risky Agents guidance states that ID Protection for agents is included with a Microsoft Entra P2 license while the capability is in preview. This is a licensing and lifecycle clarification, not a general-availability announcement; pilot owners should validate entitlement and account for the preview status.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot inclusion in Microsoft 365 E5 brings an Entra-controlled rollout
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice says Microsoft Security Copilot is included at no extra cost in Microsoft 365 E5, providing AI-driven security agents across Defender, Entra, Intune, and Purview. Rollout is phased; monthly Security Compute Units are based on user count, and administrator controls are provided through Entra ID group membership. The notice does not indicate immediate access for every tenant.

2025-11-13.headline: External ID documentation clarifies the Akamai integration’s external-tenant context
2025-11-13.overview: Microsoft updated the “Configure Akamai Integration” documentation for External ID to reference an external tenant. The evidence indicates a documentation clarification, not a new feature launch, preview, general-availability change, retirement, or documented behavior change.
2025-11-13.adminImpact: Administrators configuring the Akamai integration should review the updated guidance and its linked external-tenant documentation to determine whether their tenant configuration or rollout plans are affected. No migration or security action is supported by the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Akamai integration guidance now references an external tenant
keyChanges.detail: The External ID page “Configure Akamai Integration” was updated with a reference to an external tenant and linked creation guidance. The supplied change does not establish any change to the integration itself or to availability.

2025-11-11.headline: Sensitivity-label task guidance leads a quiet day; Entra ID and External ID add permission and WAF checks
2025-11-11.overview: 11 November was primarily a documentation-led period. A new ID Governance article explains how to see sensitivity labels during Lifecycle Workflows task creation; an Entra ID update identifies Group.Read.All as the least-privileged permission for viewing groups in health-alert notification guidance; and an External ID update calls for testing after a Cloudflare WAF connection. The evidence does not establish a preview, general-availability release, retirement, or service-behavior change.
2025-11-11.adminImpact: Impact is targeted rather than tenant-wide. Lifecycle Workflows administrators can review how labels are surfaced while creating tasks; administrators reviewing health-alert notifications should verify that Group.Read.All is the documented least-privileged permission for viewing groups; and teams connecting Cloudflare WAF to External ID should test the resulting configuration. The workflow-run reprocessing edit appears procedural, with no stated behavior change or mandatory migration.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance — new Lifecycle Workflows sensitivity-label guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Learn article explains how to see sensitivity labels during Lifecycle Workflows task creation. This is documentation describing a capability, not evidence of a new rollout, preview, or general-availability change.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID — health-alert guidance identifies Group.Read.All as least privilege
keyChanges.detail: The updated health-alert notification guidance states that Group.Read.All is the least-privileged permission required to view groups. This is a concrete permission and security clarification; it does not state that tenants must change existing assignments.

keyChanges.title: External ID — Cloudflare WAF guidance adds post-connection testing
keyChanges.detail: The updated integration guidance says to test the configuration after connecting Cloudflare WAF with Microsoft Entra External ID to confirm that it works. This is an operational documentation clarification, not evidence of a new integration launch or availability change.

2025-11-10.headline: Global Secure Access domain-controller guidance updated for client IP addresses
2025-11-10.overview: The only change on 10 November 2025 was an update to the Microsoft Learn page “Configure Domain Controllers” for Global Secure Access. The supplied evidence identifies “Client IP address” as the changed area, but does not indicate a new feature, availability change, retirement, or changed product behavior.

keyChanges.title: “Configure Domain Controllers” documentation updated
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft updated the Global Secure Access configuration guidance in the client IP address area. 2025-11-08.headline: Private Access ILA (preview), Internet Access limitations, and Entra security guidance were updated—but no launch or retirement is evidenced
2025-11-08.overview: All nine recorded items were updates to Microsoft Learn pages; there were no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The supplied evidence does not establish a launch, general availability transition, retirement, or changed service behavior; the remaining edits are mainly role and reference-page maintenance.

The excerpts do not justify changing tenant settings, role assignments, TLS configuration, or availability assumptions without page-level review.

keyChanges.title: Private Access: Intelligent Local Access preview enablement guidance updated
keyChanges.detail: The updated page explains how to enable Intelligent Local Access for Microsoft Entra Private Access and describes the capability as optimizing traffic flow for clients accessing Entra apps through private networks. It remains explicitly labeled preview in the supplied evidence; this is documentation for enablement, not evidence of general availability or a new service rollout.

keyChanges.title: Internet Access: current known-limitations reference updated
keyChanges.detail: The Current Known Limitations page was updated, but the supplied extract does not identify a specific limitation or say whether one was added, removed, or changed. keyChanges.title: Entra ID security guidance highlights Zero Trust Assessment automation

2025-11-07.headline: Number-matching documentation changed; guest-review licensing and External ID monitoring guidance were clarified

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Authentication: same-device number-matching guidance was updated
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Authenticator article was updated to cover improvements to same-device number matching. The supplied record provides no configuration instructions, rollout stage, or availability claim, so it does not establish a tenant-side change or a new release.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Authentication: the MFA number-match preview page was removed
keyChanges.detail: The MFA Number Match Preview documentation page was removed from Microsoft Learn. The record does not say whether the underlying capability was retired, made generally available, or otherwise changed; the page removal alone should not be treated as a product-lifecycle announcement.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance: guest-scoped access-review creation has a stated licensing constraint

keyChanges.title: ID Protection: centralized Log Analytics collection is recommended

2025-11-06.headline: Entra previews group-based passkey controls while cloud security groups gain 30-day recovery
2025-11-06.overview: The most consequential changes on 6 November are two Microsoft Entra ID Message Center updates: passkey profiles are entering preview in the authentication methods policy, and soft deletion/restoration is being introduced for cloud security groups. The remaining meaningful items are documentation clarifications for External ID fraud protection and ID Governance licensing for guests; the supplied Verified ID and Global Secure Access summaries do not establish additional product behavior changes.
2025-11-06.adminImpact: No action is required before the passkey preview rollout, but Microsoft advises reviewing authentication-method configurations and updating documentation afterward. Cloud security-group deletion will remove access until restoration, while deleted groups can be recovered for 30 days and actions are audited. Tenants using ID Governance features for guests should verify the stated Azure subscription and add-on requirement. The External ID item is integration guidance, not evidence of a new service rollout.

keyChanges.title: Passkey profiles enter the authentication methods policy preview
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is previewing passkey profiles in November 2025. The policy adds group-based passkey controls and a new API schema. Rollout is worldwide in early November and in GCC in mid-November; Microsoft says no pre-rollout action is needed, but administrators should review configurations and update documentation.

keyChanges.title: Cloud security groups become restorable after deletion
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is introducing soft deletion and restoration for cloud security groups. Deleted groups can be recovered within 30 days with their settings, ownership, and membership preserved; access is removed until restoration, and audit logs track the actions. The capability is in preview from late October 2025, with general availability indicated for February 2026.

keyChanges.title: External ID fraud-protection integration guidance is clarified
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Entra External ID documentation describes using the Security Store wizard in the Entra admin center to create a fraud protection provider policy for Arkose Labs. This is a documentation update and does not, from the supplied evidence, establish a new availability or rollout event.

keyChanges.title: Guest ID Governance licensing requirements are spelled out

2025-11-05.headline: Entra ID’s MFA app-password documentation was updated; no product change is evidenced
2025-11-05.overview: 5 November was a quiet period: the only recorded change was an update to Microsoft Learn documentation for Entra ID MFA app passwords. keyChanges.title: MFA app-password guidance updated

2025-11-04.headline: Entra ID’s 4 November updates are documentation-led: certificate-based authentication gets an IMPORTANT notice, while Free-license content points to phishing-resistant admin-prote​
2025-11-04.overview: All four changes were updates to Entra ID Microsoft Learn pages; there were no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. 2025-10-07.headline: 7 October was documentation-led, with Source of Authority guidance as the clearest substantive Entra ID update
2025-10-07.overview: Microsoft Entra ID updates centered on a related Source of Authority (SOA) documentation refresh. The clearest guidance describes moving group authority to Entra ID, removing AD DS groups no longer needed, and using security group provisioning back to AD DS when an on-premises group must remain. The architecture material also calls out applications that depend on LDAP access to AD. Other actionable edits clarify named-location handling of unmapped IPs, disabled Conditional Access policy cleanup, and soft versus hard deletion recovery. The two External ID entries contain only tip markers, so no specific External ID capability change can be established.
2025-10-07.adminImpact: Administrators working on AD DS minimization or SOA conversion should validate which groups are cloud-authoritative, which must continue to exist on-premises, and which applications bind to AD over LDAP before changing designs. For Conditional Access, review named locations if unknown-country IPs should be covered, and delete disabled policies only after confirming they are no longer needed. Keep recovery procedures aligned with the soft/hard-deletion distinction. These are evidence-backed review and hygiene actions; do not infer a tenant-wide rollout or new default from this documentation-only period.

keyChanges.title: Source of Authority guidance details the cloud-to-AD DS group-management pattern
keyChanges.detail: An updated Entra ID Source of Authority overview says converting Group SOA to Microsoft Entra ID lets administrators manage groups in the cloud and delete AD DS groups that are no longer needed. This is updated architecture guidance, not evidence of a new availability event or changed tenant behavior.

keyChanges.title: SOA architecture guidance highlights LDAP dependencies

keyChanges.title: Named-location guidance clarifies treatment of IPs with unknown geography
keyChanges.detail: Entra ID assignment and network guidance says IPs that cannot be mapped to a specific country or region can be captured in a geographic named location by selecting Include unknown countries/regions. keyChanges.title: Conditional Access planning reiterates removal of obsolete disabled policies

keyChanges.title: Deletion-recovery guidance separates soft and hard deletion paths
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID recovery page explains the distinction between soft and hard deletions and how to recover or recreate objects. 2025-07-15.headline: 15 July: TLS 1.0/1.1 enforcement and risky enterprise-app settings lead a documentation-only day
2025-07-15.overview: All 10 supplied records are Microsoft Learn updates; there are no new or removed items and no Message Center notice. The meaningful content is security and access guidance rather than a feature launch: Entra Domain Services documentation describes disabling TLS 1.0 and 1.1, an Entra ID provisioning page flags a dangerous combination of assignment and provisioning controls, Security Copilot access is clarified for Conditional Access Administrators, and FIDO2 key-vendor validation requirements are made explicit. The other edits are mainly maintenance—metadata, a licensing reference, a network command, a screenshot, and small troubleshooting or author changes.
2025-07-15.adminImpact: Prioritize a compatibility review for Domain Services clients because the evidence points to TLS 1.2 or later but gives no effective date; do not interpret the document update as proof that enforcement happened on 15 July. For enterprise applications, inventory cases where Assignment required is No and provisioning is neither required nor scoped, since the updated guidance identifies that combination as the highest-risk exposure. Review Security Copilot role assignments where Conditional Access Administrators need agent access. The FIDO2 change is primarily vendor and key-selection guidance, not a reported tenant-side setting change; the supplied evidence does not justify an immediate configuration change or a launch or GA claim.

keyChanges.title: Entra Domain Services: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 disablement guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated TLS enforcement page says Microsoft is disabling TLS 1.0 and 1.1, citing the 10 November 2023 communication, and explains that TLS 1.2 or later offers stronger security features such as perfect forward secrecy and stronger cipher suites. The supplied change is documentation evidence and does not state an effective date.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise application provisioning guidance flags a high-risk access combination
keyChanges.detail: The updated provisioning guidance identifies the highest risk when Assignment required is No and provisioning is not required or scoped. It says a compromised user account could then gain immediate access to applications with broad user bases, increasing exposure and possible lateral movement. This is a security warning about configuration posture, not a reported enforcement change.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot access model clarified for Conditional Access Administrators
keyChanges.detail: The Agent Optimization update states that Security Administrator and Global Administrator roles have Security Copilot access by default, while Conditional Access Administrators can be assigned access. It clarifies who may use the agent; the record does not say that this was a new feature, preview, or automatic role change on 15 July.

keyChanges.title: Passkey and FIDO2 documentation clarifies vendor validation prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Enable Passkey Fido2 update says metadata for FIDO2 security keys must be published and verified through the FIDO Alliance Metadata Service and must also pass Microsoft validation testing. The evidence points to Microsoft-compatible key-vendor requirements, not a new tenant configuration or passkey availability change.

2025-07-13.headline: Quiet day: Entra ID licensing reference updated with service-plan mappings
2025-07-13.overview: The only reported change on 13 July 2025 was an update to the Microsoft Entra ID Licensing Service Plan Reference. It updates the list of included service plans and their corresponding friendly names, string IDs, and GUIDs. The evidence describes documentation maintenance, not a new feature, preview, general availability release, retirement, or service-behavior change.
2025-07-13.adminImpact: No direct tenant configuration or security action is established. Administrators who use service-plan names, string IDs, or GUIDs for licensing review or inventory should consult the updated reference; otherwise, this is a routine documentation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Licensing Service Plan Reference updated
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID reference now documents the friendly names of included service plans alongside the corresponding string IDs and GUIDs, helping administrators correlate the human-readable plan names with their identifiers.

2025-07-12.headline: Entra Domain Services TLS 1.0/1.1 disablement is the key change; the remaining updates mainly clarify operations and documentation.
2025-07-12.overview: The supplied 12 July changes contain no evidence of a new feature, preview, or general-availability announcement. The substantive security change is updated Entra Domain Services guidance describing the disabling of TLS 1.0 and 1.1 in favor of TLS 1.2 or later. Other useful edits clarify Global Secure Access connector-group behavior, Connect SSO client support, and Microsoft Graph-based recoverability. The LinkedIn Employment Verification item is a removed documentation page, not evidence by itself that the underlying Verified ID capability was retired.
2025-07-12.adminImpact: Review Entra Domain Services dependencies for continued use of TLS 1.0 or 1.1; the supplied evidence does not provide an effective date. For Global Secure Access, ensure connector-group designs account for the multiple-connector requirement and Default-group placement. Use the Connect SSO and recoverability updates to validate supported clients and recovery procedures, while treating the Verified ID item as a documentation removal unless separate evidence confirms a service retirement.

keyChanges.title: Entra Domain Services guidance describes TLS 1.0 and 1.1 disablement
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra Domain Services security guidance says Microsoft is disabling TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 and identifies TLS 1.2 or later as the required stronger protocol baseline. This is the period’s clearest enforcement and security-related change; administrators should identify integrations that still depend on the older protocols.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documents connector-group placement and prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The updated connector-groups guidance states that groups require multiple connectors and that newly installed connectors are automatically placed in the Default group. This is an operational behavior clarification: administrators using custom groups should account for that initial placement when organizing connectors.

keyChanges.title: Connect SSO support scope is clarified
keyChanges.detail: The Connect SSO update specifies support for web browser-based clients and Office clients that support modern authentication, on platforms and browsers capable of Kerberos authentication. Use this scope when validating client and browser combinations for an SSO rollout; the evidence does not describe a newly launched capability.

keyChanges.title: Recoverability guidance points to Microsoft Graph exports
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID recoverability overview states that Microsoft Graph APIs can export the current state of many Microsoft Entra configurations. This is recovery-planning guidance rather than evidence of a new backup service, and it does not establish that every configuration is exportable.

keyChanges.title: LinkedIn Employment Verification documentation was removed
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Entra Verified ID page titled LinkedIn Employment Verification was removed. The supplied record does not say whether the underlying capability changed, so administrators should not infer a service retirement from the documentation removal alone.

2025-07-11.headline: Documentation, not rollout: Conditional Access agent guidance and a one-way Graph-sync caveat lead 11 July
2025-07-11.overview: The 11 July 2025 record contains 130 updates and no new, removed, or Message Center entries. The most consequential material is specific documentation guidance: administrators are told to review Conditional Access optimization-agent suggestions, the Connect Microsoft Graph page clarifies UPN synchronization and an irreversible enablement constraint, and updated Entra ID pages cover consent follow-up and hardware OATH-token operations. Nothing supplied establishes a new feature, preview, general-availability milestone, retirement, or service-side behavior change; the remaining examples are largely role-reference or other low-detail maintenance updates.
2025-07-11.adminImpact: Treat the day as targeted documentation review, not a tenant-wide rollout. Before enabling the feature described in Connect Microsoft Graph, validate the delayed UPN-update sequence and the fact that it cannot be disabled. When using the Conditional Access optimization agent, review each suggestion and decide whether to apply it. If the tenant restricts user consent, use the documented follow-up steps; if hardware OATH tokens are in scope, consult the Microsoft Graph operations guidance. No broader action is supported by the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access optimization-agent guidance makes the administrator decision point explicit
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID how-to says suggestions vary with what the agent finds and that the administrator must review them and decide what to do. A related Security Copilot page describes the agent as recommending policies and changes aligned with Zero Trust to help protect users and applications. Because both records are documentation updates, they should not be read as evidence of a new launch, preview, or availability change.

keyChanges.title: Connect Microsoft Graph guidance clarifies delayed UPN updates and one-way enablement
keyChanges.detail: The page says existing userPrincipalName values remain unchanged when the documented feature is enabled; a later on-premises change to userPrincipalName causes normal delta sync to update the UPN. It also states that the feature cannot be disabled after enablement. This is a behavior clarification with a concrete rollout-planning consequence, not a reported service change.

keyChanges.title: Consent guidance addresses the security work after restricting user consent
keyChanges.detail: The updated Manage Consent Requests guidance calls for follow-up steps after disabling or restricting user consent: keep business-critical applications usable, limit impact on support and IT administrators, and help prevent unmanaged accounts in non-Microsoft applications. This is security and operational guidance; the record does not indicate that the consent setting itself changed.

keyChanges.title: Hardware OATH-token documentation catalogs Microsoft Graph lifecycle operations
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID topic covers hardware OATH tokens and identifies Microsoft Graph APIs to upload, activate, and assign them. That is a useful reference clarification for token administrators, but the supplied evidence does not claim a new API, changed availability, or a required tenant configuration change.

2025-07-10.headline: 10 July 2025: Conditional Access agent guidance, MFA defaults and B2B controls clarified
2025-07-10.overview: This was a documentation-update day rather than a feature-release day: all 30 supplied changes were marked Updated, with no New or Removed entries. The most consequential updates clarify the approval boundary for the Conditional Access optimization agent, document system-preferred MFA as enabled and Microsoft-managed by default, provide device code flow blocking guidance, explain B2B domain-block behavior, and record the default for recommendation emails. The evidence does not establish a general-availability launch or retirement. An updated Global Secure Access integration page is labeled preview, but its supplied summary provides no substantive capability or availability change.
2025-07-10.adminImpact: Treat the period primarily as a review of current guidance and documented defaults, not as evidence that a new tenant-wide feature was deployed. Validate how administrators review Conditional Access optimization suggestions; assess device code flow blocking if the organization has no established use; account for the documented MFA and recommendation-email defaults; and verify that B2B domain and cross-tenant settings produce the intended treatment of new versus existing guests.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access optimization agent guidance makes the approval gate explicit
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID guidance says the agent's suggestions depend on its findings, but administrators must review the suggestions and decide what to do. No changes are made without administrator approval. This is a workflow and control clarification, not evidence of an automatic Conditional Access policy rollout.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred MFA is documented as Microsoft-managed and enabled by default
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID guidance states that system-preferred MFA is, by default, Microsoft managed and enabled for all users. Administrators evaluating MFA behavior should treat this as the documented baseline; the evidence does not show that the setting was newly enabled in tenants on 10 July.

keyChanges.title: Device code flow receives targeted Conditional Access blocking guidance
keyChanges.detail: For organizations with no established use of device code flow, the updated authentication guidance provides a Conditional Access policy that can block the flow. This is security guidance for a defined scenario, not evidence of a mandatory tenant-wide policy change.

keyChanges.title: B2B domain blocking stops new invitations but not existing guests
keyChanges.detail: The updated External ID explanation clarifies that if cross-tenant access settings allow collaboration with Fabrikam while external collaboration settings block fabrikam.com, users cannot invite new Fabrikam business guests, but existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration. Administrators need to evaluate both controls when reviewing the intended boundary.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra recommendation emails are documented as enabled by default
keyChanges.detail: The updated monitoring guidance states that tenants are opted in by default to receive Microsoft Entra recommendation emails and provides steps to turn them off. This is a notification-setting clarification; administrators can compare the documented default with their operational preferences.

2025-07-09.headline: Microsoft Authenticator changes iOS backup in September; 9 July is otherwise a documentation-heavy Entra update
2025-07-09.overview: The period's one explicit service-behavior change is MC1111780: starting in September 2025, Microsoft Authenticator on iOS will use iCloud and iCloud Keychain for backup and restore, removing the need for a Microsoft personal account. Account names and third-party TOTP credentials will be backed up automatically, and no admin action is required. The other 52 tracked items were documentation updates across Entra products and related capabilities, with no new or removed items. The supplied evidence supports deprecation, preview, and documentation-clarification guidance—not a broad new-feature or general-availability announcement.
2025-07-09.adminImpact: No tenant configuration or rollout action is required for the Authenticator change. App owners should review the updated Azure AD Graph-format app-manifest deprecation guidance and attribute differences when assessing migration or tooling impact; the supplied record gives no retirement date. Teams evaluating Global Secure Access should treat Advanced Threat Protection and Data Loss Prevention as preview, Netskope-powered guidance rather than evidence of general availability. Administrators using the Conditional Access optimization agent can use the documented 30-day discovery summary and Security Compute Unit consumption details for monitoring.

keyChanges.title: Changed behavior — Microsoft Authenticator backup and restore on iOS
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Message Center says that, starting in September 2025, Authenticator on iOS will use iCloud and iCloud Keychain for backup and restore. The update eliminates the need for a Microsoft personal account and automatically backs up account names and third-party TOTP credentials. The notice explicitly says no admin action is required.

keyChanges.title: Deprecation guidance — Azure AD Graph-format app manifests
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Entra ID article describes the deprecation of the Azure AD Graph-format app manifest and the attribute differences in the newer format. This is migration guidance, not evidence that the format was retired on 9 July; application owners should use it to assess manifest conversions and dependent tooling.

keyChanges.title: Preview documentation — Global Secure Access Advanced Threat Protection and DLP
keyChanges.detail: The updated Global Secure Access page covers Advanced Threat Protection and Data Loss Prevention policies powered by Netskope. Because the capability is explicitly labeled Preview, this record supports preview guidance rather than a general-availability or rollout claim.

keyChanges.title: Documentation clarification — Conditional Access optimization-agent metrics
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID documentation explains that the Conditional Access optimization agent's summary shows discoveries from the last 30 days and reports the agent's Security Compute Unit consumption. This adds operational monitoring detail without evidence of a newly launched agent or changed tenant policy.

2025-07-08.headline: Entra ID certificate-based authentication documentation updated for PKI container object creation
2025-07-08.overview: The 8 July 2025 period was quiet: the supplied evidence shows one Microsoft Learn update for Entra ID. The change is confined to guidance headed “To create a PKI container object:” and does not establish a new feature, availability change, retirement, or altered authentication behavior.
2025-07-08.adminImpact: Administrators using or planning Entra ID Certificate Based Authentication should review the revised PKI container object creation instructions and assess whether they affect tenant configuration, security posture, or rollout plans. No mandatory action or product behavior change is evidenced.

keyChanges.title: PKI container object creation guidance revised
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Certificate Based Authentication documentation was updated in the section covering how to create a PKI container object. The record supports a documentation change only; it does not specify a new capability or a change to the underlying authentication workflow.

2025-07-05.headline: Permissions Management offboarding guidance signals an anticipated deprecation; Security Copilot expands Conditional Access optimization-agent guidance
2025-07-05.overview: 5 July was primarily a documentation-led period: 75 changes included two new pages and 73 updates, with no removals. The consequential changes were new Security Copilot guidance for reviewing optimization-agent suggestions and monitoring its metrics and audit events, updated guidance stating a Microsoft Entra ID P1 licensing prerequisite, and an explicit Microsoft Entra Permissions Management offboarding signal. A separate Entra ID update clarifies the Azure role-assignment requirement for sign-in to Azure virtual machines and Arc-connected Windows Server. The supplied evidence does not establish a preview, general availability release, or deprecation deadline.
2025-07-05.adminImpact: Organizations using Microsoft Entra Permissions Management should review the offboarding guidance and begin transition planning, while recognizing that no deadline is provided. Teams evaluating the Conditional Access optimization agent should confirm P1 licensing, understand how suggestions are reviewed and applied, and identify the relevant audit-log monitoring. Administrators supporting Entra sign-in to Azure VMs or Arc-connected Windows Server should verify the required Azure role assignments. These updates support review and planning; they do not, by themselves, announce a new GA feature or a changed platform requirement.

keyChanges.title: Updated offboarding guidance flags an anticipated Microsoft Entra Permissions Management deprecation
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains how to transition off Microsoft Entra Permissions Management for an anticipated product deprecation. This is the clearest retirement signal in the period, but no retirement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: New Security Copilot guidance covers Conditional Access optimization-agent suggestions
keyChanges.detail: A new page explains how to review and apply suggestions from the Security Copilot for Microsoft Entra optimization agent. It documents an administrator workflow; the page is not evidence of a preview or GA launch.

keyChanges.title: New documentation describes optimization-agent metrics and audit events
keyChanges.detail: A second new Security Copilot page documents the optimization agent's metrics and events in audit logs, giving administrators guidance for observing agent activity. The supplied evidence does not state that the audit schema or availability changed.

keyChanges.title: Updated optimization-agent guidance states a Microsoft Entra ID P1 minimum
keyChanges.detail: The updated Agent Optimization Review Suggestions guidance states that at least a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license is required. This is presented as a documented prerequisite; the evidence does not establish whether the underlying licensing rule changed on this date.

keyChanges.title: Entra sign-in guidance clarifies Azure role assignments for VM and Arc server access
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance states that a Microsoft Entra user must have an Azure role assignment before signing in to an Azure virtual machine or Arc-connected Windows Server, and that the same roles apply to both. This is a documentation clarification rather than evidence of a newly introduced platform behavior.

2025-07-04.headline: Microsoft Entra sign-in background scheduled for a visual refresh; authentication-flow and B2B security guidance were clarified
2025-07-04.overview: 4 July was documentation-heavy: 16 Microsoft Learn articles were updated, with no new or removed items recorded, alongside one Message Center notice. The clearest operational change is a planned visual update to the Work or School sign-in experience. The most substantive documentation updates clarify protocol-tracked authentication sessions, reinforce tenant-restriction guidance for external accounts, and describe the Conditional Access optimization agent. The supplied evidence does not identify a preview, general availability launch, or retirement.
2025-07-04.adminImpact: No tenant configuration change is required for the sign-in background update, but Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation and help-desk guidance before the late-September-to-early-October rollout. Administrators reviewing authentication-flow policies should account for protocol tracking, and those assessing external collaboration should consider the updated tenant-restriction guidance. The agent documentation does not provide evidence of a new release status or require a rollout action.

keyChanges.title: Work or School sign-in background will receive a visual update
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is updating the default sign-in background for Work or School accounts to align with Microsoft’s Fluent design language. The rollout is stated to run from late September to early October 2025. This is a user-interface change rather than a new authentication capability; no action is required, although internal documentation and help-desk materials should be updated to reduce confusion.

keyChanges.title: Protocol tracking clarifies authentication-flow policy enforcement
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID Authentication Flows guidance explains that sessions using device code flow or authentication transfer are marked as protocol tracked, that this state persists through subsequent refreshes, and that later flows that are not themselves device-code or authentication-transfer flows can still be subject to authentication-flow policies. This is a documentation clarification of enforcement behavior, not evidence of a newly released policy feature.

keyChanges.title: B2B guidance reinforces tenant restrictions for external accounts
keyChanges.detail: Updated Microsoft Entra External ID guidance says tenant restrictions can prevent users from using accounts created in unknown tenants or accounts received from external organizations. It recommends disallowing those accounts and using B2B collaboration instead. This is security guidance for reviewing external-account controls, not a reported product launch or tenant-wide policy change.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access optimization agent is documented without a stated release status
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID Agent Optimization article describes a Conditional Access optimization agent that recommends policies and changes based on best practices aligned with Zero Trust and Microsoft’s experience. The supplied evidence identifies an updated article only; it does not establish that the capability is new, in preview, or generally available.

2025-07-03.headline: 3 July 2025: Agent ID MFA-policy guidance and Microsoft.Identity.Client deprecation notes lead a documentation-heavy Entra update
2025-07-03.overview: All 125 reported items were updates; none were new or removed, and there were no Message Center entries. The most consequential content is in existing guidance: Agent ID’s Agent Optimization page describes finding users outside MFA-requiring Conditional Access coverage and updating the policy, while Entra ID guidance calls out required application changes around Microsoft.Identity.Client and a public-client API deprecated as of release 4.73.1. Other specific updates clarify ROPC flow behavior, Verified ID policy matching, and External ID logout semantics. The supplied evidence contains no preview or general-availability announcement, retirement, or tenant-wide behavior change; many remaining representative updates are generic built-in-role reference-page refreshes.
2025-07-03.adminImpact: Treat this as a targeted documentation and configuration review rather than a broad tenant rollout. Application owners using Microsoft.Identity.Client should identify use of the affected APIs and assess the required code changes. Administrators evaluating Agent Optimization should review the Conditional Access policies it may update. Verify Verified ID policies that combine issuers or credential types, since the documented matching behavior is all-of rather than any-of, and check External ID relying-party logout expectations against browser-session invalidation. For ROPC applications, account for the documented direct password handling and silent, no-UI token acquisition. The evidence does not support a tenant-wide MFA configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID: MFA coverage and Conditional Access policy updates documented
keyChanges.detail: Classification: documentation describing an agent workflow, not a reported launch. The updated Agent Optimization page says the agent identifies users who are not covered by a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA and can update that policy. Tenants considering the workflow should review the target policies and expected MFA coverage before applying it; the item does not report an automatic tenant change.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID: Microsoft.Identity.Client application changes and public-client deprecation called out
keyChanges.detail: Classification: application compatibility and deprecation guidance. The updated Mandatory Multifactor Authentication page says changes are required when an application uses the Microsoft.Identity.Client package with one of the affected APIs, and identifies the public client API as deprecated as of the 4.73.1 release. This is application-maintenance guidance, not evidence of a tenant-side MFA policy change.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID: ROPC and username/password flow behavior clarified
keyChanges.detail: Classification: protocol-behavior documentation clarification. The updated MSAL Authentication Flows page describes the OAuth 2.0 resource owner password credentials grant as an application directly handling the user’s password, and says a desktop application can acquire a token silently through the username/password flow without UI. The update does not state that ROPC was newly introduced, recommended, or retired.

keyChanges.title: ID Governance: Verified ID credential and issuer selection is conjunctive
keyChanges.detail: Classification: policy-semantics clarification. Selecting multiple credential types from one issuer requires users to present all selected types; selecting multiple issuers requires credentials from each included issuer. The documented way to offer alternatives is to configure separate policies for each issuer or credential type.

keyChanges.title: External ID: browser-session invalidation documented for SAML and OpenID Connect sign-out
keyChanges.detail: Classification: supported-behavior clarification. The updated supported-features information states that when a SAML or OpenID Connect application directs a user to the logout endpoint, Microsoft Entra ID removes and invalidates the user’s browser session, matching workforce behavior. No rollout or newly changed service behavior is reported.

2025-07-02.headline: 2 July 2025 was documentation-heavy: explicit Entra DNS redirection guidance led the day, with Conditional Access and troubleshooting clarifications—not a feature rollout.
2025-07-02.overview: All 20 supplied records are Microsoft Learn updates. There are no new or removed records and no Message Center notices. The meaningful edits are guidance and reference changes: the Manage DNS page warns against zone-level redirection for windowsazure.com and core.windows.net; Conditional Access documentation clarifies log interpretation; Graph troubleshooting calls out email-validation sign-up failures; and Global Secure Access documents an application-discovery workflow. The evidence supports no claim of a new feature, preview, general availability, retirement, or changed runtime behavior. The External ID Cloudflare-integration update has no summary, so it cannot support a more specific claim.
2025-07-02.adminImpact: No tenant-wide rollout or mandatory configuration change is evidenced. Administrators handling the DNS scenario should follow the host-level redirection guidance; operators investigating Conditional Access or sign-up issues can use the clarified log meaning and Graph procedure. Global Secure Access administrators should treat the discovery item as usage documentation, not as an availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Manage DNS guidance limits redirection to individual host names
keyChanges.detail: The updated Manage DNS guidance says not to redirect DNS zones related to windowsazure.com or core.windows.net. If redirection is required, it says to limit it to individual host names—for example, server1.file.core.windows.net rather than file.core.windows.net. This is explicit networking guidance, not evidence of a new enforcement mechanism.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access sign-in-log terminology is clarified
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sign In Log Activity Details page defines Success as the Conditional Access policy being applied successfully to the sign-in attempt. This is a documentation clarification for interpreting existing sign-in records; the evidence does not indicate that Conditional Access evaluation changed.

keyChanges.title: Graph activity-log troubleshooting calls out email-validation sign-up failures
keyChanges.detail: The updated How to Analyze Activity Logs with Microsoft Graph guide calls out how to find sign-up attempts that failed during email validation. This provides troubleshooting coverage for a specific failure path, but the record does not indicate changed sign-up behavior or a new rollout.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documents the Application Discovery-to-private-app workflow
keyChanges.detail: The updated Application Discovery for Global Secure Access page says to use Application discovery to detect applications accessed by users and create separate private applications. It documents a capability workflow; the supplied evidence does not establish whether this is new, in preview, or generally available.

2025-07-01.headline: Microsoft Entra Domain Services TLS 1.2 migration is the day’s main operational signal; other updates clarify federation, custom domains, and forest trusts.
2025-07-01.overview: The 1 July record is a documentation-update day: all nine supplied entries are Microsoft Learn updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center announcements. The clearest operational change is security guidance for disabling TLS 1.0 and 1.1 in Microsoft Entra Domain Services; the remaining notable updates clarify configuration, permissions, or existing documentation rather than announce new features, previews, or general availability.
2025-07-01.adminImpact: Prioritize reviewing the Domain Services TLS migration guidance and identifying any dependencies on TLS 1.0 or 1.1; the supplied evidence does not provide a new enforcement date. For Workload ID federation and External ID custom URL domains, apply the documented issuer/subject and administrator-role checks. The forest-trust updates appear to be documentation maintenance, with no specific configuration or behavior change stated.

keyChanges.title: Entra Domain Services guidance points to TLS 1.2-or-later enforcement
keyChanges.detail: This is security guidance for an announced protocol change, not a feature launch. Microsoft describes disabling TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and moving to TLS 1.2 or later, citing stronger cipher suites, perfect forward secrecy, and compliance benefits. Administrators should review Domain Services integrations for legacy TLS dependencies, but no new enforcement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Workload identity federation documentation clarifies managed-identity trust validation
keyChanges.detail: The updated Workload ID guidance explains that the issuer and subject in a federated identity credential are matched against the corresponding claims in the managed identity token. Microsoft identity platform issues an app access token to the external workload only after that validation succeeds. This is a configuration and behavior clarification, not evidence of a newly introduced capability.

keyChanges.title: External ID custom URL domain guidance states the required administrator role
keyChanges.detail: The updated instruction says users must sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Domain Name Administrator. The evidence supports a permissions/documentation clarification, not a change to role definitions or RBAC behavior; administrators should use that role check when delegating custom URL domain work.

keyChanges.title: Forest trust documentation was refreshed across concepts, PowerShell, and tutorial guidance
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft updated the Entra ID pages for forest-trust concepts, PowerShell creation, and the forest-trust tutorial. The supplied summaries identify the affected documentation but do not describe a new feature, changed prerequisite, or changed forest-trust behavior, so this should be treated as documentation maintenance.

2025-06-30.headline: Quiet period: one Entra ID provisioning documentation update
2025-06-30.overview: On 30 June 2025, the supplied evidence records a single update to Microsoft Entra ID’s “What’s New” documentation for the Provisioning service category. It does not identify a new feature, preview, general availability milestone, retirement, or behavior change.
2025-06-30.adminImpact: No specific tenant configuration or rollout action is supported by the evidence. Administrators who rely on Entra provisioning documentation may review the updated page for details, but the supplied summary does not describe a concrete change requiring action.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID provisioning documentation updated
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft updated the Entra ID “What’s New” documentation under Provisioning. The available evidence does not specify which content changed, so this should be treated as a documentation update rather than evidence of a product capability change.

2025-06-29.headline: 29 June: External ID B2B controls, Agent Optimization exceptions, and security guidance were clarified
2025-06-29.overview: The supplied feed is update-only: 89 items were updated, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The strongest changes are documentation clarifications and security or operational guidance—not evidence of a new feature, preview, general-availability release, retirement, or broad behavior change. A large share of the remaining edits concern role and permissions reference pages.
2025-06-29.adminImpact: Treat this as a validation and documentation-review cycle rather than a rollout. External ID administrators should assess cross-tenant access alongside blocked-domain settings and use the documented object limit for planning. Entra ID administrators using Agent Optimization can review its documented exception controls, while security teams can use the legacy-authentication workbook to identify affected applications. The supplied role-page and SSPR updates do not by themselves prove that tenant configuration or effective permissions changed.

keyChanges.title: External ID clarifies cross-tenant access and blocked-domain interaction
keyChanges.detail: The B2B example states that allowing Fabrikam in cross-tenant access settings while blocking fabrikam.com prevents new Fabrikam business-guest invitations, but existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration. This is a documentation clarification of policy interaction, not evidence of newly changed enforcement behavior.

keyChanges.title: External ID service-limits documentation lists 300,000 total objects per tenant
keyChanges.detail: The updated Service Limits page lists 300,000 total user accounts and applications per tenant and directs administrators to Microsoft Support if an increase is needed. The evidence supports a published-limit clarification, not a quota change.

keyChanges.title: Agent Optimization guidance documents optional custom instructions
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Agent Optimization update describes an optional Custom Instructions field that supplies a prompt to the agent. It can be used to include or exclude users, groups, and roles, or to add exceptions to a suggested policy. This is capability guidance in an updated page, not a launch or availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Legacy-authentication workbook guidance supports application discovery
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sign-ins using legacy authentication workbook page explains that the workbook can identify applications using legacy methods. This is security and operational guidance; the supplied evidence does not announce a legacy-authentication retirement or enforcement date.

keyChanges.title: SSPR documentation clarifies the password-expiry default and per-user setting
keyChanges.detail: The SSPR Policy update states that Password expiry, or Let passwords never expire, has a default value of false, meaning passwords have an expiration date, and that the value can be configured for individual accounts with Update-MgUser. This is documentation clarification and does not show that existing accounts were changed.

2025-06-28.headline: Temporary Access Pass prerequisite clarified; RBAC, security, and governance guidance refreshed
2025-06-28.overview: 28 June 2025 was primarily a documentation-maintenance day: all 154 recorded changes were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center announcements. The supplied representative changes are dominated by Entra role and permissions reference edits, alongside a few more substantive clarifications covering Temporary Access Pass enrollment, Insider Risk in Conditional Access, access-package access removal, and sign-in branding. Nothing in the evidence identifies a new preview, general-availability release, retirement, or tenant-wide rollout.
2025-06-28.adminImpact: The clearest operational impact is for hybrid-joined Windows Hello for Business enrollment: update TAP and support runbooks to reflect the prerequisite authentication step. Security and governance teams should review the Insider Risk and access-package guidance where those capabilities are in scope. The branding notice requires no functional or configuration action; only training and documentation images may need refreshing. For RBAC reference edits, confirm whether a listed permission reflects an actual role-definition change before changing assignments.

keyChanges.title: Temporary Access Pass guidance adds a hybrid-join prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The updated Temporary Access Pass guidance states that users on hybrid-joined devices must first authenticate with another method, such as a password, smartcard, or FIDO2 key, before using TAP to set up Windows Hello for Business. This is an operational documentation clarification, not evidence of a new feature or policy rollout. Update enrollment and support procedures that cover this flow.

keyChanges.title: Authentication Administrator scope is clarified in the permissions reference
keyChanges.detail: The updated Permissions Reference states that Authentication Administrator can view, set, and reset authentication-method information for any non-admin user. The supplied record shows a reference-page update, but does not establish that the underlying built-in role permissions or existing assignments changed. Administrators relying on delegated authentication support should verify the current role definition before making access changes.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access guidance documents the Insider Risk integration
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains how to protect a tenant by enabling the Insider Risk condition in Conditional Access integrated with Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection. This is security guidance; the evidence does not identify the capability as a new preview or generally available release. Security teams evaluating this integration should review the updated instructions.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management clarifies access-package assignment removal
