No configuration change is needed for Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO, but onboarding and documentation should be updated. For the preview capabilities, apply the stated Global Secure Access prerequisites and use report-only mode and a pilot for Token Protection. Treat the provisioning-label changes as runbook updates rather than a required migration.

keyChanges.title: `memberOf` auto-assignment support now ends 3 November 2026
keyChanges.detail: Updated ID Governance guidance moves the end date from 27 October to 3 November 2026. Policies that still use the operator will be quarantined and stop processing assignments after the cutoff, making this a retirement deadline rather than a terminology edit.

keyChanges.title: Passkeys can be registered as users’ first MFA method
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says users can register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method, removing the former weaker-method-first requirement. Rollout is phased from January 2026 through November 2027; the supplied notice specifies no administrator configuration action.

keyChanges.title: Windows Hello and macOS Platform SSO become standalone MFA factors
keyChanges.detail: Message Center says Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors starting October 2026, allowing users to meet MFA requirements without additional passkeys. No configuration changes are required, but onboarding and documentation should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access guidance covers its preview MCP firewall
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to article—not a launch announcement—describes using the Global Secure Access MCP firewall to inspect, audit, and allow or block supported Model Context Protocol traffic by server, primitive, method, and protocol version. The documented prerequisites include Global Secure Access and Conditional Access Administrator roles, an Internet Access license, a joined device with the Global Secure Access client, and TLS inspection; the firewall is in preview.

keyChanges.title: Token Protection web-app support is documented as a preview
keyChanges.detail: A new Entra deployment guide covers enforcing Token Protection with Conditional Access for supported browser-based applications accessing Azure Resource Manager. Scope is limited to listed apps, platforms, browsers, and device configurations; the guide requires Entra ID P1 and additional Windows or macOS device setup, and recommends report-only mode followed by a pilot before enforcement.

2026-08-08.headline: Managed policies may enable after 30 days, with high-risk remediation scope clarified
2026-08-08.overview: This quiet Entra ID period contains one material change to Managed Policies guidance and one reference-data correction. The Managed Policies update shortens the documented Report-only review period from 45 to at least 30 days and adds security-group scope information for high-risk remediation. The SLA update is documentation-only; it does not indicate a product or service change.
2026-08-08.adminImpact: Review managed policies sooner because Microsoft may enable them after at least 30 days in Report-only. Administrators can enable them earlier or set them to Off, and should include the newly documented security group when assessing high-risk remediation scope. The SLA change only requires users of the performance reference to use the corrected July value.

keyChanges.title: Managed Policies review window and scope
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Managed Policies page now says Microsoft may enable a managed policy at least 30 days after introduction when it remains in Report-only, replacing the previously documented 45-day period. It also documents creation of a security group with the high-risk remediation policy.

keyChanges.title: July SLA performance data corrected
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID SLA Performance table now includes an additional 99.999% value in the July row. The source explicitly indicates that this is a reference update, not a product change.

2026-08-09.headline: Hard-match remediation guidance now explicitly requires resetting the protection flag
2026-08-09.overview: A troubleshooting update for Microsoft Entra ID clarifies the commands used to enable and verify `AllowOnPremUpdateOfOnPremisesObjectIdentifierEnabled`. It also documents restoring the setting to `$false` after remediation, so hard-match protection is re-enabled. This is a procedural documentation clarification, not evidence of a new feature or changed service behavior.
2026-08-09.adminImpact: Administrators following the remediation procedure should use the revised commands, verify the flag’s value, and set it back to `$false` when remediation is complete.

keyChanges.title: Revised Microsoft Graph troubleshooting commands clarify hard-match remediation
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID guidance shows clearer commands for enabling and verifying `AllowOnPremUpdateOfOnPremisesObjectIdentifierEnabled`, and explicitly includes the step to restore it to `$false` after remediation.

2026-08-10.headline: Token Protection now documents Preview browser support for selected Azure Resource Manager web apps
2026-08-10.overview: The period was dominated by Entra ID documentation updates. The meaningful change is expanded Token Protection guidance covering browser-based applications in Preview; the other updates revise Orgvue URL examples and remove a Conditional Access screenshot without indicating product-behavior changes.
2026-08-10.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating browser-based Token Protection should review the Web Apps deployment guide, supported browser, extension, operating-system, and configuration requirements, and note that Conditional Access enforcement uses the Windows Azure Service Management API resource. Orgvue administrators should update tutorial-based URL values as described.

keyChanges.title: Browser-based Token Protection guidance expands
keyChanges.detail: The Token Protection page now documents browser-based application support in Preview for selected web apps accessing Azure Resource Manager on Windows and macOS. Browser support on iOS and iPadOS is not supported. The update adds requirements for supported browsers, extensions, operating systems, and configurations, and identifies the Conditional Access resource used for enforcement.

keyChanges.title: Orgvue tutorial URLs and placeholders are revised
keyChanges.detail: The tutorial replaces authentication and SAML callback URLs with orgvue-staging URLs, changes the Sign-on URL to include the application login path and domain parameter, and clarifies that Reply URL and Sign-on URL values are placeholders. Administrators using the tutorial should substitute the actual domain and correct application URLs.

keyChanges.title: Token Protection policy screenshot removed
keyChanges.detail: A screenshot showing a Conditional Access policy requiring Token Protection as a session control was removed. The Primary Refresh Token link remains. This is a presentation-only documentation change, with no administrator action or product-behavior change indicated.

2026-08-11.headline: First-method passkey registration rolls out from October 2026 through February 2027
2026-08-11.overview: The period’s consequential item is a Microsoft Entra rollout announcement: users will be able to register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method, without setting up weaker methods first. The remaining changes are documentation clarifications covering Agent ID token exchange, a Microsoft Graph permission prerequisite, account discovery limits, workload identity guidance links, and PAC-file syntax. No new or removed documentation items are recorded, and the evidence does not establish a separate preview, general-availability, or retirement event.
2026-08-11.adminImpact: The first-method registration rollout requires no administrator action according to the Message Center notice. Administrators implementing Agent ID on-behalf-of flows should preauthorize delegated permissions through inheritable blueprint permissions and use the documented token audiences. Administrators using Microsoft Graph to opt out of the authentication-method policy should ensure requests have Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod; account discovery and PAC-file updates require review only where those configurations are in use.

keyChanges.title: First-method passkey and passwordless registration is scheduled to roll out
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center announcement says users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method, eliminating the need to configure weaker methods first. Rollout is stated for October 2026 through February 2027, with no administrator action required.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID guidance clarifies audiences and the preauthorization requirement
keyChanges.detail: Updated Agent ID on-behalf-of guidance says Tc must target the agent identity blueprint, while T1 targets the token-exchange resource and is validated against the blueprint and child agent identity. It also clarifies that agent identities cannot use interactive consent and that delegated permissions must be preauthorized through inheritable blueprint permissions. This is a documentation clarification with concrete configuration implications.

keyChanges.title: Graph opt-out guidance now names the required authentication-method permission
keyChanges.detail: The passkey and Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication page now states that opting out through Microsoft Graph requires Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod. The supplied evidence supports this as a documentation prerequisite clarification, not a new retirement date or separately documented API behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Account discovery documentation tightens prerequisites and limitation wording
keyChanges.detail: The account discovery article now uses lowercase “account discovery” and clarifies connector requirements, direct attribute matching, SCIM support, unsupported scenarios, the GitHub reference, and the expectation that reports take at least 30 minutes. It continues to describe the existing process; no launch or required action is indicated.

2026-08-12.headline: External ID on-behalf-of ordering targets Dynamics 365 Commerce general availability on 11 September 2026
2026-08-12.overview: The clearest product announcement is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice that on-behalf-of ordering for Dynamics 365 Commerce with Microsoft Entra External ID is scheduled for general availability on 11 September 2026. A new Microsoft Entra Internet Access article documents the V2 web-filtering model and its coexistence with V1. Most other updates are documentation clarifications or connector setup changes, including sharper Staged Rollout troubleshooting and more explicit application-claim configuration.
2026-08-12.adminImpact: Commerce administrators should note the announced availability date; the supplied notice includes no additional setup or migration steps. Internet Access administrators should understand the V2 policy and rule model before using it. Administrators troubleshooting Staged Rollout transitions should account for possible additional sign-ins, while those configuring granular AMR values must use the application manifest or Microsoft Graph for SAML. Puzzel provisioning configurations now require the documented OAuth2 client-credentials inputs.

keyChanges.title: On-behalf-of ordering gets a scheduled External ID availability milestone
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announces that on-behalf-of ordering for Microsoft Entra External ID in Dynamics 365 Commerce will reach general availability on 11 September 2026. This is a product availability announcement; the supplied notice does not provide further configuration or migration guidance.

keyChanges.title: V2 web filtering is documented as a distinct Internet Access model
keyChanges.detail: The new Global Secure Access V2 article describes one policy per security profile, multiple rules with individual actions, a default action, and URL-based FQDN destinations. Existing V1 web-content-filtering policies continue to function until migration. The new article documents the model but does not by itself establish a separate availability milestone.

keyChanges.title: Staged Rollout guidance now details additional sign-in scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Entra Connect article replaces general transition language with scenarios involving extra interactive sign-ins when users are added to or removed from Staged Rollout, including certain Microsoft Entra ID Protection remediation events such as SSPR and risk remediation. The supported administrator outcome is better troubleshooting guidance, not evidence of a newly changed sign-in behavior.

keyChanges.title: Optional Claims guidance clarifies granular AMR configuration paths
keyChanges.detail: The updated article explains that SAML applications must configure the `include_granular_amr` setting through the application manifest or Microsoft Graph because the admin center has no corresponding UI. It also documents adding the `amr` optional claim for OIDC token types and clarifies that `include_granular_amr` applies only to SAML.

keyChanges.title: Puzzel provisioning adds OAuth2 client-credentials instructions
keyChanges.detail: The Puzzel integration guide now covers OAuth2 Client Credentials Grant authentication, including creating an OIDC client, setting 3600-second token lifetimes, generating a shared secret, and entering the client ID, secret, and token endpoint. This is connector-specific setup guidance rather than a new general provisioning capability.

2026-08-13.headline: Entra ID Free SMS first-factor sign-in retirement makes alternate authentication necessary
2026-08-13.overview: The period’s main administrator-impacting notice is Microsoft’s planned retirement of SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants on 11 August 2026 because of fraud risks; SMS used for multifactor authentication remains unaffected. Microsoft also added first-party Workload ID federation tutorials for Google Cloud and SPIFFE/SPIRE, expanded Agent ID permission guidance, and revised Catalog Access Reviews documentation. Most remaining edits were maintenance, including a corrected Global Secure Access section name and updated links.
2026-08-13.adminImpact: Admins should identify users dependent on SMS first-factor sign-in and move them to other authentication methods, while leaving SMS multifactor use unchanged. For Catalog Access Reviews, account for the warning that changes made within 12 hours before a review starts may not appear; removing Preview labels from the documentation is not, by itself, an explicit general availability announcement. The new Workload ID pages support secretless federation scenarios but are tutorials rather than evidence of a product launch. Agent ID administrators can use the new channel-by-channel permissions table, while the Global Secure Access edit requires only using the corrected section name.

keyChanges.title: SMS first-factor sign-in retirement for Entra ID Free tenants
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says Microsoft will retire SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants on 11 August 2026 because of fraud risks. Users must switch to another authentication method before retirement; SMS as a multifactor method is unaffected. This is a security-related product retirement, not a documentation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Catalog Access Reviews documentation adds a 12-hour data-freshness caveat
keyChanges.detail: Updated ID Governance guidance removes Preview labels, broadens reviewer terminology beyond managers, and warns that changes made within 12 hours before a review starts may not appear. The supplied evidence does not explicitly announce general availability, so the status change should not be treated as a confirmed GA announcement.

keyChanges.title: Google Cloud workload federation gets a first-party Workload ID tutorial
keyChanges.detail: A new tutorial shows how an Entra application can trust a Google-issued service-account token, exchange it for an Entra access token, and access Azure resources without storing application secrets. It documents a configuration scenario rather than announcing a new product launch and requires permission to add a federated identity credential.

keyChanges.title: SPIFFE/SPIRE workload federation gets a first-party Workload ID tutorial
keyChanges.detail: A new tutorial documents exchanging a Kubernetes workload’s SPIFFE JWT-SVID for a Microsoft Entra access token so it can access Azure resources without stored secrets. The page is implementation guidance for an existing federation scenario, not evidence of a new product launch.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID guidance maps Microsoft 365 channels to required permissions
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance now covers agents communicating through Outlook email, OneDrive and SharePoint comments, Teams chats, and Teams channels, with permissions for receiving events and sending responses. Administrators can use the channel-by-channel table to configure agent access; no underlying product behavior change is stated.

2026-08-14.headline: Agent ID guidance now directs provisioning through identity blueprints, not app registrations
2026-08-14.overview: 14 August produced no new or removed entries and was dominated by documentation maintenance, particularly across Microsoft Entra Agent ID. The most consequential update clarifies that agents should use identity blueprints and the #Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity object rather than standard application-registration APIs. Other notable edits clarify Identity Protection remediation, dynamic-group treatment of agent accounts, replica-set networking, and a Windows passkey preview label; none of the supplied diffs independently announces a new feature or general availability.
2026-08-14.adminImpact: Review Agent ID provisioning runbooks and automation against the blueprint-based creation model and its supported channels, roles, and permissions. Do not use standard application-registration APIs for agents. Add explicit dynamic-group conditions if agent accounts must be included or excluded, and verify fully meshed connectivity across virtual networks hosting replica sets. Use the updated Identity Protection terminology when assessing remediation, while treating the Windows passkey label removal as insufficient evidence of general availability.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID provisioning guidance moves to identity blueprints
keyChanges.detail: The architecture guidance now directs administrators to create agents from an agent identity blueprint and the #Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity object, rather than through standard application-registration APIs. It also documents supported creation channels, roles, permissions, and .NET usage. This is a guidance clarification, not a separately announced launch.

keyChanges.title: Identity Protection clarifies the attacker-added-device response
keyChanges.detail: The Identity Protection Policies article replaces “Device disablement” with “Attacker-added device” and spells out the documented response: the Entra device object is disabled, new token issuance is blocked, device-bound refresh tokens are revoked, and user sessions are revoked. The supplied change clarifies the remediation scope rather than announcing a new control.

keyChanges.title: Dynamic-group guidance now covers agent user accounts
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID guidance now explains that agent user accounts are evaluated by user-based membership rules and are not distinguished from other users by default. Administrators can explicitly include or exclude them, including accounts associated with a particular agent identity blueprint.

keyChanges.title: Replica-set guidance makes full virtual-network meshing explicit
keyChanges.detail: The replica-set documentation now states that all virtual networks hosting replica sets must be connected. It also specifies that replica sets are deployed in one Active Directory site and depend on a fully meshed virtual-network topology, clarifying a deployment prerequisite.

keyChanges.title: Windows passkey registration loses its preview label
keyChanges.detail: The “Register a Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows” page no longer includes “(preview)” in its title or heading. No procedural change is shown, and the supplied diff does not explicitly announce general availability or a product launch.

2026-08-15.headline: Global Secure Access guidance details guided V1-to-V2 web filtering migration
2026-08-15.overview: The main substantive addition is a new Global Secure Access how-to for migrating eligible web content filtering policies from V1 to V2. The existing Web Filtering page now links to that guidance. Separate Entra ID and ID Protection updates clarify documented limitations and remediation behavior rather than announcing new features.
2026-08-15.adminImpact: Global Secure Access administrators should verify migration eligibility, account for changed evaluation across multiple security profiles, and manually handle profiles that already contain V2 policies. For external users signing in with Microsoft personal accounts, review authentication-strength policies and use the MFA grant control where required. Update Identity Protection runbooks to match the revised device-block description; the evidence does not establish a product-behavior change.

keyChanges.title: New guidance maps V1 web filtering policies into V2 rules
keyChanges.detail: The Global Secure Access migration guide covers eligible and ineligible security profiles, naming, and the guided migration process. Each V1 policy becomes a rule in one enabled V2 policy while preserving destinations, actions, and priorities. Profiles that already contain V2 policies require manual handling, and evaluation across multiple security profiles differs between V1 and V2.

keyChanges.title: Authentication-strength guidance excludes MSA-authenticated external users
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID guidance states that authentication-strength policies cannot currently be applied to external users authenticating through Microsoft personal (MSA) accounts. It directs administrators to use the MFA grant control instead. This documents a limitation and alternative control; it does not establish a newly introduced product behavior.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection revises the documented device-block remediation behavior
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says disabling the Entra device blocks new token issuance, revokes user sessions, and prompts the user to sign in again. It no longer mentions revoking existing device-bound refresh tokens, making this a documentation clarification rather than evidence of a behavior change.

2026-08-18.headline: Federated sign-in validation tightens as Windows Hello and macOS SSO gain standalone MFA
2026-08-18.overview: The day’s consequential changes are two Entra authentication behavior updates. Microsoft says the federatedTokenValidationPolicy default will block federated sign-ins when internalDomainFederation does not match the user’s UPN domain for federated domains configured before December 2025. Starting in October 2026, Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO will count as standalone MFA factors. Workload ID’s flexible federated identity credential preview guidance also tightens GitHub claim matching, while the remaining updates are lower-impact synchronization and licensing reference maintenance.
2026-08-18.adminImpact: Review federated domains configured before December 2025 against the new internalDomainFederation and UPN-domain matching condition; Microsoft Graph customization is available but discouraged. No configuration change is required for Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO, but onboarding and MFA-registration guidance should be updated. For GitHub flexible FICs, match sub plus repository_id or repository_owner_id as documented, using eq for the supported immutable claims. Review the synchronization guidance only when sAMAccountName synchronization with Microsoft Entra Domain Services is in scope, and use the updated licensing reference when matching the affected Windows 365 plans.

keyChanges.title: FederatedTokenValidationPolicy default will block mismatched federated domains
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s Message Center notice describes a mid-August 2026 default change affecting federated domains configured before December 2025. Federated sign-ins will be blocked when internalDomainFederation does not match the user’s UPN domain. Administrators can customize the policy through Microsoft Graph, although Microsoft discourages customization.

keyChanges.title: Windows Hello and macOS Platform SSO become standalone MFA factors
keyChanges.detail: Starting in October 2026, Microsoft Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors, allowing users to satisfy MFA requirements without an additional passkey. Microsoft says no configuration changes are required, but onboarding and MFA-registration guidance should be updated.

keyChanges.title: GitHub flexible FIC preview guidance requires immutable repository claims
keyChanges.detail: The updated preview documentation says GitHub flexible federated identity credentials must match sub and at least one immutable claim: repository_id or repository_owner_id. The examples and operator guidance now use these claims with the eq operator when defining or reviewing trust.

keyChanges.title: Synchronization guidance adds sAMAccountName coverage for Domain Services
keyChanges.detail: The Synchronization page now describes enhanced support for synchronizing sAMAccountName with Microsoft Entra Domain Services and links to dedicated guidance for that scenario.

keyChanges.title: Licensing reference adds Windows 10 ESU identifiers to Windows 365 entries
keyChanges.detail: The reference, updated August 14, 2026, adds Windows 10 ESU service-plan identifiers to two Windows 365 plan entries. No administrator action is stated beyond using the updated reference when matching those plans.

2026-08-19.headline: Global Secure Access V2 guidance now spells out profile order and migration differences
2026-08-19.overview: The period's clearest administrator-relevant update concerns Global Secure Access web filtering: V2 selects the first applicable profile containing a V2 policy, individual rules do not support user or group targeting, and enforcement may differ from V1 during migration. ID Governance guidance also expands delegation coverage to multi-resource access reviews, while Entra ID clarifies the scope of application-owner permissions.
2026-08-19.adminImpact: Administrators planning V1-to-V2 migration should review overlapping profiles, consolidate policies where possible, and test allowed and blocked destinations. Governance administrators can control delegation to managers, specific groups, or any directory user and require expiration dates; single-resource access reviews are not included. The application-owner clarification supports more accurate permission guidance, with no mandatory action stated.

keyChanges.title: V2 profile selection and rule-targeting limits are now explicit
keyChanges.detail: Updated web-filtering guidance says V2 selects the first applicable profile containing a V2 policy. It also states that individual rules do not support user or group targeting and that enforcement may differ from V1 during migration.

keyChanges.title: My Access guidance adds delegated multi-resource access reviews
keyChanges.detail: The updated preview guidance covers delegating multi-resource access reviews in addition to access package approvals. Administrators can control delegation to a manager, specific groups, or any directory user, apply delegate-selection restrictions, set maximum delegation duration, and require expiration dates. Single-resource access reviews are not included.

keyChanges.title: Application-owner permissions are clarified by application scope
keyChanges.detail: The Assign App Owners guidance now compares application owners with application administrators, stating that owners can manage only the enterprise applications they own and have equivalent permissions within that application's scope.

keyChanges.title: V1-to-V2 migration instructions are now presented as numbered steps
keyChanges.detail: The migration guide now presents the V1-to-V2 procedure and migration options as numbered steps, making the sequence clearer to follow. No administrator action is required.

2026-08-20.headline: Custom CSS branding guidance spells out July 21 cutoff and property retirement
2026-08-20.overview: Most of the day's entries were documentation maintenance, but several updates have direct planning or configuration implications. Entra ID branding guidance says tenants created after January 5, 2026, cannot use custom CSS, older tenants not already using it cannot configure it after July 21, 2026, and custom CSS layout and positioning properties are being retired. A new federated sign-in page documents cross-root-domain blocking and related Microsoft Graph beta APIs; provisioning, Token Protection, and Lifecycle Workflows also received substantive guidance.
2026-08-20.adminImpact: Branding owners should identify existing CSS that uses layout or positioning properties and review their tenant configuration. Federation teams can assess cross-domain mappings; provisioning teams should enable “Flow null values” only where empty source values should remove target data and only in supported inbound scenarios. Token Protection planners can use the updated Apple support status, while ID Governance administrators should verify the 15-day mover-removal default against their access-removal requirements.

keyChanges.title: Company branding CSS restrictions and retirement
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID branding guidance says tenants created after January 5, 2026, cannot use custom CSS. After July 21, 2026, older tenants that were not already using it cannot configure it; support for custom CSS layout and positioning properties is being retired.

keyChanges.title: Federated sign-in security policy guidance
keyChanges.detail: A new Entra ID page explains that the policy blocks federated sign-ins when the trusted realm and mapped user account have different root domains. It also documents related Microsoft Graph beta APIs, which are subject to change and unsupported for production applications.

keyChanges.title: Inbound provisioning null-value clearing preview
keyChanges.detail: New Entra ID provisioning guidance documents clearing an existing target attribute when the source value is null or empty. The capability is opt-in, requires enabling “Flow null values” on both source and target mappings, and supports only single-valued attributes in specified inbound scenarios.

keyChanges.title: Apple Token Protection support status
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Token Protection reference now lists token protection for iOS/iPadOS and macOS as generally available. Supported web apps accessing Azure Resource Manager on macOS remain in preview.

keyChanges.title: Mover workflow access-removal timing
keyChanges.detail: ID Governance task guidance now applies “Remove all access package assignments for user” to both leaver and mover templates. For mover templates, scheduled removal defaults to 15 days; administrators can customize the timing or choose immediate removal.

2026-08-21.headline: Custom CSS branding faces late-October retirement after July 21 new-use cutoff
2026-08-21.overview: Microsoft Entra’s most consequential change is the planned retirement of custom CSS layout and positioning properties in company branding by late October 2026. The schedule blocks new use from July 21, 2026, and affected branding will revert to default layouts after retirement. Other updates primarily refresh FIDO2 hardware references and clarify authentication terminology.
2026-08-21.adminImpact: Review company branding configurations that use custom CSS layout or positioning properties and update them before late October 2026. Administrators evaluating FIDO2 hardware should consult the refreshed attestation and compatibility tables. Use the clarified PRMFA and multi-factor CBA terminology when interpreting authentication references; the ordering and formatting edits require no action.

keyChanges.title: Custom CSS company-branding properties will retire in late October
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra will retire custom CSS layout and positioning properties in company branding by late October 2026 to enhance security and reduce phishing risks. New use is blocked from July 21, 2026, and branding will revert to default layouts after retirement.

keyChanges.title: FIDO attestation data now reflects Metadata Service version 275
keyChanges.detail: The FIDO2 hardware reference now reflects FIDO Metadata Service version 275, with updated model entries, AAGUIDs, capability indicators, and newly listed authenticators. Use the refreshed table to verify hardware eligibility and supported capabilities.

keyChanges.title: Compatibility indicators change for several FIDO2 vendor entries
keyChanges.detail: Compatibility indicators were updated for several Arculus, Feitian, Hyper FIDO, and IDmelon authenticators, while multiple vendor entries were removed. Use the revised compatibility table when evaluating or deploying FIDO2 authenticators.

keyChanges.title: SAML guidance now labels synced passkeys as phishing-resistant MFA
keyChanges.detail: The SAML protocol reference now labels synced passkeys as phishing-resistant MFA and clarifies that the certificate-based authentication designation applies to multi-factor CBA. The associated SAML mappings are unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Optional claims reference explicitly identifies PRMFA authentication entries
keyChanges.detail: The Optional Claims Reference now labels synced passkeys as PRMFA and specifies that the PRMFA certificate-based authentication entry applies to multi-factor CBA. The clearer labels help distinguish authentication methods when interpreting optional claims.

2026-08-22.headline: External ID guidance details delegated API for customer-owned passkeys
2026-08-22.overview: A new External ID reference describes delegated credential management for signed-in customers’ passkeys, while ID Governance guidance now spells out the billing, role, and policy prerequisites for governed workforce tenant creation. Global Secure Access also records macOS client version 1.1.26060207, including Home Network traffic control, a Connections page, agentic detection support, Secure DNS bypass, and fixes. Most remaining changes refine terminology, links, and procedures; one Rouse Sales provisioning tutorial was removed.
2026-08-22.adminImpact: External ID implementers must manually provision the credential-management API service principal and grant the required delegated permission; app-only tokens aren't supported. Administrators creating governed workforce tenants should verify a paid Enterprise Agreement or Pay-As-You-Go subscription, the required subscription role, and the documented policy prerequisites. Intune deployers using the listed Global Secure Access macOS release should remove `com.microsoft.autoupdate2` from detection rules as directed in the release notes.

keyChanges.title: Delegated passkey management API is now documented for External ID customer apps
keyChanges.detail: Applications can use delegated access tokens to list, register, and delete signed-in customers’ passkeys. The service principal must be provisioned manually, and app-only tokens aren't supported.

keyChanges.title: Governed workforce tenant guidance now specifies paid billing and role prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The guidance specifies a paid Azure subscription associated with an Enterprise Agreement or pay-as-you-go billing account, along with the required tenant-creation permission, role, and default governance-policy prerequisites. Free or trial tenants cannot create additional tenants.

keyChanges.title: Governing-tenant default policy template is now optional in creation guidance
keyChanges.detail: The governing tenant’s default governance policy template is labeled optional rather than required. The tenant-creation service still uses only the template with ID `default`.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access macOS notes add version 1.1.26060207 deployment details
keyChanges.detail: The release notes document version 1.1.26060207, released August 21, 2026, with Home Network traffic control, a Connections page, agentic detection support, Secure DNS bypass, and several fixes. The Intune deployment guidance says to remove `com.microsoft.autoupdate2` from detection rules.

2026-08-24.headline: First-factor system-preferred authentication rolls out as Lifecycle Workflow guidance expands to 365 days
2026-08-24.overview: Microsoft Entra is applying system-preferred authentication to first-factor sign-ins for tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, with rollout continuing through late September 2026. ID Governance guidance now documents 365-day event offsets and clarifies the Time based attribute V2 trigger, while Global Secure Access records an August macOS client release with new controls and deployment considerations. Most remaining updates are documentation maintenance, including Connect Health version and download references and lifecycle-page reorganization.
2026-08-24.adminImpact: During the authentication rollout, review the system-preferred setting for Microsoft-managed tenants and update user guidance; admins can retain or change the setting. For Lifecycle Workflows, account for the documented 365-day range, ensure both workflows and schedules are enabled, and consider V2’s lack of a three-day catch-up window. For macOS deployments, review the new Global Secure Access release and check Intune detection rules for com.microsoft.autoupdate2, which the installation guidance says can optionally be removed from the Included apps list.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred authentication now covers first-factor sign-ins
keyChanges.detail: For tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, Microsoft Entra now selects the most secure registered authentication method for first-factor sign-ins. Rollout runs from late June through late September 2026; administrators can keep or change the setting and should update user guidance.

keyChanges.title: Lifecycle Workflow guidance documents 365-day event offsets
keyChanges.detail: The updated Execution Conditions page now states that the limits for Days from event, and Days to event when using Between, increased from 180 to 365 days. It describes conditions up to one year before or after an event and states that no administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Time based attribute V2 guidance clarifies comparisons and catch-up behavior
keyChanges.detail: The documentation describes Exactly, Less than or equal to, and Between comparisons with offsets from 0 to 180 days before or after supported date attributes. It also says both the workflow and schedule must be enabled, V2 has no three-day catch-up window, and the preview admin center may show two choices representing the same trigger.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access macOS release adds controls and Secure DNS bypass
keyChanges.detail: Release notes for August 21, 2026 list Home Network traffic controls, a Connections page, agentic detection support, and Secure DNS bypass, along with connectivity, sign-in, tunnel, cache-reset, and crash fixes. Administrators should review the release when planning macOS deployments.

keyChanges.title: macOS installation guidance flags an Intune detection conflict
keyChanges.detail: The installation page states that client version 1.1.26060207 includes com.microsoft.autoupdate2 and that an existing installation may conflict with Intune detection rules. It advises optionally removing that app from the Included apps list.

2026-08-25.headline: Linux broker 2.0.2 now uses Entra join for device trust
2026-08-25.overview: The most consequential update affects Microsoft Single Sign-On for Linux: version 2.0.2 and later uses Microsoft Entra join instead of device registration for device trust, and existing upgraded devices must be re-joined and re-enrolled. New Entra ID guidance also details enhanced synchronization for sourcing sAMAccountName. Most remaining updates are mechanical example-ID, browser-reference, or wording changes.
2026-08-25.adminImpact: Before deploying Linux broker 2.0.2 or later, allow users to join devices through Entra admin center > Devices > Device settings > Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra. Upgrade procedures should remove broker state, reinstall the broker, and re-join and re-enroll existing devices. For the SAM Account Name setting, review source values and application dependencies before enabling it; the setting applies to Enterprise or Premium managed domains and requires the Application Administrator and Groups Administrator roles.

keyChanges.title: Linux broker 2.0.2 switches device trust from registration to join
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Single Sign-On for Linux version 2.0.2 and later uses Microsoft Entra join for device trust. Existing upgraded devices must be re-joined and re-enrolled, with the documented upgrade process covering broker-state removal, reinstallation, and device re-join.

keyChanges.title: Enhanced synchronization can source sAMAccountName for hybrid users
keyChanges.detail: New guidance documents sourcing hybrid users’ sAMAccountName from onPremisesSamAccountName. Existing domains retain current behavior until the setting is enabled; enabling it updates existing hybrid users during synchronization. Cloud-only users without the source value continue using mailNickname-based generation.

keyChanges.title: Arc sign-in guidance limits the scenario to machines without another domain
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance states that enabling sign-in joins an Arc-enabled machine to Microsoft Entra and is intended for machines not planned to join another domain, including on-premises Active Directory or Microsoft Entra Domain Services. Administrators should confirm domain-join plans before enabling the capability.

2026-08-26.headline: Entra self-service identity management shifts to cloud.microsoft worldwide in late November
2026-08-26.overview: Microsoft Entra will move its self-service identity management domain from myaccount.microsoft.com to myaccount.cloud.microsoft worldwide in late November 2026. Global Secure Access release notes also set out automatic Windows Update upgrades for eligible clients beginning in November, while new App Gallery guidance and revised administration documentation clarify publishing, group creation, and tenant-creation requirements.
2026-08-26.adminImpact: Ensure network policies allow *.cloud.microsoft ahead of the Entra domain rollout. For Global Secure Access, review minimum client versions and decide whether automatic Windows Update delivery is acceptable; opting out requires the documented installer parameter and manual update management. Assign the Tenant Creator role to accounts that create add-on tenants, and do not assume SSGM controls every group-creation path: the revised guidance scopes it to the My Groups portal.

keyChanges.title: Self-service identity sites move to cloud.microsoft in late November
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is updating the self-service identity management domain from myaccount.microsoft.com to myaccount.cloud.microsoft and consolidating related sites. The worldwide rollout is planned for late November 2026; users need no action, but administrators should allow *.cloud.microsoft in network policies.

keyChanges.title: Eligible Global Secure Access Windows clients will receive automatic upgrades
keyChanges.detail: Starting in November 2026, eligible Windows clients will receive Global Secure Access upgrades through Windows Update. Version 2.32.294 adds Prefer local network, faster tunnel creation, and other fixes and improvements. Administrators opting out must use the documented installer parameter and maintain updates manually.

keyChanges.title: New App Gallery workflow details validation, submission, and review
keyChanges.detail: A new tutorial documents the self-service publishing workflow: complete validation prerequisites, create a submission, select capabilities, provide required application details, submit for Microsoft review, and track drafts. The guidance is primarily relevant to administrators supporting application publishers.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Creator is required regardless of the tenant restriction setting
keyChanges.detail: The Create Tenant guidance now states that the Tenant Creator role is required regardless of the “Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants” setting. Accounts expected to create add-on tenants therefore need that role.

keyChanges.title: SSGM guidance scopes its control to the My Groups portal
keyChanges.detail: The Groups Settings V2 guidance now states that standard users can create groups by default regardless of SSGM, and that SSGM controls behavior only in the My Groups portal. The MSODS reference was removed from the documentation.

2026-08-27.headline: LES Writeback, Android Play Integrity, and SCIM mailNickname rules sharpen Entra guidance
2026-08-27.overview: The period was dominated by ordinary documentation maintenance—sample GUIDs, example identifiers, a corrected link, and PowerShell example syntax. The substantive updates were clearer Conditional Access guidance for Android integrity checks, new Exchange Hybrid detail on LES Writeback, and a precise SCIM description of how Entra ID handles mailNickname during user creation.
2026-08-27.adminImpact: Review the revised Conditional Access guidance when troubleshooting Android access blocks. SCIM integrations can omit mailNickname but should account for Entra ID deriving it from userName. Teams working with LES Writeback can use the newly documented flow and attribute mappings. Recheck the listed application IDs when copying consent-policy rules; sample-identifier-only edits do not require tenant changes.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access guidance documents Android Play Integrity enforcement
keyChanges.detail: The Assignment Network guidance now says Microsoft Authenticator for Android uses the Google Play Integrity API for jailbreak detection and denies access when the API is unavailable, unless the policy is disabled. Use this detail when troubleshooting blocked Android access under Conditional Access.

keyChanges.title: Exchange Hybrid guidance adds Entra2ADExchangeOnlineAttributeWriteback detail
keyChanges.detail: The article now documents Entra2ADExchangeOnlineAttributeWriteback, also called LES Writeback, including its cloud-managed attribute flow, distinction from Exchange hybrid writeback, supported attributes, mappings, and related guidance.

keyChanges.title: SCIM reference clarifies mailNickname creation and PATCH limits
keyChanges.detail: When creating a user, mailNickname may be omitted, null, or empty. Entra ID derives it from the characters before the first @ in userName, and after creation it cannot be removed with PATCH.

keyChanges.title: Consent policy examples replace documented application IDs
keyChanges.detail: The Manage App Consent Policies guidance replaces the application IDs shown for Apple Mail, Spark Email, eM Client, Android-Samsung, Android-Mail, and Thunderbird. Administrators using those identifiers in consent-policy rules should verify them against the updated examples.

2023-09-25.headline: Entra ID sets 30 September 2025 deadline to leave legacy MFA and SSPR method management
2023-09-25.overview: The period’s only supplied update is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID. Microsoft says it will retire the ability to manage authentication methods through the legacy Multifactor Authentication (MFA) and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) policies on 30 September 2025. This is a forward-looking retirement notice, not evidence of an immediate behavior change this week.
2023-09-25.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to migrate methods managed through the legacy MFA and SSPR policies to the converged Authentication methods policy before the deadline. Microsoft describes that policy as the central management point for passwordless, multifactor authentication, and SSPR scenarios. The supplied notice does not include migration steps or technical prerequisites.

keyChanges.title: Management of methods in the legacy policies will be retired
keyChanges.detail: On 30 September 2025, Entra ID will no longer support managing authentication methods in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies. The notice specifically describes retirement of management in those policies; it does not say that the authentication methods themselves will be removed on that date.

2023-12-04.headline: Entra ID FIDO2 registration may offer passkey creation on another device
2023-12-04.overview: The week contains one Entra ID Message Center notice. It describes a changed FIDO2 security key registration experience in which users may receive an operating system- or browser-generated prompt to create a passkey on another device, such as a phone or tablet; some users may see a QR code for that flow. The notice does not establish a preview or general-availability milestone, a policy change, or a required administrator action.
2023-12-04.adminImpact: The concrete impact is to the user experience during FIDO2 registration. Administrators and support teams should be aware that a passkey-on-another-device prompt or QR code may be expected. The supplied evidence identifies no configuration change, migration, retirement, or mandatory action.

keyChanges.title: Alternate-device passkey prompts can appear during FIDO2 registration
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID users registering a FIDO2 security key may see a prompt generated by their operating system or browser to create a passkey on another device, including a phone or tablet. In some cases, a QR code facilitates the option. This is a registration-experience change, not evidence of a separate product launch or availability announcement.

2024-01-22.headline: India-specific removal of MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp is the only Entra ID change recorded
2024-01-22.overview: For the week of 22 January 2024, the supplied data records one Entra ID item: a 26 January Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about removing MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India. There are no recorded new, updated, or removed feature or documentation items, and the notice is a service-change communication rather than a feature launch or preview.
2024-01-22.adminImpact: Organizations without users in India can safely disregard the notice, according to its summary. Organizations with users in India should determine whether they rely on this delivery route. The supplied evidence does not state an effective date, replacement method, or specific migration task.

keyChanges.title: MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp is being removed in India
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Authentication notice describes a regional removal of this MFA delivery capability. It is an operational behavior change, not evidence of general availability, preview, or documentation clarification. No timing or replacement channel is provided in the supplied message.

2024-02-19.headline: Entra ID prepares a device-bound passkey preview, with FIDO2 policy and sign-in changes
2024-02-19.overview: The period’s sole supplied item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about a substantive Entra ID authentication change, not a general-availability announcement or a documentation clarification. Beginning in mid-March 2024, Entra ID is expected to add preview support for device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices alongside existing FIDO2 security-key support. The rollout also changes FIDO2 policy handling and makes the end-user sign-in terminology cover passkeys from all supported device types.
2024-02-19.adminImpact: Administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow the passkey providers they intend to support. They should also expect the Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in option to use new, broader wording. The supplied notice does not state that existing FIDO2 security-key support is being retired or that a migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Device-bound passkeys enter Entra ID as a preview authentication method
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-March 2024, Entra ID will support device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices, in addition to its existing support for FIDO2 security keys. The notice identifies this as a preview; it does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 policy must permit the intended passkey providers
keyChanges.detail: To allow specified passkey providers, administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy. This is the concrete configuration impact of extending supported credentials beyond security keys.

keyChanges.title: The Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in label becomes more inclusive
keyChanges.detail: The end-user option will be renamed to "Face, fingerprint, PIN, or security key." The updated sign-in experience will also use the term "passkey" so the wording covers passkey credentials presented from security keys, computers, and mobile devices.

2024-03-04.headline: Microsoft 365 Admin Center user-consent setting to be retired in early April
2024-03-04.overview: The only reported Entra ID change for the week is the retirement of the “User consent to Apps” setting in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. This changes where the tenant-wide user consent policy is managed, not the existing policy itself.
2024-03-04.adminImpact: No preparation is required. Existing settings will remain unchanged, but administrators will no longer be able to view or edit the policy in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center after the retirement. Use the user consent settings in the Entra portal instead.

keyChanges.title: Retirement of the Microsoft 365 Admin Center consent setting
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Admin Center experience for “User consent to Apps” will be retired in early April 2024. Management of the tenant-wide user consent policy moves to the corresponding Entra portal experience; the change does not alter existing settings.

2024-03-11.headline: Entra ID: PIM enters Power Platform public preview while Copilot welcome emails expand to external license assignments
2024-03-11.overview: The week of 11 March 2024 contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices for Entra ID. One announces the public preview of Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in the Power Platform admin center, a capability already available since 5 February. The other describes an upcoming late-March through late-April rollout that will send Copilot for Microsoft 365 welcome emails when licenses are assigned through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center. These notices represent a public preview and a change in email behavior—not a reported general-availability release or retirement.
2024-03-11.adminImpact: Power Platform administrators should treat the PIM integration as preview functionality. Organizations that assign Copilot for Microsoft 365 licenses through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center can review direct-communication preferences ahead of the rollout. The notice says organizations can adjust preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center, while individual users can change their own settings through security and privacy controls; it identifies no required migration.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM is in public preview in the Power Platform admin center
keyChanges.detail: The 13 March notice announces public preview availability of Entra Privileged Identity Management within the Power Platform admin center; the capability was made available on 5 February 2024. Microsoft describes PIM as providing management, control, and monitoring of access to important organizational resources. The supplied notice does not claim general availability or specify additional requirements.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Power Platform admin center

keyChanges.title: Copilot welcome emails will cover licenses assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center
keyChanges.detail: PowerShell and the Microsoft Entra admin center will support Copilot for Microsoft 365 welcome emails when licenses are assigned through methods other than the Microsoft 365 admin center. The rollout is scheduled to begin in late March 2024 and finish in late April 2024. End users will automatically receive the email when direct communications from Microsoft are enabled, and organizations or users can change the applicable communication preferences.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Microsoft Entra admin center / PowerShell

2024-03-18.headline: Entra ID is moving Teams app consent to new resource-specific controls while retiring legacy RSC interfaces
2024-03-18.overview: The period’s only supplied item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice describing a service rollout and retirement, not a documentation clarification. Entra ID and Microsoft Teams are introducing teams- and chat-specific resource-specific consent settings for apps using Chat RSC and Team RSC. The notice does not identify the change as preview or generally available.
2024-03-18.adminImpact: The change began taking effect on March 7, 2024, with rollout to all tenants scheduled to complete by April 14, 2024. Administrators whose processes or tooling depend on the existing Group owner consent settings or API, or the existing Chat RSC API, need to account for their retirement. The new settings are managed through Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets, and Teams-level administrators can manage them independently.

keyChanges.title: New consent controls apply to Teams and chat resources
keyChanges.detail: Resource-specific consent settings are being introduced for apps in Microsoft Teams, covering Chat RSC and Team RSC. Microsoft describes the change as intended to enhance secure app adoption, but supplies no further security requirements or configuration details.

keyChanges.title: Legacy consent settings and APIs are retiring
keyChanges.detail: The existing Group owner consent settings and API, together with the existing Chat RSC API, will be retired as part of this update. This creates a compatibility and administration impact for tenants or automation that still depend on those interfaces.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — Group owner consent and Chat RSC

keyChanges.title: Administration shifts to Microsoft Graph PowerShell during a staged rollout
keyChanges.detail: The new teams-specific consent settings are managed using Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets. Teams-level admins can manage them independently; the notice says the rollout started taking effect on March 7 and will be complete across tenants by April 14, 2024.

2024-04-29.headline: Dataverse user cleanup for Microsoft Entra identities enters public preview
2024-04-29.overview: The only supplied Entra-related change for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for a Microsoft Entra ID–related Dataverse capability. The feature is identified as a Public Preview launching 1 May 2024; it is not described as generally available or as a retirement.
2024-04-29.adminImpact: Administrators responsible for Dataverse environments may gain the ability to delete users in a disabled status, including delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Microsoft cites privacy and regulatory requirements and storage reduction as the intended benefits. The evidence does not state that action is mandatory or provide rollout, configuration, eligibility, or automation details.

keyChanges.title: Public Preview of deleting disabled Dataverse users
keyChanges.detail: The announcement covers delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Its summary describes the capability as deleting users with a disabled status from Dataverse environments. Microsoft positions this as a way to support privacy and regulatory obligations and free storage; no evidence is supplied about the deletion workflow or required administrator steps.

2024-05-13.headline: Week of 13 May: replace Workload ID symmetric keys by 15 June; passkey support begins rolling out
2024-05-13.overview: The supplied period contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no documented Entra content additions, updates, or removals. The most consequential change is the planned disablement of symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Separately, Entra ID is beginning a staged authentication-strength improvement for device-stored passkeys.
2024-05-13.adminImpact: Organizations using symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals must replace them with asymmetric keys by 15 June 2024 to avoid authentication failures. No preparation is required for the Entra ID passkey rollout, although administrators may update relevant user documentation to reflect the new registration options.

keyChanges.title: Workload ID will disable symmetric keys for first-party application service principals
keyChanges.detail: This Microsoft 365 Message Center major update describes a security-driven authentication behavior change. Organizations must switch from symmetric to asymmetric keys by 15 June 2024; otherwise, affected authentication attempts may fail.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID authentication strength is being improved to support device-stored passkeys
keyChanges.detail: The rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-May 2024 and complete by early August 2024. Users will see new passkey registration options in My Security Info. The notice says no administrator preparation is needed; updating relevant documentation is optional.

2024-05-20.headline: Entra PIM is generally available for time-bound Dynamics 365 and Power Platform tenant admin roles
2024-05-20.overview: The week contained one Entra ID Message Center announcement. Microsoft announced general availability, beginning May 23, 2024, of managing admin roles for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform through Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM). No documentation additions, updates, or removals were supplied.
2024-05-20.adminImpact: Administrators can use Microsoft Entra PIM to assign tenant admin roles for a defined period in Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform. The supplied announcement does not identify additional prerequisites, migration work, or configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: General availability of Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform
keyChanges.detail: This is a general availability change—not a preview or documentation clarification. Beginning May 23, 2024, Microsoft Entra PIM supports assigning tenant admin roles for these workloads for a certain time period. The announcement was published in the Microsoft 365 Message Center on May 24.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Privileged Identity Management

2024-07-01.headline: Entra ID Conditional Access Insider Risk condition reaches general availability
2024-07-01.overview: The period’s sole substantive update is the general availability of Microsoft Entra’s Insider Risk condition in Conditional Access. The capability uses insider risk signals from Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection so organizations can enforce Conditional Access actions according to user risk levels. Rollout begins in early July 2024 and is expected to complete by early August 2024.
2024-07-01.adminImpact: Use of the capability requires an Entra ID P2 license and Adaptive Protection to be enabled. Eligible organizations can configure Conditional Access policies that respond to the resulting insider-risk signals; tenants may receive the capability during the stated rollout window.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk condition is now generally available in Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: This moves the condition from its prior status into general availability and adds insider-risk signals from Adaptive Protection as inputs for Conditional Access policy decisions. The available enforcement behavior is based on user risk levels, rather than only the existing Conditional Access conditions described in the evidence.

keyChanges.title: Prerequisites and rollout are explicit
keyChanges.detail: Organizations need both an Entra ID P2 license and enabled Adaptive Protection to use the feature. Microsoft’s message says rollout starts in early July 2024 and completes by early August 2024, so availability may arrive during that window rather than simultaneously for every tenant.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection

2024-07-08.headline: Azure AD Graph retirement is the clearest lifecycle signal in a sparse Entra week
2024-07-08.overview: The supplied period contains one Microsoft 365 Message Center item, posted 12 July, summarizing June 2024 Microsoft Entra updates. It flags Azure AD Graph retirement, Entra ID releases described as generally available, Apple-device security enhancements, and Entra ID updates affecting older Windows builds. No new, updated, or removed documentation items were supplied, and the record does not include the detail needed to establish feature names, dates, affected versions, or required actions.
2024-07-08.adminImpact: Azure AD Graph retirement is the most consequential item to validate in the underlying Message Center detail, but this record does not support a migration deadline or specific tenant action. The GA, Apple, and Windows references likewise lack enough detail to assess rollout, configuration, or compatibility impact. The period provides no evidence of an ordinary documentation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Azure AD Graph retirement called out
keyChanges.detail: The June 2024 roundup identifies Azure AD Graph Retirement. This is a capability-lifecycle change rather than a documentation update; the supplied message gives no retirement date, scope, migration guidance, or affected workload details.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD Graph

keyChanges.title: Entra ID general availability releases
keyChanges.detail: The message explicitly describes June releases for Entra ID as generally available. It does not name the releases, so no feature-level behavior, eligibility, or administrator step can be stated from the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Security enhancements for Apple devices
keyChanges.detail: The roundup says that security enhancements for Apple devices were included. It does not identify the Apple platforms, controls, rollout behavior, or configuration changes, so their administrative impact cannot be determined.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID updates affecting older Windows builds
keyChanges.detail: The summary flags Entra ID updates affecting old Windows builds. No build numbers or description of the change are provided, so the evidence does not establish whether this is a support, compatibility, or behavior change.

2024-07-29.headline: Entitlement Management will prevent privileged administrators from bypassing access package approvals
2024-07-29.overview: Starting August 26, 2024, Entitlement Management will enforce access package policy approval settings for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators. The supplied period contains a single Message Center notice describing this behavior change; it does not report a new feature launch, preview, retirement, or documentation update.
2024-07-29.adminImpact: No action is required from organizations because Microsoft says the change is automatic. Administrators should expect the affected privileged roles to be subject to the approval requirements configured in access package policies rather than being able to bypass them.

keyChanges.title: Approval enforcement extends to Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators
keyChanges.detail: Changes to Entitlement Management will prevent these two administrator roles from bypassing access package policy approvals. The change takes effect on August 26, 2024 and is described as an automatic update.

2024-08-05.headline: Week of 5 August 2024: Edge mobile Copilot retirement leads several Entra availability rollouts
2024-08-05.overview: The supplied period contains five Microsoft 365 Message Center announcements and no new, updated, or removed documentation items. The most consequential user-facing change is the retirement of Copilot in the Microsoft Edge mobile application for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August. Other substantive announcements move Attacker in the Middle detection in ID Protection, the AD FS application migration wizard, and device-based Conditional Access on Red Hat Enterprise Linux to general availability. A separate Dynamics 365 notice announces availability of a feature for deleting certain Microsoft Entra group users.
2024-08-05.adminImpact: The only explicit communication request is to inform affected users about the Edge mobile Copilot retirement and direct them to the Microsoft 365 mobile app for work or web chat. The ID Protection, AD FS migration wizard, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux Conditional Access announcements each state that no action is required before rollout. The Dynamics 365 notice confirms availability beginning 8 August but does not provide enough detail to infer a required cleanup, configuration change, or deletion workflow.

keyChanges.title: Retirement: Copilot in the Edge mobile application for Entra ID users
keyChanges.detail: Copilot in the Microsoft Edge mobile app will be retired with version 128 in late August 2024 for Entra ID users. No administrator action is required, but Microsoft recommends informing users and directing work users to the Microsoft 365 mobile app or web chat instead.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: Attacker in the Middle detection alert
keyChanges.detail: The Attacker in the Middle detection feature in Microsoft Entra ID Protection is scheduled to reach general availability by late August. The capability is intended to identify compromised user accounts, and the notice says no action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: AD FS application migration wizard
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Entra ID AD FS application migration wizard provides a guided experience for migrating AD FS relying-party applications. Rollout begins in mid-August and is expected to complete by late August; no administrator action is required before the rollout.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: Device-based Conditional Access on Red Hat Enterprise Linux
keyChanges.detail: Device-based Conditional Access for Microsoft 365 and Azure resources on Red Hat Enterprise Linux is going generally available in mid-to-late August. The stated support includes Entra ID registration, Conditional Access policies, SSO, Intune compliance, and Red Hat RPM packages; no action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Available: Dynamics 365 deletion of certain Microsoft Entra group users
keyChanges.detail: Starting 8 August 2024, Dynamics 365 will have a generally available feature to delete stub, unlicensed, and removed Microsoft Entra group users. The supplied announcement does not describe the trigger, scope, or administrator workflow, so it does not support a more specific operational recommendation.

2024-08-12.headline: Microsoft requires tenant MFA for admin-portal access by 15 October 2024
2024-08-12.overview: The week’s sole supplied change was a Microsoft 365 Message Center Major update for Entra ID Authentication. It is a security-enforcement notice, not a new feature or documentation clarification: tenants must enable MFA to retain administrative access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center.
2024-08-12.adminImpact: Administrators should enable MFA before 15 October 2024. The notice also identifies an option to apply to postpone the enforcement date if necessary; without MFA, administrative access to the listed portals will be restricted.

keyChanges.title: Tenant MFA deadline and access restriction announced
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s 16 August notice says MFA must be enabled for the tenant by 15 October 2024 for access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. It advises setting up MFA early or applying to postpone enforcement where necessary. No other Entra feature, availability change, retirement, or documentation update is supplied for this period.

2024-09-02.headline: Microsoft Entra ID announces public preview of FIDO2 provisioning APIs
2024-09-02.overview: The period’s only supplied Entra change is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for new FIDO2 provisioning APIs in public preview. The capability is intended to let organizations pre-provision security keys for users, simplifying onboarding and supporting phishing-resistant authentication. Rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-September 2024 and finish by late September.
2024-09-02.adminImpact: No administrator action is required for the rollout. The announcement does not provide configuration, eligibility, or migration requirements, and the capability should be treated as a public preview rather than a generally available feature.

keyChanges.title: Pre-provisioning of FIDO2 security keys enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is introducing APIs that enable security keys to be provisioned for users before onboarding. This changes the onboarding workflow the preview is designed to support, while the supplied notice does not establish general availability or require administrators to make changes during rollout.

2024-09-09.headline: Tenant MFA action deadline set for 15 October 2024
2024-09-09.overview: The week contains one Microsoft 365 Message Center action for Microsoft Entra ID. Administrators are asked to enable multifactor authentication (MFA) for the tenant by 15 October 2024 to access the Microsoft Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. No supplied evidence indicates a new Entra feature, documentation change, or retirement during this period.
2024-09-09.adminImpact: Review tenant MFA readiness before the deadline. Postponement is possible, but administrators signing in without MFA will be prompted to register for it, which changes the sign-in experience and may affect access to the listed admin centers.

keyChanges.title: MFA becomes an explicit prerequisite for access to key admin centers
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice calls for tenant MFA enablement by 15 October 2024 for access to the Azure, Entra, and Intune admin centers. This is an administrative security action and deadline, not a product launch. If MFA is not enabled, admin sign-in will prompt MFA registration; the notice also states that postponement is available.

2024-10-07.headline: Microsoft Edge Mobile will change the New tab experience for Microsoft Entra ID users
2024-10-07.overview: The week contained one Microsoft 365 Message Center notice and no recorded Entra documentation additions, updates, or removals. The notice concerns Microsoft Edge Mobile rather than a new Entra ID capability: Wallpaper will be enabled by default on the New tab page, and a weather icon will be added. The changes were expected to roll out in early and late October 2024, respectively.
2024-10-07.adminImpact: No administrator action is required before the rollout. Administrators should expect affected Microsoft Entra ID users on Microsoft Edge Mobile to see the updated New tab defaults as the changes arrive.

keyChanges.title: Edge Mobile is changing the default New tab experience
keyChanges.detail: For Microsoft Entra ID users, Wallpaper will be enabled by default, with the wallpaper rollout expected in early October 2024. A weather icon was expected to follow in late October 2024. This is an announced user-experience behavior change, not evidence of a new Entra ID feature or a change to Entra ID administration.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge Mobile / Entra ID users

2024-10-14.headline: Entra message flags Azure AD Graph retirement, MFA enforcement and Apple-device security changes—but provides no operational details
2024-10-14.overview: The only supplied signal for the week of 14 October 2024 is a 15 October Microsoft 365 Message Center roundup for Microsoft Entra ID. Its summary says the September 2024 update covered general-availability releases, Azure AD Graph retirement, security enhancements for Apple devices and MFA enforcement.
