2024-11-04.headline: Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp for MFA OTP delivery in India starting December 2024
2024-11-04.overview: The only supplied change for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update affecting Entra ID. Beginning in December 2024, users in India who have WhatsApp will receive MFA one-time passcodes through WhatsApp, with SMS used as a fallback. Microsoft says the channel will expand to additional countries, but does not specify which ones or when.
2024-11-04.adminImpact: Review whether WhatsApp-based OTP delivery fits the organization’s authentication policy before the rollout. Administrators can disable the feature or direct users toward stronger methods such as Microsoft Authenticator; the supplied notice does not provide configuration steps or a more specific rollout schedule.

keyChanges.title: WhatsApp becomes an MFA OTP delivery channel again
keyChanges.detail: This is a planned service behavior change and regional rollout—not a documentation-only clarification. Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp delivery in India from December 2024, with expansion to more countries. Users with WhatsApp will receive the code there, while SMS remains the fallback channel.

2025-01-20.headline: Entra ID is enabling Authenticator passkeys for FIDO2 organizations without key restrictions
2025-01-20.overview: The week of 20 January 2025 contains one substantive item: a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID Authentication. Starting in late January 2025, organizations with an enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and no key restrictions will have passkeys available in the Microsoft Authenticator app. The supplied evidence describes an enablement notice, not a documentation change, and does not label the capability as preview or generally available.
2025-01-20.adminImpact: Administrators in the affected configuration should expect users to be able to add an Authenticator passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, with use enforced by Conditional Access policy. Organizations that do not want this enablement can impose key restrictions. No additional rollout scope or administrative steps are provided.

keyChanges.title: Authenticator passkeys become available under a specific FIDO2 policy configuration
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in late January 2025, passkeys in the Microsoft Authenticator app will be available to organizations that have enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and have not configured key restrictions. Users can add the passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, and Conditional Access policy governs enforcement. This is the period’s only supplied change.

2025-02-17.headline: Entra is introducing a dedicated Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
2025-02-17.overview: The week of 17 February contains one reported Entra change: a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement about a new built-in role for Viva Glint. The rollout is expected from late March to early April 2025. No separate Entra documentation updates, retirements, or other product changes are included in the supplied period.
2025-02-17.adminImpact: The role is intended to let administrators manage Viva Glint settings without Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. Administrators should review the role documentation, assess current role assignments, and communicate the change to affected staff before the rollout.

keyChanges.title: New built-in Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is introducing the role in Microsoft Entra to provide Viva Glint settings management without requiring Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. This is a planned rollout announcement, not evidence that the role is already generally available; the stated rollout window is late March to early April 2025.

2025-03-03.headline: Microsoft Entra rolls out a People administrator role while ID Protection alerts move to Defender XDR
2025-03-03.overview: The supplied record for the week of 3 March contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices and no documentation additions, updates, or removals. Microsoft Entra is rolling out a new People administrator role, while Entra ID Protection alerts are being removed from Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR.
2025-03-03.adminImpact: The People administrator role is intended to support people-related administration and profile-photo management without requiring high privileges; the notice does not specify assignment steps or label the capability as preview or generally available. For ID Protection, the notice says no administrator action is required, but asks administrators to review their configuration and notify users about the change in alert location.

keyChanges.title: New People administrator role begins rollout
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is introducing a People administrator role based on customer feedback. It allows management of people-related settings and profile photos without requiring high privileges. The stated rollout began in early February 2025 and is expected to complete by late March; the notice describes a rollout but does not establish preview or general-availability status.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection alerts leave Defender for Cloud Apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting 5 March 2025, Microsoft Entra ID Protection alerts are no longer available in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and are integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR. This is a change to where the alerts are surfaced, not an evidence-based statement that ID Protection alerting itself is being retired. The notice says no admin action is required, while recommending configuration review and user notification.

2025-03-10.headline: Entra ID: “Require approved client app” control planned for retirement in March 2026
2025-03-10.overview: The only supplied update for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center reminder that the “Require approved client app” Conditional Access control will be retired in March 2026. Microsoft directs organizations to update affected policies to use the “Require application protection policy” grant control. This is a planned retirement notice, not a new feature, preview, general availability announcement, or evidence that the control has already been removed.
2025-03-10.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies that use the retiring control and plan updates to the named replacement before March 2026. The supplied notice does not provide an exact retirement date or migration details, so administrators should validate the replacement in their policies before making production changes.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access control scheduled for retirement
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the “Require approved client app” grant control in Microsoft Entra Conditional Access will be retired in March 2026 and advises organizations to use “Require application protection policy” instead. No other Entra changes were supplied for this period.

2025-04-07.headline: Entra ID authentication-registration interface will change from late April to late May
2025-04-07.overview: The week of 7 April contained one Entra-related Microsoft 365 Message Center notice. Microsoft plans to update the “More information required” user interface shown during authentication method registration, beginning in late April 2025 and completing by late May 2025. The supplied evidence describes a planned user-experience change, not a new feature, preview, retirement, or documented change to authentication policy.
2025-04-07.adminImpact: The rollout will happen automatically and requires no administrator action. Microsoft recommends notifying users and updating internal documentation as needed. The notice does not specify changes to registration requirements, authentication methods, or administrative controls.

keyChanges.title: Authentication method registration prompt will be refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The affected experience is the “More information required” interface in Microsoft Entra ID. The notice does not explain how the screen or user flow will differ, so it does not support inferring a change to authentication methods or enforcement. Rollout is scheduled to start in late April 2025 and finish by late May 2025.

2025-04-14.headline: Workload ID sets a 31 March 2026 remediation deadline; the rest of the week is mostly Entra guidance and preview documentation
2025-04-14.overview: The week of 14 April 2025 was documentation-heavy: 380 entries were updated, four were new, three were removed, and there were no Message Center items. The clearest operational signal is updated Workload ID guidance stating that service principal-less authentication will no longer be supported from March 2026, with action required before 31 March 2026 to avoid application authentication failures. Other notable updates cover mandatory MFA readiness and lockout guidance, plus the explicitly preview Conditional Access optimization agent. The supplied evidence does not establish a new general-availability launch or a tenant-wide service change this week.
2025-04-14.adminImpact: Prioritize the Workload ID mitigation path for affected applications: verify access, create an enterprise application, and verify tokens before the stated deadline. Use the updated Entra ID guidance to verify mandatory MFA readiness for Azure and other management portals. Treat the Conditional Access optimization agent as preview, and validate Conditional Access scope, diagnostics, and External ID connector certificate handling only where those capabilities are in use; the documentation updates alone do not imply blanket tenant configuration changes.

keyChanges.detail: Two updated Workload ID pages say Microsoft Entra ID will no longer support service principal-less authentication behavior from March 2026. A related retirement page says administrators must act before 31 March 2026 to avoid application authentication failures, and the mitigation guidance specifically calls for verifying access, creating an enterprise application, and verifying tokens. This is a documented future deprecation and behavior change, not evidence that retirement began during this week.

keyChanges.detail: On 20 April, a new Entra ID authentication page covering users locked out by mandatory MFA was added, while the mandatory MFA and user-verification pages were also updated. This is security and rollout-readiness guidance; the records do not indicate that MFA enforcement behavior or rollout timing changed this week.

keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra ID pages describe the Conditional Access optimization agent as being in preview. The update clarifies the preview scope; it is not a general-availability announcement.

2025-04-21.headline: Entra Connect application-based authentication is the week’s clearest operational signal
2025-04-21.overview: The updated Microsoft Entra Connect guidance describes an application-based authentication path using an Entra application identity and OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow, with a single-tenant third-party application created to enable it. The period was otherwise overwhelmingly Microsoft Learn maintenance—2,785 records were updated and only three were new—so the strongest additional signals are targeted MFA and Conditional Access clarifications, a new token-security article, and two Message Center notices. 2025-05-05.headline: Week of 5 May 2025: a global Defender for Identity sensor notice leads a largely documentation-driven Entra update
2025-05-05.overview: The period was principally documentation maintenance: 138 of 145 records were updates, with three new and three removed entries. The clearest operational notice was the 9 May Microsoft 365 Message Center item for deploying the Defender for Identity sensor on Microsoft Entra Connect servers; it says the update is globally available, recommends installation for monitoring, and says no action is required before rollout. The most meaningful Learn changes are scope and behavior clarifications for Workload ID token lifetimes, External ID passkeys, and Access Reviews, plus preview setup guidance for Security Copilot. Other clusters, including phishing-resistant passwordless planning and custom authentication-extension documentation, are guidance updates rather than evidence of launches. The three removals have no supplied detail, so no retirement can be characterized.
2025-05-05.adminImpact: Do not treat this as a broad tenant-reconfiguration week. For hybrid identity, no pre-rollout action is called for by the sensor notice, but teams should evaluate the recommended sensor installation on Entra Connect servers. Anyone using or evaluating the Workload ID token-lifetime preview must account for its managed-identity exclusion; External ID designs must not assume guest or B2B users in the resource tenant can register FIDO2 passkeys; and Access Review operators must remember that mid-review changes do not update the running instance. For the Security Copilot agent preview, initial enablement requires a Security Administrator or Global Administrator; Conditional Access Administrators can be delegated access after setup when they have Security Copilot access.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity sensor on Entra Connect servers is described as globally available
keyChanges.detail: The 9 May Message Center entry instructs organizations to deploy a Defender for Identity sensor on Microsoft Entra Connect servers and describes the update as globally available for hybrid-identity monitoring and threat detection. It also says no admin action is required before rollout while recommending installation. Because the supplied summary uses both new and classic sensor terminology, the evidence supports an operational availability notice, not a clear retirement or breaking change.

keyChanges.title: Configurable token lifetimes remain explicitly scoped as a Workload ID preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated page says access, ID, and SAML token lifetimes can be configured for all apps in an organization, multitenant applications, or specific service principals. It explicitly excludes managed identity service principals. This is a supported-scope clarification for a preview, not evidence of general availability or a newly changed limit.

keyChanges.title: External ID documentation clarifies the guest passkey limitation
keyChanges.detail: The updated passkey and FIDO2 guidance states that internal or external guest users, including B2B collaboration users in the resource tenant, cannot register passkey credentials. This establishes a documented support boundary; the supplied evidence does not show that guest behavior changed during the week.

keyChanges.title: Access Reviews use a snapshot taken when each review instance starts
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Entra ID Governance FAQ says that an access review captures user assignments, group membership, and reviewer configuration at the start of the review. keyChanges.title: Security Copilot preview guidance sets the initial setup role boundary
keyChanges.detail: The updated Agent Optimization guidance says initial agent enablement and setup during the preview requires either the Security Administrator or Global Administrator role, which have Security Copilot access by default. After setup, Conditional Access Administrators can be assigned Security Copilot access and use the agent. This is preview onboarding and delegation guidance, not a general-availability announcement.

2025-05-12.headline: Tenant Restrictions v2 enforcement guidance and an Entra ID token-correlation preview headline a documentation-heavy week
2025-05-12.overview: The week of 12 May 2025 was overwhelmingly a Microsoft Learn maintenance cycle: 768 entries were updated, four were new, four were removed, and there were no Message Center items. The meaningful content is concentrated in security and authentication: an Entra ID preview describes linkable identifiers in all access tokens; related External ID and Global Secure Access pages clarify Tenant Restrictions v2 scope, Universal Tenant Restrictions behavior, and migration from v1; and a new Security Copilot page covers phishing-resistant MFA. The remaining notable items are security-control or application-migration guidance, while many other edits—such as Windows and Linux sign-in, passkey tables, provisioning, and SSO tutorials—are ordinary reference updates. The new Adobe Creative Cloud SSO and Entra Suite scenario pages are how-to content, not evidence of launches. No supplied item establishes general availability or a tenant-wide rollout; the removed records contain no details from which to infer a retirement.
2025-05-12.adminImpact: Treat this as a targeted review queue rather than a blanket tenant change. Tenant Restrictions and Global Secure Access administrators should check their v1/v2 posture and how own-tenant versus cross-tenant authentication will be treated. Security investigators can assess whether the preview identifiers and MFA log-correlation details fit their hunting workflows. Security Copilot owners should review the phishing-resistant MFA guidance. App teams should verify device-code usage before using the documented Conditional Access block and locate SPAs still using implicit grant before following the MSAL.js authorization-code and PKCE migration path. The evidence does not establish an automatic policy change, mandatory enforcement, GA status, deprecation, or retirement.

2025-10-13.headline: Teams group-chat authentication is the week’s main Entra behavior rollout; most other changes are administrator guidance
2025-10-13.overview: The week of 13 October 2025 is dominated by Microsoft Learn maintenance: 35 updated entries, two new pages, one Microsoft 365 Message Center notice, and no removed entries. The meaningful product change is the scheduled Microsoft Teams group-chat agent and bot support for Microsoft Entra authentication. The strongest operational exceptions are updates to Group Source of Authority and Microsoft Entra Connect guidance, along with security and Global Secure Access troubleshooting material. Nothing supplied is labeled preview or general availability, and no retirement is announced. The two new Entra ID pages—SharePoint Backup Administrator and Exchange Backup Administrator—contain only their titles in the supplied excerpts, so they are new documentation, not evidence of newly introduced roles or permissions. For deployments using Group Source of Authority or Microsoft Entra Connect, the updated documentation provides concrete workflow and host-support checks. Security teams working on passwordless or FIDO2 authentication can use the refreshed guidance, and Global Secure Access operators gain more documented troubleshooting signals. The supplied evidence does not support a mandatory tenant change, client upgrade, RBAC assignment, or retirement.

2025-10-20.headline: Entra ID backup authentication guidance clarifies CRL revocation limits; most other updates are procedural
2025-10-20.overview: The week of 20 October 2025 is a documentation-only period in the supplied data: 20 Microsoft Learn records were updated, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The most consequential update is an Entra ID resilience and security clarification: the backup authentication system cannot perform a fresh certificate revocation list (CRL) check and instead uses the CRL state from the last backed-up session. Other substantive updates describe ID Governance workflows and a Workday provisioning setting. The evidence does not establish any launch, preview, general availability, retirement, or underlying service-behavior change.
2025-10-20.adminImpact: If a session must be revoked before the backup expires, the documented action is to explicitly revoke the session rather than wait for a fresh CRL check. Administrators configuring Workday provisioning or entitlement-management dynamic approval can use the specific procedure updates, while the Access Review Agent article should not be treated as evidence of a tenant-wide rollout or availability status. Several remaining edits are ordinary documentation clarification, including External ID sign-in screenshots, a Conditional Access Save-button step, Global Secure Access sign-in and script instructions, and author, include-file, or checklist changes.

keyChanges.title: Backup Authentication System: revocation behavior is explicitly documented
keyChanges.detail: The updated Entra ID architecture guidance says the backup authentication system cannot perform fresh CRL checks. It relies on the CRL result recorded when the session was last backed up; when revocation is needed before that backup expires, administrators should explicitly revoke the session. This is security guidance describing the documented fallback behavior, not evidence that the service behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: Access Review Agent: reviewer assistance is described, not announced as a release
keyChanges.detail: The ID Governance article describes an Access Review Agent that gathers insights, generates recommendations, and guides reviewers in Microsoft Teams with natural-language summaries and proposed decisions. Reviewers still make the final call. The supplied update provides capability documentation but gives no preview, general availability, or rollout information.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management dynamic approval: Logic App setup details are spelled out
keyChanges.detail: The updated ID Governance guidance covers creating a custom extension backed by an Azure Logic App, assigning its system-assigned identity a role in the catalog, editing the Logic App action to perform the business logic, and testing the workflow. This is implementation guidance; the record does not indicate a newly released capability or changed availability.

keyChanges.title: Workday provisioning: termination lookahead is called out as a configuration setting
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID provisioning article specifically instructs administrators to enable the Termination Lookahead query for a Workday-to-AD or Workday-to-Microsoft Entra ID provisioning job. The evidence supports treating this as integration configuration guidance rather than a new provisioning-feature announcement.

2025-10-27.headline: PIM Iteration 2 API retirement and eDiscovery access enforcement are the week’s consequential changes
2025-10-27.overview: The week of 27 October 2025 was dominated by documentation maintenance: 121 items were updated, with no new or removed items recorded. The two Message Center notices carry the clearest operational impact. Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) Iteration 2 beta APIs now have a retirement date, while Microsoft Purview is applying Entra Conditional Access compliance to eDiscovery administrators’ SharePoint access. Other notable updates clarify existing behavior or describe capabilities explicitly marked as preview; they do not establish a new GA launch on the supplied evidence.
2025-10-27.adminImpact: Inventory applications that use PIM Iteration 2 beta APIs, stop new development on them, and plan migration to the Iteration 3 GA APIs before 28 October 2026. Review the Conditional Access requirements affecting eDiscovery administrators and account for the new FilePreviewed audit activity. Administrators using the Conditional Access optimization agent or external authentication methods should apply the clarified role and test-group guidance. The Lifecycle Workflows changes remain preview documentation rather than evidence of a tenant-wide rollout.

keyChanges.detail: Retirement notice for Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. Applications that continue using the Iteration 2 beta APIs will fail after the retirement date. 2025-11-03.headline: Passkey-profile preview and 30-day cloud-group recovery headline the week of 3 November 2025

2025-11-24.headline: Entra ID Protection alert defaults shift on 11 December; agent identity governance is the main documentation theme
2025-11-24.overview: The supplied week is mostly maintenance rather than a launch cycle: 37 records are Microsoft Learn updates, no item is classified as new, one External ID page was removed, and one Message Center notice was issued. That notice announces the clearest behavior change—the Defender XDR alert configuration and default for Entra ID Protection. 2025-12-08.headline: DigiCert G2 trust deadline is the week’s urgent Entra action; EAM preview registration is now enforced
2025-12-08.overview: The week of 8 December 2025 was not a launch-heavy period: the supplied record shows no new or removed items, and most entries are Microsoft Learn documentation updates. The material exceptions are an Entra certificate-trust change with a 7 January 2026 deadline, an External Authentication Methods (EAM) public-preview registration change, and the continuing Microsoft baseline-security rollout. Other notable edits describe Agent ID preview governance and clarify existing authentication and app-consent behavior; they do not establish general availability or a retirement. The authentication edits also clarify that security questions are for SSPR only, not sign-in, and cannot verify administrator accounts during SSPR.
2025-12-08.adminImpact: Verify that DigiCert Global Root G2 is trusted for Entra services and remove any G1 pinning before 7 January 2026; the Message Center update warns that otherwise authentication failures may occur. For EAM, prepare for inline setup by users added after 2 December 2025, communicate the preview registration requirement, and note that admins can register users. For Baseline Security Mode, use the dashboard, impact reports, and risk-based recommendations as the rollout proceeds; the update says there is no immediate user impact. If using the Microsoft-managed app-consent setting, account for its documented ability to update with Microsoft’s latest recommended defaults. The supplied Agent ID material gives no GA date or migration requirement.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra is moving from DigiCert Global Root G1 to G2
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center major update says Entra will switch to DigiCert Global Root G2 certificates by 7 January 2026. Organizations must trust the G2 root CA, remove any pinning to G1, and update trust settings to avoid authentication failures or service disruption. This is an operational certificate-trust requirement, not a documentation-only clarification.

keyChanges.title: External Authentication Methods public preview now enforces registration
keyChanges.detail: The EAM public preview update says registration enforcement begins 8 December 2025. The changed onboarding path should be communicated and reflected in configuration reviews. The notice identifies EAM as public preview, not generally available.

keyChanges.title: Baseline Security Mode continues its cross-workload security rollout
keyChanges.detail: The major update describes Microsoft Baseline Security Mode rolling out from November 2025 through March 2026 across Office, SharePoint, Exchange, Teams, and Entra. It centralizes recommended security standards and provides a dashboard with impact reports and risk-based recommendations. The update explicitly says there is no immediate user impact, so this is a security-posture assessment and improvement rollout rather than an immediate user-facing change.

No tenant action is required for the Microsoft Rewards retirement. For Agent ID, Temporary Access Pass, and Quick Access, use the updated pages to validate designs and settings, but do not infer a new release or changed service behavior from documentation updates alone.

Review the affected paths if you use External ID customer sign-in or SSPR, Global Secure Access or Internet Access filtering, AI Gateway security capabilities, or Lifecycle Workflows. The numerous updated partner provisioning and SSO pages should be rechecked for integrations you operate, but their status and summaries do not demonstrate new connectors or changed provisioning behavior. Preserve the documented preview, additional-cost, and admin-center-versus-Graph distinctions in implementation plans.

2026-03-02.overview: This was a maintenance-heavy period rather than a broad release wave: 111 items were updated and 8 were new. The clearest operational change is the Microsoft 365 Message Center notice for expanded AI Administrator permissions in Agent 365, with rollout starting in March 2026. Microsoft says the AI Administrator role is updated to support Agent 365, enabling delegated agent management without Global Administrator involvement for routine tasks. The expanded scope includes agent lifecycle management, tenant-wide consent except Microsoft Graph app permissions, and risk monitoring through Identity Protection. Rollout starts in March 2026; no more precise date is supplied.

keyChanges.detail: When Global Secure Access is deployed as a cloud-based network proxy, Secure Service Edge infrastructure routes user traffic. 2026-03-09.headline: Application Proxy and Global Secure Access dominate the week’s documentation refresh; Agent ID adds new AI-guided setup documentation
2026-03-09.overview: The week of 9 March was primarily a Microsoft Learn maintenance and expansion cycle: 103 entries, including 5 new pages and 98 updates, with no removals or Message Center notices. The most consequential content is a coordinated refresh for Microsoft Entra application proxy and a broad set of Global Secure Access, Internet Access, and Private Access deployment and inspection guides. Application Proxy owners can compare current deployment, connector, certificate, assignment, and publishing procedures with the revised guidance. The evidence supports review where these capabilities are in use, not a blanket configuration change.

2026-03-23.headline: Security Copilot’s E5 rollout and My Groups enhancements headline a documentation-heavy Entra week

keyChanges.detail: The updated policy guidance says Windows 11, version 23H2, with KB5034848 or later no longer needs a Conditional Access exclusion intended to avoid the authentication prompt. 2026-04-20.headline: Cross-tenant group sync, Account Discovery, and automatic passkey campaign updates lead a documentation-heavy week
2026-04-20.overview: The week of 20 April 2026 was mostly low-impact documentation maintenance: 97 Microsoft Learn entries were updated, with no items marked new or removed, alongside three Message Center notices. Those notices carry the substantive rollout information: ID Governance cross-tenant security group synchronization is in public preview with general availability announced by the end of May; ID Governance Account Discovery is an off-by-default public preview with general availability beginning in August; and Entra ID Registration Campaigns will receive automatic Passkeys (FIDO2) updates worldwide from mid-May through late June. The other notable material is documentation or security guidance around Agent ID backup and recovery, PIM, authentication, and MFA—not evidence of additional launches or retirements.

If adopting cross-tenant group synchronization, the notice says to enable it through attribute mappings and access policies; Account Discovery requires administrator opt-in and otherwise has no user impact; and the passkey campaign notice says no immediate action is required because eligible tenants are updated automatically. Treat the Learn edits as reference or security guidance rather than assuming they changed tenant settings or enforcement.

keyChanges.title: Stricter federated sign-in validation begins in mid-August 2026

keyChanges.detail: Starting in June 2026, Microsoft Entra will enable App Instance Lock by default for new applications. This is a changed provisioning default, not a retroactive change to existing applications.
