keyChanges.detail: The 25 June notice says Excel Power Query is changing its Organizational Accounts authentication flow for Microsoft Entra ID. Excel 2021 version 21.08 or older must be updated to build 16.0.14334.20754 or later by 24 July 2026, or upgraded to a newer Excel version, to avoid authentication loss. Microsoft 365 and newer Excel versions are stated to be unaffected. This is a client update dependency, not a tenant-side Entra feature launch.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Excel Power Query

keyChanges.title: Changed behavior: Teams for the web will respect Entra KMSI
keyChanges.detail: The 26 June notice says Teams for the web will respect Microsoft Entra ID Keep Me Signed In settings starting in late June 2026. A session persists only when the user chooses to stay signed in; otherwise, the session clears when the browser closes. Microsoft explicitly says no immediate action is required. The practical change is in session persistence, particularly on shared devices.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Teams for the web

keyChanges.title: Upcoming Conditional Access enforcement change has insufficient detail for remediation
keyChanges.detail: The 23 June Message Center entry flags an upcoming change described as improved enforcement for Conditional Access policies with resource exclusions. The supplied record includes no effective date, affected resource types, or before-and-after enforcement semantics. It is a watch item, but this evidence does not support a specific policy edit or impact assessment.

keyChanges.title: Security and resilience documentation expands for recovery and Global Secure Access operations
keyChanges.detail: A new Plan for tenant recoverability page covers tenant-scoped recovery under the shared responsibility model. Related updates address deletion impact, supported objects and attributes, object recovery, and difference reports; the documentation says Backup Reader can review difference reports, while Backup Administrator can review and create them, and Global Administrator includes those permissions. The updated application-secret recovery page is explicitly labeled Preview. New Global Secure Access PowerShell pages
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID Backup and Recovery; Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access

2026-06-29.headline: Entra will block new Partner Tier1/Tier2 Support assignments on 3 August; Global Secure Access guidance expands
2026-06-29.overview: The period’s clearest administrator-impacting change is a Microsoft Entra retirement notice: new assignments to the Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support roles will be blocked starting 3 August 2026, while existing assignments remain valid. The Learn entries are otherwise predominantly procedural or reference maintenance, with a connected set of Global Secure Access tutorials, substantive ID Protection risk-signal documentation, and OIDC security guidance as the main exceptions. The supplied evidence does not identify a general-availability release for those new pages; HTTP method request filtering is explicitly marked preview. The removed Entra Customer Lockbox Approver item is identified only as a page removal, not as evidence of a corresponding capability retirement.
2026-06-29.adminImpact: If these partner roles are used, update scripts that make future assignments and select alternatives such as User Administrator before 3 August. Existing assignments remain valid, and tenants that do not use the roles are unaffected. Use the new Global Secure Access pages as configuration and validation procedures, but do not treat their new-document status as proof of a launch or GA availability; treat HTTP method filtering as preview. Analysts using ID Protection reports should account for the documented correlation of signals and the risky-user report aggregation option, without assuming a new policy requirement. Application owners should review SPA registrations that rely on implicit grant against the documented authorization-code-with-PKCE guidance; the evidence does not say that En.{

keyChanges.title: Partner support-role retirement changes future assignments
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra’s Message Center notice says the Partner Tier1 and Partner Tier2 Support roles are being retired. Starting 3 August 2026, new assignments will be blocked, but existing assignments remain valid. The notice specifically calls for updating scripts and using alternatives such as User Administrator; tenants that do not use these roles are unaffected. This is the period’s concrete retirement and behavior change.

keyChanges.title: New Global Secure Access tutorials document a connected Microsoft-traffic configuration path
keyChanges.detail: New tutorials cover enabling the Microsoft traffic profile, assigning users, installing the client, and verifying traffic forwarding; enabling source IP restoration and checking Microsoft Entra sign-in logs; requiring a compliant network through Conditional Access; and configuring universal tenant restrictions. A separate Microsoft traffic labs tutorial groups source IP restoration, compliant network checks, and tenant restrictions. These are procedural Learn additions, not an announced GA release or product launch

keyChanges.title: HTTP method request filtering is documented as a preview control
keyChanges.detail: An updated Global Secure Access web-content-filtering page explicitly lists HTTP method request filtering as preview, with GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE as examples of methods that can be blocked or allowed. Related content-policy documentation describes real-time protection for file and text content. No GA date or broader availability statement is supplied.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection documents compounded user risk across Microsoft security signals
keyChanges.detail: New and updated ID Protection pages describe unified risk signals: correlated identity-risk signals from Entra ID Protection, Microsoft Defender, and other Microsoft security products are evaluated within the same time window to calculate a compounded user-risk score. The Risky User Report update documents an `Aggregate risk signals by risky sign-ins` option, and the dashboard documentation carries the same model. The record does not label this as preview or GA.

keyChanges.title: OIDC documentation adds an extensibility map and reinforces authorization-code guidance
keyChanges.detail: A new OIDC extensibility reference maps each Microsoft identity platform OIDC extensibility surface to the relevant configuration article and Microsoft Graph resource. Related Entra ID updates say the implicit-flow ID-token manifest flag defaults to false, discourage implicit grant even for JavaScript SPAs, and recommend authorization code flow with PKCE; OIDC setup guidance also reiterates adding a redirect URI. This is security and developer guidance, not an announced protocol-enforcement change.

2026-07-06.headline: Custom Controls retirement sets a September 2026 deadline to move affected Conditional Access policies to External MFA
2026-07-06.overview: During the week of 6 July 2026, the strongest administrator signal is a Conditional Access lifecycle change rather than a broad Entra feature launch. Custom Controls are scheduled to retire by May 2027, with policy migration to External MFA required by September 2026; system-preferred authentication also now applies to first-factor sign-in for tenants in the Microsoft-managed state. The other substantial thread is passkey operations: new and revised guidance spans synced passkeys, Authenticator, FIDO2, and Windows Hello, with the Windows path explicitly in preview. An iOS Authenticator restore improvement is scheduled worldwide for August, while Dynamics 365 Contact Center user management through Entra security groups has an explicit 24 July general availability date. The remaining supplied items are mostly how-to, troubleshooting, migration, licensing, or maintenance documentation.
2026-07-06.adminImpact: The clearest near-term task is to migrate affected Conditional Access policies from Custom Controls to External MFA by September 2026; the retirement target is May 2027. For tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, decide whether to keep or change system-preferred authentication and update user guidance, because first-factor sign-in now selects the most secure registered method. Use the passkey registration, sign-in, and Conditional Access loop guidance where relevant, but do not infer general availability from documentation updates; the Windows path remains preview. The iOS restore notice explicitly requires no administrator changes or action.

keyChanges.title: Retirement: Conditional Access Custom Controls move to External MFA
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center major update says Entra ID will retire Custom Controls in Conditional Access by May 2027. Administrators must migrate policies by September 2026, replacing Custom Controls with External MFA for standardized third-party MFA integration. This is an explicit retirement and migration notice, not a new-feature or general availability announcement.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — Conditional Access and External MFA

keyChanges.title: Changed behavior: system-preferred authentication now covers first-factor sign-in
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra now applies system-preferred authentication to first-factor sign-in for tenants in the Microsoft-managed state and selects the most secure registered method. The notice says rollout starts in late June 2026; tenants can keep or change the setting and should update user guidance. This is a changed authentication behavior, not a new authentication method.

keyChanges.title: Passkeys: new and revised operating guidance, with Windows explicitly in preview
keyChanges.detail: New and updated Microsoft Learn pages cover enabling, registering, and signing in with synced passkeys; Microsoft Authenticator on Android and iOS; FIDO2 security keys; and backup and restore when moving Authenticator to a new phone. The Windows-specific Entra passkey flow uses Windows Hello as a FIDO2 passkey provider and is labeled preview. A related External ID troubleshooting update warns that a phishing-resistant authentication-strength Conditional Access policy scoped to All resources can loop when a userAdds
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / External ID — Passkeys and Conditional Access

keyChanges.title: Authenticator passkey restore on iOS is scheduled for worldwide August availability
keyChanges.detail: Message Center describes a clearer, guided device-migration flow for restoring Microsoft Authenticator passkeys on iOS for users with iCloud backups. It will be available worldwide in August 2026, is enabled by default, and requires no administrator changes or action. This is a user-experience rollout, not a tenant configuration change.

keyChanges.title: General availability: Dynamics 365 Contact Center user management through Entra security groups
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announced that managing Dynamics 365 Contact Center users through Microsoft Entra security groups will reach general availability on 24 July 2026. This is a GA milestone for that Contact Center integration; the supplied message does not state additional Entra configuration steps.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — Security groups / Dynamics 365 Contact Center

2026-07-13.headline: Passkeys default in September; SMS/voice and SharePoint OTP retirements set Entra’s agenda
2026-07-13.overview: The period is dominated by two concrete authentication retirements and a related default change: Microsoft Entra says passkeys become the default on September 1, 2026, Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire on February 1, 2027, and SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication retires in October 2026 as external sharing transitions to Entra B2B. The other substantive thread is Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Global Secure Access Explicit Forward Proxy: this week’s Learn content documents PAC-based deployment and Entra/Conditional Access session controls, with HTTP-header session management marked preview. Microsoft also says Purview DLP network-layer filtering is targeted for general availability by September 2026. The remaining supplied Learn entries—RBAC and token reference, Lifecycle Workflows procedures, Netskope provisioning, Linux troubleshooting, and SLA data—are ordinary documentation maintenance; their summaries do not establish additional launches, behavior changes, or required configuration.
2026-07-13.adminImpact: Treat the authentication and external-sharing notices as the planning priorities. For SMS/voice, the Message Center notice says customers must configure telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store or risk disruption; the companion Learn page focuses on migrating users to passkeys. For SharePoint, the notice says new external sharing has used Entra B2B since May 2026, external users need guest accounts, and admins should update policies and manage those accounts. For Explicit Forward Proxy deployments, the guidance says Conditional Access is not required but recommends restricting use to trusted networks and using Conditional Access to assign Internet Access security profiles; HTTP-header session management is preview. The DLP notice says policy controls are managed through Purก์

keyChanges.title: Passkeys become the default while Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire
keyChanges.detail: This Entra ID change combines a behavior change with a retirement. Passkeys become the default authentication method on September 1, 2026, while Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire on February 1, 2027. Customers using SMS or voice must configure telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store or risk disruption. The notice describes passkeys as phishing-resistant and available at no extra cost; the new Learn page provides migration and preparation guidance.

keyChanges.title: SharePoint OTP transitions to Microsoft Entra B2B
keyChanges.detail: The External ID notice sets October 2026 as the retirement point for SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication. It says new external sharing has used Microsoft Entra B2B since May 2026, and external users need guest accounts for access. The stated administrator preparation is to update policies and manage those guest accounts.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra External ID / Microsoft Entra B2B

keyChanges.title: Explicit Forward Proxy documentation broadens the deployment and security playbook
keyChanges.detail: The supplied Internet Access and Global Secure Access entries describe using Explicit Forward Proxy without the Global Secure Access client in PAC-capable browsers, hosting custom PAC files, delivering proxy and certificate-authority trust settings to Edge through Intune MAM, and using manual or DHCP/WPAD configuration for unmanaged devices. The session model uses Entra authentication and authorization, Conditional Access, passkeys, and Continuous Access Evaluation; basic, digest, NTLM, and Kerberos proxy author­
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access / Global Secure Access

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP integration receives a preview-to-GA timeline
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center item describes Microsoft Purview DLP integrating with Entra Global Secure Access Internet Access to filter sensitive files at the network layer and prevent leaks to unmanaged cloud apps. Its stated timeline places public preview in mid-November 2025 and general availability by September 2026. Administrators can create granular policies through Purview and Defender; the period’s notice is not evidence that general availability has already occurred.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access / Global Secure Access

keyChanges.title: Admin control for SSO prompts is documented for managed Windows devices
keyChanges.detail: A new Entra ID Learn page says IT administrators can automatically accept SSO permissions on managed Windows devices through a supported registry setting. The supplied entry provides no rollout date or preview/GA status, so it should be treated as a newly documented control rather than a dated product-launch announcement.

2026-07-20.headline: Passkey GA and automatic FIDO2 migration lead the period, with network-layer DLP close behind
2026-07-20.overview: Authentication is the period’s main story, but the notices describe a mix of already-dated GA statuses and staged future rollouts rather than one July launch. Entra passkey profiles and synced passkeys are moving to GA for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled, with existing configurations migrating through October. Windows passkeys are described as GA from late April, while passwordless password change is scheduled for late October and remains disabled by default. External ID documentation clarifies future SMS and voice retirement scope for B2B and internal guest users. Separately, Microsoft Purview DLP is rolling network-layer inspection and protection through Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access) from July to October. The remaining Learn work is mostly maintenance or clarification; the new GSA egress-range and Databricks SCIM pages are operational references, not evidence of new service launches.
2026-07-20.adminImpact: Existing Passkeys (FIDO2) configurations and registration campaigns are subject to the stated regional migration. Windows passkeys are controlled through Authentication Methods policies and Conditional Access; the notice says no action is needed unless blocking is desired. The My Sign-Ins passwordless password-change capability remains off until an administrator activates it, while the SSPR CAPTCHA replacement requires no user or administrator action. The DLP rollout is cross-product, affecting Purview, Entra, and Defender administrators, but the supplied notice gives no specific configuration task. For External ID, the evidence establishes the affected user populations and planned passkey timing, not a retirement date or migration procedure. Learn updates are mostly documentation: the GSA

keyChanges.title: Passkey profiles and synced passkeys reach GA with automatic FIDO2-tenant migration
keyChanges.detail: The July 21 Message Center major update describes GA beginning in March 2026 for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled. Existing configurations migrate to a Default passkey profile with a new `passkeyType` property, while automatic migration and registration-campaign changes roll out regionally through October 2026. Because the schedule is already underway, this is a GA and migration update rather than a new July launch.

keyChanges.title: Windows passkeys are GA; passwordless password change is a separate, later admin-enabled capability
keyChanges.detail: The Windows passkey notice places Entra passkeys on Windows in GA from late April 2026, without explicit opt-in, for corporate, personal, and shared devices. Authentication Methods policies and Conditional Access are the stated admin controls. Separately, passwordless users will be able to change passwords in My Sign-Ins with passkeys or Windows Hello, without the current password or SSPR; that capability is disabled by default, requires admin activation, and is scheduled for global rollout in late October 2026.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Windows passkeys and My Sign-Ins

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP is extending to the network layer through Entra Internet Access
keyChanges.detail: The major update describes Microsoft Purview DLP integrating with Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access) to inspect and protect sensitive data at the network layer, including in AI interactions and cloud services. The stated capabilities include policy enforcement, alerts, and auditing, with rollout scheduled from July through October 2026. It explicitly affects Purview, Entra, and Defender administrators, but the supplied summary does not provide additional configuration steps.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access) / Microsoft Purview DLP

keyChanges.title: External ID documentation clarifies SMS and voice retirement scope for B2B and internal guests
keyChanges.detail: An updated External ID page says B2B users and internal guest users are included in the retirement scope for Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication. It also says passkey support for those users is planned by the end of calendar year 2026. This is a future-scope clarification, not evidence that the retirement or passkey support completed during this period; no migration procedure or retirement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: SSPR is replacing legacy CAPTCHA with backend abuse controls
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in early August 2026, Microsoft Entra self-service password reset is scheduled to replace its legacy CAPTCHA with backend throttling and behavior-based abuse detection. The notice says current password-reset functionality remains, no new controls are introduced, and neither users nor administrators need to act. This is a security and accessibility behavior change, not a new admin feature to configure.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Self-service password reset

2026-07-27.headline: Custom-branding CSS retirement and SMS/voice authentication phase-out lead the week
2026-07-27.overview: The week of 27 July 2026 is driven more by retirements, security guidance, and changed behavior than by a broad feature launch. Microsoft Entra ID has a Message Center retirement for custom CSS positioning in company branding beginning October 2026. Updated guidance prepares public-cloud tenants for the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication and migration to passkeys. A separate Conditional Access notice describes stronger enforcement for certain narrow-scope sign-ins. Workload ID guidance moves GitHub Actions federated credentials toward immutable subjects. ID Governance also received substantial Tenant Governance guidance covering snapshots, configuration drift monitoring, related-tenant signals, and a Microsoft Graph preview; the supplied evidence does not establish a new GA launch for those documentation updates.
2026-07-27.adminImpact: Treat the branding and authentication items as planning work: identify custom CSS positioning properties, assess public-cloud users who still rely on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice authentication, and review GitHub Actions federated credentials that use mutable subjects. Evaluate custom applications requesting only the OIDC or directory scopes covered by the Conditional Access notice. If adopting Tenant Governance, review the application permissions and roles required for snapshots and monitors, and note that the Graph-related capability is marked preview. The passkey-registration optimization notice says organizations need no action; the other tenant-architecture, workflow, and setup changes are documentation guidance rather than confirmed service changes.

keyChanges.title: Custom branding CSS positioning properties retire in October 2026
keyChanges.detail: This Microsoft 365 Message Center major update affects Microsoft Entra ID company branding, not just documentation. Support for custom CSS positioning properties is scheduled to retire starting October 2026. Existing users must remove those properties; there is no migration path, and branding elements may remain visible but revert to default placement. Administrators should inventory affected branding configurations and plan their removal before the stated deadline.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication guidance shifts users toward passkeys
keyChanges.detail: An updated Microsoft Entra ID article explains how to prepare for retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication and migrate users to passkeys. The supplied timeline clarification applies to public cloud only; other cloud environments will follow later schedules with advance communications. Separately, a Message Center notice says passkey registration optimizations across Registration Campaign, Authentication Strengths, and My Sign-Ins will roll out in late August 2026, prioritize local-device passk​

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access enforcement changes for policies with resource exclusions
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice says that, starting June 15, 2026, Conditional Access policies targeting All resources with exclusions are enforced for sign-ins requesting only certain OIDC or directory scopes. Some users may encounter new challenges such as MFA. Most organizations need no action, but custom applications that request only the affected scopes should be evaluated. This is a changed-behavior notice, not a new Conditional Access feature launch.

keyChanges.title: GitHub Actions federated credentials should use immutable subjects
keyChanges.detail: New and updated Workload ID security guidance explains that mutable OIDC subject claims expose federated identity credentials to subject recycling, while immutable claims reduce that risk. For GitHub Actions, the guidance covers migrating to GitHub's immutable subject format and creating a separate credential for each subject a workflow presents, such as a branch or environment. Organizations using these credentials should review their current subject configuration; no migration deadline is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Governance documentation adds snapshots, drift monitoring, and related-tenant investigation
keyChanges.detail: New and updated ID Governance guidance now covers creating configuration snapshots for baselines or audit evidence, configuring monitors to evaluate a baseline and report drift, viewing monitor results, and assigning the service permissions and roles needed for those operations. Related-tenant guidance also explains how to use Microsoft Graph in preview to retrieve the users and applications behind tenant-discovery signals. These entries document an operational workflow and a preview API; they are not evidence of a

2026-08-03.headline: MemberOf retirement and MFA deadlines reshape Entra access administration
2026-08-03.overview: The week’s most consequential changes are deadline-driven: Microsoft Entra ID will retire the MemberOf rule operator on November 3, 2026; SMS and voice MFA guidance sets a September 1, 2026 passkey transition and a February 1, 2027 service cutoff for tenants without a customer-managed telecom provider; and SSPR will require explicitly registered methods from November 9, 2026, following a registration campaign beginning October 5. Two new security guides cover capabilities that remain in preview: the Global Secure Access MCP firewall and web-app Token Protection. Most other activity clarified provisioning navigation, labels, and terminology rather than introducing product behavior changes.
2026-08-03.adminImpact: Inventory and replace MemberOf rules before the November deadline, including rules used by dynamic groups, administrative units, and entitlement policies. Review users relying on SMS or voice MFA and plan migration, the documented temporary opt-out, or a customer-managed provider; also prepare users for the SSPR registration campaign and its November enforcement date. Preview evaluations require the documented Global Secure Access roles, Internet Access license, joined device, and TLS inspection for the MCP firewall, while Token Protection guidance calls for Microsoft Entra ID P1, supported device setup, report-only mode, and a pilot group. For the many provisioning updates, revise runbooks to match the new portal paths and labels rather than infer a feature migration.

keyChanges.title: MemberOf rules must be replaced before November 3
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID will retire the MemberOf rule operator on November 3, 2026. Rules in dynamic groups, administrative units, and entitlement policies must be replaced to avoid stale access, licensing, and policy-enforcement outcomes.

keyChanges.title: SMS and voice MFA face a two-stage retirement timeline
keyChanges.detail: Updated Entra authentication guidance says passkeys will be automatically enabled for users using SMS or voice on September 1, 2026. From February 1, 2027, tenants without a customer-managed telecom provider will no longer be able to use SMS or voice for MFA. The timeline applies to the public cloud and excludes Azure AD B2C and Entra External ID.

keyChanges.title: SSPR will require explicitly registered methods from November
keyChanges.detail: Starting November 9, 2026, self-service password reset verification will require explicitly registered authentication methods; directory-sourced contact information will not qualify unless it is registered. A user registration campaign begins October 5, 2026.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documents an MCP firewall preview
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to covers configuring the Global Secure Access MCP firewall to inspect, audit, and allow or block supported Model Context Protocol traffic. Controls include MCP servers, primitives, methods, and protocol versions. The firewall is currently in preview and requires the documented roles, Internet Access license, joined device, client, and TLS inspection setup.

keyChanges.title: Token Protection web-app enforcement guidance arrives in preview
keyChanges.detail: A new deployment guide explains Conditional Access Token Protection for supported browser-based applications accessing Azure Resource Manager. Web-app support is limited to listed applications, platforms, browsers, and device configurations and is explicitly in preview; Microsoft Entra ID P1 and additional Windows or macOS device setup are required.

2026-08-10.headline: SMS first-factor sign-in retires for Entra ID Free tenants on August 11
2026-08-10.overview: The week’s biggest administrator deadline was Microsoft’s August 11 retirement of SMS first-factor sign-in for Entra ID Free tenants; SMS used for multifactor authentication remains available. Microsoft also announced first-method passkey and passwordless registration rolling out from October 2026 through February 2027, a September 11 general-availability target for Dynamics 365 Commerce on-behalf-of ordering with Microsoft Entra External ID, and new Global Secure Access V2 migration guidance. Token Protection’s browser-based support is documented as Preview; much of the remaining activity, especially across Agent ID, was terminology, sample, and procedural clarification rather than a launch.
2026-08-10.adminImpact: Prioritize Free-tenant users still relying on SMS first-factor sign-in and move them to another authentication method; do not confuse this retirement with SMS MFA. The passkey-first registration rollout requires no administrator action according to the notice. For Global Secure Access, check security-profile eligibility, use the Global Secure Access Administrator role, review changed V2 evaluation behavior, and manually handle profiles that already contain V2 policies. Administrators evaluating browser-based Token Protection should verify the documented browser, extension, operating-system, and Conditional Access requirements. The External ID notice provides a GA date but no additional required action.

keyChanges.title: SMS first-factor sign-in retirement affects Entra ID Free tenants
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice says Microsoft will retire SMS first-factor sign-in for Entra ID Free tenants on August 11, 2026, because of fraud risks. Users must switch to another authentication method, while SMS as a multifactor method remains unaffected. This is a security-driven retirement, not a documentation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Passkeys can become users’ first multifactor authentication method
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announced that users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method instead of setting up a weaker method first. The change rolls out from October 2026 through February 2027, and the notice says no administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Global Secure Access documents V1-to-V2 web-filtering migration
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to article describes the guided migration experience, including eligible and ineligible security profiles and the conversion of V1 policies into rules within one enabled V2 policy while preserving destinations, actions, and priorities. Profiles that already contain V2 policies require manual handling, and administrators should review changed evaluation behavior across multiple security profiles. This is migration documentation, not evidence of a separate product launch.

keyChanges.title: Token Protection adds documented browser support in Preview
keyChanges.detail: The updated Token Protection page documents Preview support for selected browser-based web apps accessing Azure Resource Manager on Windows and macOS. Browser use on iOS and iPadOS is unsupported; administrators must review the supported browsers, extensions, operating systems, configurations, deployment guidance, and the Windows Azure Service Management API resource used for Conditional Access enforcement.

keyChanges.title: External ID on-behalf-of ordering targets September general availability
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announced that on-behalf-of ordering can be enabled for Microsoft Entra External ID in Dynamics 365 Commerce, with general availability scheduled for September 11, 2026. The announcement does not specify additional administrator action.

2026-08-17.headline: Custom branding CSS retirement sets October deadline for Entra administrators
2026-08-17.overview: The clearest operational deadline is Microsoft Entra’s retirement of custom CSS layout and positioning properties in company branding: new use is blocked from July 21, 2026, and existing branding will revert to default layouts after retirement in late October. Two authentication changes are scheduled for October: B2B users will gain passkey registration and sign-in support, while Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO will count as standalone MFA factors. The period also added actionable preview guidance for clearing null or empty values through inbound provisioning and for securing GitHub flexible federated identity credentials with immutable repository claims.
2026-08-17.adminImpact: Audit company-branding CSS configurations and replace affected layout or positioning properties before the late-October retirement. No configuration change is required for B2B passkeys or standalone MFA recognition, but review MFA policy scopes and update onboarding guidance. For provisioning, enable Flow null values on both source and target mappings only where empty values should clear target data; for GitHub federation, update flexible credentials to include the required immutable repository claims.

keyChanges.title: Company branding CSS layout and positioning properties are being retired
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says new use is blocked from July 21, 2026. Retirement is planned for late October 2026, after which branding reverts to default layouts. Organizations using these properties must update their branding configurations before the deadline.

keyChanges.title: B2B users will receive passkey support for resource-tenant MFA
keyChanges.detail: Passkey registration and sign-in for B2B users will be enabled by default and roll out from October 2026 through February 2027, helping guests meet resource-tenant MFA requirements. No administrator action is required, although Microsoft recommends reviewing user scopes and MFA policies.

keyChanges.title: Windows Hello and macOS Platform SSO become standalone MFA factors
keyChanges.detail: Starting in October 2026, Microsoft Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors, allowing users to satisfy MFA requirements without an additional passkey. No configuration change is needed; onboarding and MFA registration guidance should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Inbound provisioning preview documents opt-in clearing of target attributes
keyChanges.detail: When a source value is null or empty, provisioning can clear the existing target attribute. Administrators must enable “Flow null values” on both the source and target mappings; the behavior supports only single-valued attributes in specified inbound provisioning scenarios.

keyChanges.title: GitHub flexible federated credentials require immutable repository claims
keyChanges.detail: Updated preview guidance requires a GitHub credential to match `sub` plus `repository_id`, `repository_owner_id`, or both. Portal and Microsoft Graph examples now include these claims; administrators configuring trust should use the numeric immutable values from the GitHub OIDC token.

2026-08-24.headline: System-preferred authentication now applies to first-factor sign-ins; My Account moves in November
2026-08-24.overview: Most updates this week were maintenance-level documentation edits involving sample identifiers, links, and formatting. The consequential exceptions are a first-factor authentication behavior rollout, a late-November self-service domain migration, automatic Windows client upgrades for Global Secure Access, a Linux device-trust migration, and enhanced sAMAccountName synchronization guidance.
2026-08-24.adminImpact: For tenants in the Microsoft managed state, review system-preferred authentication and update user guidance. Allow *.cloud.microsoft in network policies before the My Account migration rolls out worldwide in late November 2026. Decide whether eligible Windows Global Secure Access clients may upgrade automatically; if opting out, use the documented installer parameter and maintain updates manually. Update Linux broker upgrade procedures for Entra join, re-enrollment, and device-join permissions. Before enabling sAMAccountName synchronization, review source values and application dependencies.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred authentication reaches first-factor sign-ins
keyChanges.detail: For tenants in the Microsoft managed state, Microsoft Entra now applies system-preferred authentication to first-factor sign-ins, selecting the most secure registered method. Rollout runs from late June through late September 2026; tenants can keep or change the setting and should update user guidance.

keyChanges.title: My Account identity services move to the cloud.microsoft domain
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is moving self-service identity management from myaccount.microsoft.com to myaccount.cloud.microsoft and consolidating related sites. The worldwide rollout is scheduled for late November 2026. Users need no action, but administrators should allow *.cloud.microsoft in network policies.

keyChanges.title: Eligible Windows Global Secure Access clients will auto-upgrade
keyChanges.detail: Starting in November 2026, eligible Windows clients will automatically receive Global Secure Access upgrades through Windows Update. Version 2.32.294 also adds Prefer local network, faster tunnel creation, and other fixes. Administrators who opt out must use the documented installer parameter and maintain updates manually.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Single Sign-on for Linux changes its device-trust model
keyChanges.detail: Beginning with broker version 2.0.2, Microsoft Single Sign-on for Linux uses Microsoft Entra join instead of device registration for device trust. Existing upgraded devices must be re-joined and re-enrolled. Upgrade procedures should remove broker state, reinstall the broker, and re-join devices after allowing users to join devices through Entra device settings.

keyChanges.title: Enhanced synchronization can source hybrid sAMAccountName values
keyChanges.detail: New guidance documents an enhanced synchronization setting that sources hybrid users’ sAMAccountName from onPremisesSamAccountName. Existing domains retain current behavior until enabled; enabling it updates existing hybrid users during synchronization, while cloud-only users without the source value continue using mailNickname-based generation. The setting applies to Enterprise or Premium managed domains and requires Application Administrator and Groups Administrator roles.

2023-09.headline: Entra ID announces a 30 September 2025 retirement deadline for legacy MFA and SSPR method management
2023-09.overview: September’s supplied record contains one consequential change: a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update issued on 29 September 2023. Microsoft says administrators will no longer be able to manage authentication methods through the legacy Multifactor Authentication (MFA) and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) policies after 30 September 2025. This is a forward-looking retirement notice, not evidence of an immediate behavior change, new feature launch, preview, or general-availability milestone.
2023-09.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to move authentication methods managed in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies to Entra ID’s converged Authentication methods policy before the deadline. Microsoft describes the converged policy as the central management point for passwordless, multifactor authentication, and SSPR scenarios. The supplied notice does not provide migration steps or technical prerequisites, so more specific implementation guidance cannot be inferred.

keyChanges.title: Management is moving from separate legacy policies to the converged Authentication methods policy
keyChanges.detail: The announced retirement changes where authentication methods are managed: the legacy MFA and SSPR policies will lose that management capability on 30 September 2025, while Microsoft directs organizations to the converged Authentication methods policy for centralized management across passwordless, MFA, and SSPR scenarios.

2023-12.headline: Entra ID FIDO2 registration may now offer cross-device passkey creation
2023-12.overview: December’s substantive Entra change was a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about the FIDO2 security key registration experience. During registration, users may see an operating system- or browser-generated prompt to create a passkey on another device, such as a phone or tablet; some users may instead see a QR code. The supplied evidence does not identify a preview or general-availability milestone, policy change, retirement, or required administrator action.
2023-12.adminImpact: The impact is primarily to the user and support experience. Administrators and support teams should recognize the cross-device passkey prompt or QR code as an expected possibility during FIDO2 registration. No configuration change, migration, or mandatory action is identified in the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 registration can present a cross-device passkey flow
keyChanges.detail: The registration experience may invoke a prompt generated by the operating system or browser to create a passkey on another device, including a phone or tablet. In some cases, a QR code facilitates that flow. This is a behavior change in registration—not evidence of a new policy, rollout milestone, or administrative requirement.

2024-01.headline: India-specific removal of WhatsApp-delivered MFA text messages was the only January Entra ID change
2024-01.overview: The supplied January 2024 data contains one Entra ID item: a 26 January Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about removing MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India. This is a service-change communication, not a new feature, preview, general-availability announcement, or documentation update. No new, updated, or removed Entra feature or documentation items were recorded.
2024-01.adminImpact: Organizations without users in India can safely disregard the notice. Organizations with users in India should determine whether they rely on this MFA delivery route. The supplied evidence does not provide an effective date, replacement method, or specific migration task, so no further action can be inferred.

keyChanges.title: Removal of MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft 365 Message Center announced the removal of this India-specific authentication delivery route. Administrators with affected users should assess current reliance on it; the available evidence does not state when the removal takes effect or what replacement method is provided.

2024-02.headline: Entra ID plans a mid-March preview of device-bound passkeys, with FIDO2 policy and sign-in changes
2024-02.overview: February’s substantive Entra item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice, not a general-availability announcement or a documentation clarification. It says Microsoft Entra ID will begin preview support in mid-March 2024 for device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices, alongside existing FIDO2 security-key support. The change also introduces FIDO2 policy handling requirements and broadens end-user sign-in terminology.
2024-02.adminImpact: Administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow the passkey providers they intend to support. They should also expect the Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in option to be renamed and the sign-in experience to use broader passkey terminology. The notice does not state that existing FIDO2 security-key support is being retired or that migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Device-bound passkeys enter preview as an additional authentication method
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-March 2024, Microsoft Entra ID is expected to support passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices in preview. This adds to, rather than replaces, the existing support for FIDO2 security keys; the supplied notice does not describe this as a general-availability release.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 key restrictions will control permitted passkey providers
keyChanges.detail: The notice says administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow specified passkey providers. It does not identify the providers or provide additional policy parameters.

keyChanges.title: Windows Hello and FIDO2 sign-in wording becomes broader
keyChanges.detail: The end-user option for Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 security keys will be renamed to “Face, fingerprint, PIN, or security key.” The updated experience will also mention “passkey” so the terminology covers credentials presented from security keys, computers, and mobile devices.
keyChanges.product: Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in experience

2024-03.headline: March 2024: Entra consent administration shifts to new Teams controls and the Entra portal as legacy interfaces retire
2024-03.overview: March’s supplied Entra record consists of Microsoft 365 Message Center notices rather than documentation changes. The main operational theme is consent control migration: Teams and chat resource-specific consent settings are rolling out while legacy Group owner and Chat RSC interfaces retire, and the tenant-wide user-consent setting is leaving the Microsoft 365 admin center for the Entra portal. The other notices cover Entra PIM in public preview in the Power Platform admin center and changed Copilot welcome-email behavior for licenses assigned through PowerShell or the Entra admin center.
2024-03.adminImpact: Use the Entra portal for tenant-wide user-consent policy after the Microsoft 365 admin-center retirement; existing settings remain unchanged and no preparation is required for that transition. Teams administrators or automation that depend on the retiring consent settings or APIs should account for the new Microsoft Graph PowerShell-managed settings as rollout reaches all tenants by April 14. Treat the Power Platform PIM capability as preview. If Copilot licenses are assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center, organizations can adjust direct-communication preferences there, while individual users can change their own settings through security and privacy controls.

keyChanges.title: Teams and chat app consent gets new resource-specific controls
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Teams are introducing teams- and chat-specific consent settings for Team RSC and Chat RSC. The existing Group owner consent settings and API, along with the existing Chat RSC API, will be retired. The new settings are managed with Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets, and Teams-level administrators can manage them independently. The rollout began taking effect on March 7 and is scheduled to reach all tenants by April 14. The notice describes a staged service change, not a preview or a
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Teams

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 admin-center user-consent control retires
keyChanges.detail: The User consent to Apps setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center will be retired in early April. This changes the administration surface rather than the policy itself: existing settings remain unchanged, but administrators will no longer be able to edit the tenant-wide policy there. The Entra portal is the replacement location, and the notice says no preparation is required.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM is in public preview in the Power Platform admin center
keyChanges.detail: The March notice announces public preview of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management in the Power Platform admin center, while noting that the capability was already available there on February 5. It brings Entra PIM’s ability to manage, control, and monitor access into that administrative context. This is a preview announcement, not evidence of general availability or a new March launch.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Power Platform admin center

keyChanges.title: Copilot welcome emails extend to licenses assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center
keyChanges.detail: During a late-March through late-April rollout, end users assigned Copilot for Microsoft 365 licenses through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center will automatically receive a welcome email when direct communications from Microsoft are enabled. Organizations can change communication preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and individuals can change their own through security and privacy settings. This is a change in email behavior, not a reported licensing or provisioning migration.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Copilot for Microsoft 365

2024-05.headline: May 2024: Workload ID key disablement creates an urgent June deadline, alongside passkey, PIM, and Dataverse changes
2024-05.overview: The supplied May record is announcement-led: four Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no supplied documentation additions, updates, or removals. The most consequential change is the required replacement of symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Other notices cover a staged passkey-related behavior improvement, general availability of Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform, and a Dataverse cleanup capability entering public preview.
2024-05.adminImpact: Organizations using symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals must replace them with asymmetric keys by June 15, 2024, or risk authentication failures. No preparation is required for the passkey rollout, although relevant user documentation may need updating. PIM is available for time-bounded tenant admin roles, while the Dataverse cleanup capability is preview functionality and is not described as mandatory.

keyChanges.title: Symmetric keys for first-party service principals will be disabled
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announced a security-related behavior change for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Organizations must switch from symmetric to asymmetric keys by June 15, 2024, to avoid authentication failures.

keyChanges.title: Authentication-strength improvements begin supporting device-stored passkeys
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is rolling out new authentication-strength support for passkeys stored on devices. Users will see additional registration options in My Security Info as the rollout proceeds from mid-May through early August 2024. No preparation is required, though administrators may update relevant documentation.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Beginning May 23, administrators can use Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management to assign Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform tenant admin roles for a defined period. The announcement does not identify additional prerequisites, migration work, or configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Dataverse user cleanup enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: Beginning May 1, the preview provides the ability to delete disabled-status users from Dataverse environments, including delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Microsoft cites privacy and regulatory requirements and storage reduction as intended benefits; the supplied evidence does not make deletion mandatory or specify eligibility and configuration details.

2024-07.headline: Insider Risk in Conditional Access reaches GA; Entitlement Management will enforce approvals for privileged administrators
2024-07.overview: July’s supplied record is sparse and message-center-led, with no new, updated, or removed documentation items. Its clearest capability change is the general availability of the Insider Risk condition in Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, using Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection signals. The supplied July 29 brief also reports an automatic Entitlement Management behavior change effective August 26. A July roundup flags Azure AD Graph retirement and Apple/older-Windows updates, but does not provide enough detail for migration or compatibility guidance.
2024-07.adminImpact: Organizations need an Entra ID P2 license and Adaptive Protection enabled to use the Insider Risk condition; eligible tenants can configure policies as rollout proceeds from early July through early August 2024. The Entitlement Management change requires no preparation according to the supplied notice, but Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators should expect configured access-package approval requirements to apply to them. The Azure AD Graph reference supports follow-up validation, not a specific deadline or migration action.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk condition in Conditional Access reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can use insider-risk signals from Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection to enforce policy actions according to user risk levels. This is a generally available capability, not a preview. Use requires Adaptive Protection and an Entra ID P2 license, with rollout stated to begin in early July 2024 and complete by early August 2024.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access / Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management will stop privileged-role bypass of access-package approvals
keyChanges.detail: Starting August 26, 2024, the supplied notice says access package policy approval settings will be enforced for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators. This is a behavior change: those roles will no longer bypass configured approval requirements. The notice says the change is automatic and requires no organizational action.

keyChanges.title: Azure AD Graph retirement is flagged without migration detail
keyChanges.detail: The July 12 “What’s new in Microsoft Entra – June 2024” message names Azure AD Graph retirement and also mentions unspecified GA releases, Apple-device security enhancements, and changes affecting older Windows builds. It provides no retirement date, affected versions, feature names, or required action, so these references should be treated as lifecycle signals rather than a complete migration or compatibility advisory.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD Graph

2024-08.headline: Tenant MFA deadline leads August: privileged approval bypass ends and Edge mobile Copilot retires
2024-08.overview: August’s supplied Entra record is operational rather than documentation-led: all seven entries are Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no new, updated, or removed documentation items. The highest-impact item is the requirement to enable tenant MFA by 15 October 2024 to preserve access to three admin centers. Two other behavior changes affect users and privileged administrators: Copilot in Edge mobile retires for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August, and Entitlement Management will enforce access-package approvals for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators from 26 August. The remaining substantive notices are general-availability rollouts for ID Protection detection, AD FS application migration, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux device-based Conditional Access.
2024-08.adminImpact: Enable MFA before 15 October, or use the stated postponement option if necessary; without it, access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center will be restricted. No pre-rollout action is stated for the general-availability notices or the automatic Entitlement Management change, but administrators should expect configured access-package approval requirements to apply to the two named privileged roles. For the Edge retirement, Microsoft recommends informing users and pointing them to the Microsoft 365 mobile app for work or web chat. The separate Dynamics 365 deletion notice confirms availability but provides too little detail to support a cleanup or configuration recommendation.

keyChanges.title: Tenant MFA is required for admin-portal access by 15 October
keyChanges.detail: This is security-enforcement guidance, not a new capability: tenants must enable MFA by 15 October 2024 to access the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. The notice says tenants may set up MFA early or apply to postpone enforcement; without MFA, administrative access will be restricted.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management removes privileged-administrator approval bypass
keyChanges.detail: This behavior change takes effect on 26 August 2024: Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators can no longer bypass the approval settings configured in access package policies. Microsoft describes the update as automatic and says no organizational action is needed.

keyChanges.title: Copilot in Edge mobile is retired for Entra ID users
keyChanges.detail: This is a retirement, not a rollout: Copilot leaves the Microsoft Edge mobile application for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August 2024. No admin action is required, but Microsoft recommends informing affected users and directing them to the Microsoft 365 mobile app for work or to web chat.

keyChanges.title: Attacker in the Middle detection reaches general availability in ID Protection
keyChanges.detail: The security detection feature is scheduled to reach general availability by late August 2024. Its detection alert is intended to identify compromised user accounts in Microsoft Entra ID Protection. The notice states that no admin action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: AD FS migration and RHEL device-based Conditional Access reach general availability
keyChanges.detail: The AD FS application migration wizard reaches general availability in mid-to-late August and provides a guided experience for migrating AD FS relying-party applications. Device-based Conditional Access for Microsoft 365 and Azure on Red Hat Enterprise Linux also goes generally available, including Entra ID registration, Conditional Access, SSO, Intune compliance, and Red Hat RPM package support. Neither notice requires action before rollout.

2024-09.headline: Tenant MFA deadline is September’s key Entra action; FIDO2 provisioning APIs enter public preview
2024-09.overview: The supplied September activity consists of two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices for Entra ID, both focused on authentication. The immediate operational requirement is to enable tenant MFA by October 15, 2024, for access to the Microsoft Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. Separately, FIDO2 provisioning APIs entered public preview, with rollout scheduled from mid- to late September. No supplied item reports a generally available release, retirement, or documentation change.
2024-09.adminImpact: Prioritize tenant MFA readiness before October 15. Postponement is possible, but administrators who sign in without MFA will be prompted to register, changing the sign-in experience for the named admin centers. The FIDO2 API rollout requires no administrator action; the supplied notice provides no configuration, eligibility, or migration requirements, and the capability should be treated as a preview rather than as generally available.

keyChanges.title: Tenant MFA deadline for administrative access
keyChanges.detail: The September 14 action notice asks organizations to enable MFA for the tenant by October 15, 2024, to access the Microsoft Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. This is a time-bound administrative requirement, not a new product launch.

keyChanges.title: Admins without MFA will be prompted to register at sign-in
keyChanges.detail: The notice states that administrators signing in without MFA will be prompted to register for it. This changes the administrative sign-in experience, although the supplied evidence does not state that access will be blocked outright.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 provisioning APIs move to public preview
keyChanges.detail: The APIs are intended to pre-provision FIDO2 security keys for users, simplifying onboarding and supporting phishing-resistant authentication. Rollout was scheduled to begin in mid-September and finish by late September 2024; no administrator action was required for the rollout, and the capability remains a public preview.

2024-10.headline: October’s concrete change was an Edge Mobile New tab update for Entra ID users; an Entra roundup separately flagged Azure AD Graph retirement and MFA enforcement without operating
2024-10.overview: The period contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices and no recorded new, updated, or removed Entra documentation. The specific user-facing change is in Microsoft Edge Mobile: Wallpaper will be enabled by default and a weather icon will be added for Microsoft Entra ID users. A separate 15 October roundup of the September Microsoft Entra update mentions general-availability releases, Azure AD Graph retirement, Apple-device security enhancements, and MFA enforcement, but supplies no implementation details. This was primarily a communication period rather than a documented Entra feature-release period.
2024-10.adminImpact: No administrator action is required before the Edge Mobile rollout. Administrators should expect the New tab defaults to change for affected Entra ID users, with Wallpaper expected in early October 2024 and the weather icon in late October. The Entra roundup alone does not establish a migration task or MFA change: it does not provide the Azure AD Graph retirement date or scope, the MFA population or schedule, or the Apple-device behavior and prerequisites. Administrators need the referenced release notes, blog, or email material to assess those topics.

keyChanges.title: Edge Mobile enables Wallpaper by default for Entra ID users
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Edge Mobile will update the New tab page for Microsoft Entra ID users by enabling Wallpaper by default. The rollout was expected in early October 2024. This is a client-side default change, not a new Entra ID capability, and the notice says no administrator action is required before rollout.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge Mobile / Microsoft Entra ID users

keyChanges.title: Edge Mobile adds a weather icon to the New tab page
keyChanges.detail: A weather icon will be added to the New tab page for Microsoft Entra ID users, with rollout expected in late October 2024. The supplied notice does not identify a configuration requirement or administrative control and states that no action is required before rollout.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge Mobile / Microsoft Entra ID users

keyChanges.title: A September Entra roundup flags major areas but gives no operational parameters
keyChanges.detail: The 15 October Message Center communication says the September 2024 Microsoft Entra update included general-availability releases, Azure AD Graph retirement, Apple-device security enhancements, and MFA enforcement. It points administrators to blog, email, and release-note material; it is not, by itself, a detailed feature, preview, retirement, or documentation-change record. The supplied evidence does not specify the affected GA releases, retirement date or migration scope, Apple-device behavior, or MFA targets, en

2024-11.headline: Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp for MFA OTP delivery in India in December 2024
2024-11.overview: November’s only supplied change is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Microsoft Entra ID. Beginning in December 2024, users in India who have WhatsApp will receive MFA one-time passcodes through WhatsApp, with SMS as a fallback. Microsoft says the channel will expand to additional countries, but the notice does not identify them or provide timing. It describes a planned channel and behavior change, not a stated preview or general-availability milestone.
2024-11.adminImpact: Review whether WhatsApp-based OTP delivery fits the organization’s authentication policy before the rollout. Administrators can disable the feature or steer users toward stronger methods such as Microsoft Authenticator. The supplied notice does not include configuration steps or a more precise rollout schedule.

keyChanges.title: WhatsApp is reintroduced as an Entra ID MFA OTP delivery channel
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2024, eligible users in India will receive MFA one-time passcodes through WhatsApp, while SMS serves as the fallback channel. Microsoft indicates that the rollout will later expand to more countries, without specifying which countries or when.

2025-01.headline: Entra Authenticator passkeys begin enabling for FIDO2 organizations without key restrictions
2025-01.overview: January’s supplied evidence contains one substantive Entra update: a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID Authentication. Starting in late January 2025, organizations with an enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and no key restrictions will have passkeys available in the Microsoft Authenticator app. The notice describes an enablement, but does not identify the capability as preview or generally available.
2025-01.adminImpact: In the affected configuration, users can add an Authenticator passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, and its use is enforced through Conditional Access. Organizations that do not want this enablement can impose key restrictions. No broader rollout scope or additional administrative steps are supplied.

keyChanges.title: Authenticator passkeys enabled for unrestricted FIDO2 policies
keyChanges.detail: This is an enablement and behavior change rather than a documentation update. Beginning in late January, passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator become available to organizations whose Entra passkey (FIDO2) policy is enabled and does not specify key restrictions. Users can add the passkey from aka.ms/MySecurityInfo; the supplied notice does not classify the capability as preview or generally available.

2025-02.headline: Microsoft Entra is introducing a dedicated Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
2025-02.overview: February 2025 contained one reported Entra change: a February 20 Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement about a new built-in Microsoft Entra role for Viva Glint. The role is intended to let administrators manage Viva Glint settings without Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. Rollout is expected from late March to early April 2025. The supplied period contains no separate Entra documentation updates, retirements, or other product changes, and the announcement does not establish preview or general availability status.
2025-02.adminImpact: Before rollout, administrators should review the role documentation, assess current role assignments, and communicate the change to affected staff. The supplied evidence identifies no migration requirement or additional deployment action.

keyChanges.title: New built-in Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra will add a dedicated role for managing Viva Glint settings, reducing the need to grant Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges for that task. This is an upcoming Message Center-announced change, with rollout expected from late March to early April 2025; its preview or general availability status is not specified.

2025-03.headline: March 2025: plan for the Conditional Access control retirement while ID Protection alerts move to Defender XDR
2025-03.overview: The supplied March record contains three Microsoft 365 Message Center notices and no documentation additions, updates, or removals. The most consequential item is a planned March 2026 retirement of the Entra ID Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control. The period also covers the completed transition of Entra ID Protection alerts out of Defender for Cloud Apps and the rollout of a new People administrator role in Microsoft Entra.
2025-03.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies that use “Require approved client app” and plan to replace it with “Require application protection policy” before March 2026; the supplied notice does not give an exact retirement date or migration procedure. For ID Protection, Microsoft says no administrator action is required, but asks administrators to review their configuration and notify users about the new alert location in Microsoft Defender XDR. The People administrator notice describes a lower-privilege administrative option for people-related settings and profile photos, but supplies no assignment steps and does not identify the role as preview or generally available.

keyChanges.title: “Require approved client app” is scheduled for retirement in March 2026
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s March 13 reminder says the Conditional Access control will be retired in March 2026 and directs organizations to use the “Require application protection policy” grant control instead. This is a planned retirement, not evidence that the control has already been removed. Administrators should identify affected policies and validate the replacement before changing production policy.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID Protection alerts moved from Defender for Cloud Apps to Defender XDR
keyChanges.detail: The March 6 reminder says Entra ID Protection alerts stopped being available in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps on March 5, 2025, with the alerts integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR. Microsoft states that no administrator action is required, while still asking administrators to review configuration and notify users about the change in alert location.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra introduced a People administrator role
keyChanges.detail: The March 8 notice describes a new role intended to manage people-related settings and profile photos without requiring highly privileged administration. Its rollout was stated to begin in early February 2025 and complete by late March 2025. The supplied evidence does not specify assignment steps or establish preview or general-availability status.

2025-04.headline: April 2025: Workload ID guidance states a 31 March 2026 remediation deadline; Power Automate hybrid join has a 31 May GA date
2025-04.overview: April was overwhelmingly a documentation-maintenance month: 3,252 items were updated, compared with 10 new items, alongside eight removals and three Message Center notices. The meaningful exceptions were a Workload ID support-removal signal, an Entra Connect application-identity authentication path, an explicitly preview Conditional Access optimization agent, and an announced general-availability milestone for Entra hybrid join in Power Automate hosted machine groups. Most other edits were clarification, troubleshooting, tutorials, or security and user-experience guidance; the supplied removal entries do not establish additional product retirements.
2025-04.adminImpact: Identify applications using the affected Workload ID authentication mode and follow the documented remediation path—verify access, create an enterprise application, and verify tokens—before 31 March 2026. Entra Connect owners should review the application-based flow, but the evidence supplies no universal migration requirement or GA label; manage the created application or service principal and certificate only if that path reaches their deployment. Treat the Conditional Access optimization agent as preview and follow its setup guidance. If the Power Automate hosted-machine-group capability is in use, track 31 May 2025. Registration and Authenticator sign-in UI changes roll out automatically; notify users and update local instructions, while the Message Center notices require no admin-­drі

keyChanges.title: Retirement signal: Workload ID service principal-less authentication
keyChanges.detail: An updated Workload ID guidance item says service principal-less authentication will no longer be supported from March 2026, with remediation required by 31 March 2026 to avoid application authentication failures. The supplied mitigation sequence is to verify access, create an enterprise application, and verify tokens. Because the evidence does not define the complete scope, treat this as an affected-application remediation signal rather than proof that every workload must change.

keyChanges.title: General availability date: Entra hybrid join for Power Automate hosted machine groups
keyChanges.detail: The April announcement sets general availability for Entra hybrid join for Power Automate hosted machine groups on 31 May 2025. This is an explicit availability milestone, not merely a newly edited Learn page. The supplied evidence gives no additional prerequisites or migration steps.
keyChanges.product: Entra hybrid join / Power Automate hosted machine groups

keyChanges.title: Entra Connect documents application-based authentication
keyChanges.detail: Revised guidance describes an application-based alternative to the connector account’s locally stored password, using an Entra application identity and OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow. Entra Connect creates a single-tenant third-party application in the customer tenant; later guidance frames the rollout around a certificate-based application identity. The record does not label this capability preview or generally available and does not require all existing connectors to migrate.

keyChanges.title: Preview: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access optimization agent
keyChanges.detail: New and updated pages identify the Conditional Access optimization agent as being in preview. It recommends policies and changes aligned with Microsoft’s Zero Trust guidance; its documented preview scope covers MFA requirements, device controls such as compliance, app protection policies, and domain-joined devices, as well as blocking legacy authentication and device code flow. Setup begins with View details and Start agent. No GA or mandatory tenant-wide rollout is established.

keyChanges.title: Authentication updates are security guidance or UX changes, not a new policy rollout
keyChanges.detail: A new Protecting Tokens in Microsoft Entra ID article addresses token theft and replay, but the evidence presents it as security guidance rather than a new token-protection control. Updated mandatory-MFA pages add verification, lockout, and postponement procedures. Separately, Message Center describes an automatic change to the More information required registration interface from late April through late May and a new Authenticator Lite and Authenticator app message telling users to refresh notifications when no…

2025-05.headline: May 2025: Power Automate hybrid join gets a 31 May GA date while Entra Connect security and preview guidance lead a maintenance-heavy month
2025-05.overview: May was overwhelmingly a documentation-maintenance period: 5,758 of 5,804 records were updates, compared with 26 new and 18 removed entries, and only two Message Center notices. The clearest operational signals were the explicit GA date for Entra hybrid join in Power Automate hosted machine groups and the global availability notice for the Defender for Identity sensor on Microsoft Entra Connect servers. Learn updates separately mark linkable identifiers in Entra ID and TLS inspection in Microsoft Entra Internet Access as previews, while Tenant Restrictions v2 and certificate-based authentication content clarify security behavior. New entries such as the External ID emailOtpSend reference and the ID Governance PIM for Groups how-to are documentation additions, not evidence of launches. The 18 removals have no supplied scope, so no retirement can be established.
2025-05.adminImpact: Power Automate teams using hosted machine groups should track the stated 31 May GA date. The Defender for Identity notice says no action is required before rollout, while recommending sensor installation for monitoring and threat detection. Security teams can assess the linkable-identifier and TLS-inspection previews, but the evidence supplies no GA, tenant-wide rollout, prerequisite, or enablement instruction.
