The notice concerns the greeting experience, not a stated retirement of voice MFA itself; the supported preparation is to inform users and review relevant MFA configurations.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP’s Enforcement plane label changes from “Entra” to “Application”
keyChanges.detail: Naming clarification: Microsoft Purview DLP began renaming the Enforcement plane in mid-January. There is no stated functional, user, or compliance impact. New audit logs use “Application,” while existing logs retain “Entra,” so scripts and documentation that depend on the label may need updating.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access Optimization Agent guidance documents an activator-identity distinction
keyChanges.detail: A coordinated update to five Entra Conditional Access Optimization Agent pages records that agents enabled after November 17, 2025 no longer use the identity of the user who activated them. Earlier agents may fail when the activating account relied on Privileged Identity Management but lacked the required permissions when the agent ran. This is operational documentation and troubleshooting guidance; it does not establish a preview, general-availability event, or January-wide rollout.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Conditional Access Optimization Agent

keyChanges.title: External ID guidance adds an explicit Akamai WAF verification step
keyChanges.detail: The updated Akamai integration guidance tells administrators to verify after configuration that Akamai WAF is protecting the external tenant by connecting the authentication credentials to the WAF configuration. Related External ID security guidance frames credential stuffing, automated bot sign-ups, account takeover, and traffic spikes as CIAM threats requiring layered controls and integrations. These are implementation and security clarifications, not evidence of a new External ID capability or availability shift

2026-02.headline: February 2026: Entra adds Conditional Access web-filtering guidance, Global Secure Access flags a location limitation, and Rewards account linking is scheduled to retire
2026-02.overview: The month's most consequential items are a cross-product implementation path, a concrete Global Secure Access limitation, targeted External ID authentication clarifications, and one explicit retirement—not a broad release wave. The record contains 2,701 changes: 2,686 updates, 8 new items, 6 removals, and one Message Center notice. The new February 19 web-filtering page and February 27 Internet Access update describe integration with Microsoft Entra ID and Conditional Access, but the supplied evidence does not label the capability preview or generally available. The supplied briefs do identify prerelease or preview material for External ID B2B Guest Access and Prompt Shield, without providing scope or an availability commitment. Most remaining changes are ordinary Microsoft Learn maintenance, including broad Conditional Access reference refreshes and partner SSO and provisioning tutorials.
2026-02.adminImpact: Use targeted validation rather than a tenant-wide rollout. For web content filtering, follow the documented Conditional Access session-control path; the supplied guidance describes propagation as typically under five minutes for changes made in the Global Secure Access experience and about one hour for Conditional Access changes. Before enabling strict location enforcement, inspect IP location-based Conditional Access policies targeting non-Microsoft resources. External ID administrators who need custom alias validation must plan to configure it through Microsoft Graph, and should verify password-migration error handling and SMS cost and first-factor assumptions. Agent ID administrators can review the updated guidance for blocking risky agent identities. No administrator action is required

keyChanges.title: [New and updated documentation] Web content filtering is documented as a Conditional Access-integrated capability
keyChanges.detail: A new February 19 Microsoft Entra Conditional Access page covers web content filtering integration. Related Microsoft Entra Internet Access guidance says its first Secure Web Gateway features include domain-name filtering and that granular policies integrate with Microsoft Entra ID and Conditional Access, making them user-aware and context-aware. This establishes an implementation path in the documentation, not a supplied preview or GA announcement.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID Conditional Access; Internet Access; Global Secure Access

keyChanges.title: [Known limitation and security guidance] Global Secure Access warns against strict location enforcement in a specific policy combination
keyChanges.detail: The February 10 update to Global Secure Access Current Known Limitations says not to enable strict location enforcement when IP location-based Conditional Access policies target non-Microsoft resources. This is an explicit operational guardrail for that configuration, not a general feature launch or tenant-wide behavior change.
keyChanges.product: Global Secure Access; Entra ID Conditional Access

keyChanges.title: [Retirement] Azure AD Account Linking for Microsoft Rewards ends by March 19, 2026
keyChanges.detail: The sole supplied Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says users will no longer be able to link work accounts to earn Microsoft Rewards points by March 19, 2026. Existing points are unaffected, personal accounts continue to work, and the notice explicitly says no administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: [Documentation clarification] External ID authentication guidance adds Graph-only validation and flow constraints
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sign In Alias guidance documents custom username validation through the validationRegEx setting, which is not available in the admin center and must be configured through Microsoft Graph using the authenticationAttributeCollectionInputConfiguration resource. External ID MFA guidance says SMS has an additional cost for second-factor verification and self-service password reset in external tenants and is not supported for first-factor authentication. The period's password-migration guidance also records a

keyChanges.title: [Security guidance] Agent ID documentation covers blocking high-risk agent identities with Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: An updated February 4 Agent ID page explains how to configure Conditional Access policies to block risky agent identities and presents related best practices. The supplied record does not establish new enforcement, preview status, or GA; administrators should treat this as security guidance for Agent ID deployments.
keyChanges.product: Agent ID; Entra ID Conditional Access

2026-03.headline: March 2026: Windows passkeys preview, AI Administrator RBAC expansion, and an upcoming Authentication Methods audit-log change lead the Entra story
2026-03.overview: March was dominated by Microsoft Learn maintenance—623 updates out of 648 records, with 18 new pages and 5 Message Center notices—rather than a broad Entra release wave. The meaningful operational exceptions are the Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows public preview, the AI Administrator RBAC rollout for Agent 365, and the April Authentication Methods Policy audit-event format change. ID Governance also added preview documentation for Tenant Governance, while Security Copilot is scheduled for phased inclusion in Microsoft 365 E5. New native-auth pages cover email and SMS OTP MFA and strong authentication method registration on Android, iOS, and macOS, but the evidence describes implementation guidance and a private-preview path, not general availability. Updated Conditional Access, Application Proxy, Global Secure Access, Private Access, and External ID pages are best treated as targeted documentation clarification. The removed page records do not establish retirement of the underlying capabilities.
2026-03.adminImpact: Actions are scoped to affected environments rather than tenant-wide. Organizations that want to test Windows passkeys must opt in and configure passkey policies; existing security policies remain unchanged. If Agent 365 is in scope, review AI Administrator assignments and the expanded consent and risk-monitoring scope as the role rollout reaches the tenant. If tooling processes Authentication Methods Policy audit events, review automated processing before the April worldwide rollout because the logged property set will change even though event names and policy enforcement will not. Use the Tenant Governance and native-auth material for evaluation or implementation planning; the evidence does not require a rollout. Track the Security Copilot E5 rollout from April 20 through June 30, 2026, d

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows move into public preview
keyChanges.detail: The March 19 Message Center notice says Windows Hello-backed passkeys provide phishing-resistant, passwordless sign-in on managed and unmanaged devices. The preview runs from late March through May 2026 and requires organizational opt-in and passkey-policy configuration. Existing security policies remain unchanged, so this is a public preview rather than a general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: AI Administrator RBAC expands for Agent 365
keyChanges.detail: A role update rolling out from March 2026 lets AI Administrators handle routine agent lifecycle management without Global Administrator involvement. It also expands delegated tenant-wide consent, excluding Microsoft Graph app permissions, and adds risk monitoring through Identity Protection. This is a permissions and operating-model change, so affected organizations should review assignments and consent boundaries.

keyChanges.title: Authentication Methods Policy audit events are getting a new property set
keyChanges.detail: The supplied Message Center summary says an April 2026 worldwide rollout will change the properties recorded for Entra ID Authentication Methods Policy update events. Event names and policy enforcement remain unchanged, making this a telemetry and automation compatibility change rather than a change to policy behavior. Event-consuming integrations should be reviewed before rollout.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — audit logs and Authentication Methods Policy

keyChanges.title: Tenant Governance receives end-to-end preview documentation
keyChanges.detail: ID Governance added three pages covering Tenant Governance setup, tenant discovery, governance, configuration monitoring, and the signals and metrics used to identify and evaluate related tenants. The titles explicitly mark the capability as preview. These pages support evaluation and planning but do not establish general availability, a mandatory rollout, or retirement of an existing capability.
keyChanges.product: ID Governance — Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot is scheduled for phased Microsoft 365 E5 inclusion
keyChanges.detail: The March 26 Message Center notice sets a rollout window of April 20 through June 30, 2026. It describes 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 users and core agentic features across Microsoft security products, while noting that advanced capabilities may incur additional costs. The notice describes a plan entitlement rollout, not an Entra configuration change.

2026-04.headline: Microsoft Entra in April 2026: Conditional Access enforcement changes, Agent ID’s May 1 transition, and ID Governance prerequisites lead
2026-04.overview: April was chiefly a documentation-maintenance period: 388 of 403 records were Learn updates, with four new and four removed records, while seven Message Center notices carried the clearest operational timing. The substantive exceptions are different in kind: Conditional Access guidance describes changed enforcement; Agent ID has a dated retirement of two admin blades and an API transition; ID Governance has an already-effective subscription gate and two separately timed previews; and Authentication Methods audit logs change shape without changing enforcement. The passkey campaign notices are not reconciled in the supplied evidence. Most remaining Learn edits—such as Linux SSO, system-preferred authentication, social sign-in, External ID browser language, and MFA, AD FS, and MFA Server guidance—are ordinary clarification or security and migration guidance, not evidence of new availability. Late-April Tenant Governance and Global Secure Access Explicit Forward Proxy material remains preview or reference content, with no supplied GA statement.
2026-04.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies that target All resources with resource exclusions; the new article and FAQ explain how to assess impact and retain legacy behavior, but provide no rollout date. Related guidance says report-only and disabled policies count toward the 240-policy limit and points users of custom controls toward replacement. For Agent ID, teams that depend on the current blades or API should track the May 1 transition; the notice says no immediate action is required, and it does not indicate that agent identities themselves are being retired. Verify that an Azure subscription is linked before creating or updating guest-scoped governance policies; existing policies continue, but those new actions can be blocked without the subscription. If adopting the governance previews,‌​

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access resource exclusions receive improved enforcement guidance
keyChanges.detail: New April 15 Entra ID documentation and FAQs describe improved enforcement for policies targeting All resources with resource exclusions. They explain how to assess impact and retain legacy behavior. The evidence supplies no rollout date or GA statement, so this is a behavior-change and rollout signal rather than a new product launch. Separate Conditional Access edits clarify custom-control replacement and that report-only and disabled policies count toward the 240-policy limit.

keyChanges.title: Agent ID administration shifts to Agent 365 on May 1
keyChanges.detail: The April 10 Message Center notice says the Agent registry and Agent collections blades will be retired from the Microsoft Entra admin center starting May 1, 2026. Agent 365 becomes the unified management platform, and a new API replaces the existing API; the notice says no immediate admin action is required. This is a retirement of admin surfaces and an API transition, not evidence that agent identities are being retired. Updated Learn pages on agent service principals, blueprints, and the documented GA capability

keyChanges.title: ID Governance pairs an effective guest-governance gate with two previews
keyChanges.detail: The April 17 major update says tenants have needed a linked Azure subscription since January 30, 2026 to use guest governance features. Without it, creating or updating guest-scoped policies is blocked, while existing policies continue; new actions require subscription-linked billing under the Monthly Active User model. Separately, cross-tenant security group synchronization is in public preview, with GA by the end of May announced, and is enabled through attribute mappings and access policies. Account Discovery is

keyChanges.title: Authentication Methods Policy audit logs change format, not policy behavior
keyChanges.detail: The April worldwide rollout changes Entra ID audit logs so Authentication Methods Policy updates show only changed properties with old and new values. Event names and policy enforcement remain unchanged. Organizations with automated log processing should review parsing logic; this is a telemetry and readability change, not a new authentication control.

keyChanges.title: Passkey registration-campaign status remains unsettled
keyChanges.detail: The April 16 notice says Microsoft canceled the planned addition of Passkeys (FIDO2) to Microsoft Registration Campaigns and will not implement the planned automatic settings updates and nudges. The April 24 notice says Passkeys will continue in Enabled and Microsoft-managed Registration Campaign states, with worldwide updates planned from mid-May through late June 2026 and automatic nudges after MFA. The supplied messages do not say whether they cover different scopes or whether the later notice supersedes theearl

2026-05.headline: May 2026: actionable-message token retirement leads the period’s consequential Entra changes
2026-05.overview: May was primarily a documentation-maintenance period, but several Message Center notices describe concrete behavior changes. External access tokens for actionable messages are being replaced by Microsoft Entra authentication; federatedTokenValidationPolicy defaults tighten in mid-August; Conditional Access will apply during Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO registration in July; and App Instance Lock will be enabled by default for new applications in June. Dataverse Agent users are a separate Microsoft Entra Agent ID public preview with phased rollout. Most Learn edits clarify existing authentication, Conditional Access, External ID, Agent ID, and Global Secure Access guidance rather than announcing tenant-wide changes. The five removed items have no supplied detail establishing another product retirement. An early-access Power Apps and Dynamics 365 in-app-skills control was scheduled to move to a new underlying service on May 21 in preparation for GA, not as a GA announcement.
2026-05.adminImpact: Prioritize integrations using legacy actionable-message tokens: the notice lists May 15, 2026 as the retirement date and June 8 as completion of the phase-out, and says messages using legacy tokens will fail. Affected integrations need to move to Microsoft Entra authentication. Before the later rollouts, federation administrators should check the stated scope—federated domains configured before December 2025—for internalDomainFederation and UPN mismatches; enrollment teams should test Conditional Access requirements such as MFA and trusted locations during Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO registration; and application-creation automation should be reviewed for App Instance Lock. Existing applications are explicitly unaffected, and administrators can disable the lock. Treat

keyChanges.title: External access tokens for actionable messages are being retired
keyChanges.detail: Retirement and breaking integration change: Microsoft is replacing external access tokens with Microsoft Entra authentication. Messages that continue using legacy tokens will fail. The notice lists May 15, 2026 as the retirement date and June 8, 2026 as completion of the phase-out.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access will apply during Windows and macOS identity registration
keyChanges.detail: Scheduled behavior change: starting July 6, 2026, with rollout completion scheduled for July 13, Conditional Access policies will apply to Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO registration. The notice specifically calls out requirements such as MFA and trusted locations during enrollment.

keyChanges.title: Federated sign-in validation will use stricter defaults
keyChanges.detail: Scheduled security hardening: beginning in mid-August 2026, Microsoft Entra will enforce stricter federatedTokenValidationPolicy defaults and block federated sign-ins when internalDomainFederation does not match the user’s UPN domain. The stated scope is tenants with federated domains configured before December 2025.

keyChanges.title: App Instance Lock becomes the default for new applications
keyChanges.detail: Scheduled default change for June 2026: new applications will have App Instance Lock enabled to protect sensitive properties from unauthorized changes outside the home tenant. Existing applications are explicitly unaffected, and administrators can disable the lock if needed.

keyChanges.title: Dataverse Agent users enter public preview
keyChanges.detail: New capability, public preview—not GA: Dataverse Agent users are powered by Microsoft Entra Agent ID. The rollout was scheduled to start May 4, 2026, and was expected to reach North America by May 22; the notice describes a phased preview rollout rather than general availability.

2026-06.headline: June 2026 Entra briefing: SSPR registration becomes mandatory in September, partner support assignments close in August, and Excel 2021 has a July authentication deadline
2026-06.overview: June was dominated by Learn maintenance—5,217 updates versus 32 new items. Representative edits covered native-authentication tutorials, combined-registration troubleshooting, licensing, and lab instructions, so a new page should not be read as a feature launch. The most consequential administrator-facing exceptions were the upcoming SSPR verification change, retirement of new Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support assignments, the Excel 2021 client deadline, Internet Access web-category changes, and a planned Agent ID service-plan rollout. The supplied record contains no general-availability announcement. Microsoft Entra PIM role-activation extensions are explicitly described as preview, while the new Workload ID assignment-restriction and Lifecycle Workflows execution-limit pages provide guidance without stating availability.
2026-06.adminImpact: Prepare users through the SSPR registration campaign beginning 6 August for the 7 September verification change. Inventory Excel 2021 installations at version 21.08 or earlier and update them to build 16.0.14334.20754 or later, or upgrade; Microsoft 365 and newer Excel versions are unaffected. If automation assigns Partner Tier1 or Tier2 Support, change it to an alternative such as User Administrator before 3 August; existing assignments remain valid. For Internet Access, review filtering policies if reclassified sites change intended access—the notice says no action is required. Agent ID service plans are expected to enable automatically, with no policy changes or immediate action, although a license review is recommended. A separate Authenticator notice describes automatic warning-then-­

keyChanges.title: SSPR will require explicitly registered authentication methods — 7 September 2026
keyChanges.detail: This is a change in password-reset verification behavior, not a new SSPR feature announcement. Users will need explicitly registered authentication methods; directory-sourced contact information will no longer be sufficient unless it has been registered. A registration campaign begins on 6 August.

keyChanges.title: New Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support assignments will be blocked — 3 August 2026
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is retiring these partner support roles for new assignments. Existing assignments remain valid, and tenants that do not use the roles are unaffected. Scripts that create new assignments should be updated to use alternatives such as User Administrator.

keyChanges.title: Excel 2021 Power Query requires an authentication update — 24 July 2026
keyChanges.detail: Excel 2021 version 21.08 or earlier must be updated to build 16.0.14334.20754 or later, or upgraded to a newer version, to avoid losing Organizational Account authentication for Power Query. Microsoft 365 and newer Excel versions are unaffected. This is a client requirement, not an Entra service launch.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID / Excel Power Query

keyChanges.title: Internet Access web categorization changes affect filtering inputs
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice announced a mid-June update that adds an AI Agents category and refines existing categories. Some sites may be reclassified, which can change the results of category-based filtering policies. The notice says no action is required but advises reviewing and adjusting policies if intended access is affected.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access / Global Secure Access

keyChanges.title: Agent ID service plans are scheduled for an automatic July rollout
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is adding Conditional Access for Agents and ID Protection for Agents to Microsoft Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 E7, with rollout starting in July 2026. The notice specifies automatic enablement and no policy changes or immediate action; it recommends reviewing licensing. This is a planned service-plan rollout, not evidence of a June general-availability feature launch.

2026-07.headline: July 2026: passkeys become the default while Custom Controls and SharePoint OTP enter retirement
2026-07.overview: July’s substantive Entra story is lifecycle change rather than a wave of July launches. Microsoft says passkey profiles and synced passkeys are reaching general availability for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled, with existing configurations migrating regionally through October 2026. Passkeys become the default on September 1, 2026, while Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retires on February 1, 2027. In parallel, affected Conditional Access policies must move from Custom Controls to External MFA by September, and SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication retires in October as external sharing moves to Entra B2B. Purview’s network-layer DLP integration with Entra Internet Access—Global Secure Access—is the main cross-product rollout. Most remaining Learn activity is procedural or clarifying rather than evidence of a new launch; the GitHub Actions immutable-subject page is security guidance, while Tenant Governance Graph retrieval is explicitly preview documentation.
2026-07.adminImpact: Prioritize identifying Custom Controls policies and migrating them to External MFA by September 2026. Plan the passkey transition and, as directed in the notice, configure telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store to avoid SMS or voice disruption. Before the October SharePoint OTP retirement, update external-sharing policies and guest-account management. If Partner Tier1 or Tier2 Support roles are used, change automation for new assignments before August 3; existing assignments remain valid. For the Purview and Global Secure Access rollout, coordinate Purview, Entra, and Defender ownership, noting that the supplied evidence does not specify a mandatory configuration step. For tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, system-preferred authentication now applies to first-factor‌​‍

keyChanges.title: Passkey profiles reach GA as Entra moves away from Microsoft SMS and voice authentication
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice describes passkey profiles and synced passkeys as reaching GA from March 2026 for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled. Existing configurations migrate to a Default passkey profile with a new passkeyType property, and automatic migration plus Registration Campaign updates roll out regionally through October. A separate notice makes passkeys the default on September 1, 2026 and retires Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication on February 1, 2027; it says customers must configure a##

keyChanges.title: Custom Controls retirement creates a near-term Conditional Access migration
keyChanges.detail: Custom Controls are scheduled to retire by May 2027 and be replaced by External MFA for standardized third-party MFA integration. The notice sets September 2026 as the deadline to migrate affected Conditional Access policies, making this a required policy conversion rather than a preview or documentation-only change.

keyChanges.title: SharePoint OTP gives way to Entra B2B for external sharing
keyChanges.detail: SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication retires in October 2026. New external sharing has used Microsoft Entra B2B since May 2026; the notice says external users need guest accounts for access and asks administrators to prepare by updating policies and managing those accounts. This is an authentication and identity-model retirement, not a new Learn-page launch.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP extends into the Global Secure Access network layer
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft describes inspection and protection of sensitive data in AI interactions and cloud services through Entra Internet Access, with policy enforcement, alerts, and auditing. A related notice covers sensitive-file filtering to unmanaged cloud apps: public preview was stated to start in November 2025, with GA targeted by September 2026, while the broader rollout is described as July through October 2026. The change affects Purview, Entra, and Defender administrators, but the supplied evidence specifies no newly
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Purview / Global Secure Access (Entra Internet Access)

keyChanges.title: New Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support assignments will be blocked in August
keyChanges.detail: Starting August 3, 2026, Entra will block new assignments to the Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support roles, while existing assignments remain valid. Tenants that use these roles need to change automation for future assignments and consider alternatives such as User Administrator; tenants that do not use them are unaffected.

2026-08.headline: Branding CSS and MemberOf retirements headline Microsoft Entra’s August changes
2026-08.overview: August’s most consequential Entra developments were scheduled retirements and changed authentication behavior. Custom company-branding CSS and MemberOf rules gained firm deadlines, while SSPR verification and system-preferred first-factor sign-ins moved toward stricter or more secure behavior. The documentation track added a guided Global Secure Access V1-to-V2 migration path and detailed Tenant Governance snapshot prerequisites, rather than signaling a broad product launch.
2026-08.adminImpact: Inventory custom-branding CSS and MemberOf rules now, replacing affected configurations before their deadlines. For Entra ID Free tenants, verify that users no longer depend on SMS first-factor sign-in; SMS used for MFA remains unaffected. Prepare users for the SSPR registration campaign beginning October 5 and its November 9 enforcement date, and update first-factor sign-in guidance as system-preferred authentication rolls out.

keyChanges.title: Custom branding CSS properties face late-October retirement
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra will retire custom CSS layout and positioning properties in company branding by late October 2026. New use has been blocked since July 21, 2026, and existing branding will revert to default layouts after retirement. Audit branding configurations and replace affected properties before the cutoff.

keyChanges.title: MemberOf rules require replacement across Entra access configurations
keyChanges.detail: The MemberOf rule operator will retire on November 3, 2026. The change affects uses in dynamic groups, administrative units, and entitlement policies; Microsoft advises replacing those rules to avoid stale access, licensing, and policy-enforcement results.

keyChanges.title: SMS first-factor sign-in ends for Entra ID Free tenants
keyChanges.detail: SMS first-factor sign-in retired for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants on August 11, 2026, because of fraud risks. SMS used as a multifactor authentication method remains available, so administrators should identify affected users and move first-factor sign-in to another method.

keyChanges.title: SSPR shifts to explicitly registered verification methods
keyChanges.detail: Starting November 9, 2026, self-service password reset will require explicitly registered authentication methods for verification. Directory-sourced contact information will no longer qualify unless the method is registered. Microsoft’s registration campaign begins October 5, giving organizations time to prepare users.

keyChanges.title: System-preferred authentication expands to first-factor sign-ins
keyChanges.detail: For tenants in the Microsoft-managed state, system-preferred authentication now applies to first-factor sign-ins and selects the most secure registered method. Rollout runs from late June through late September 2026; tenants can retain or change the setting, while user sign-in guidance should reflect the change.
